title: [KV-Offloading][TP] : Expand replicated_layout detection to multi-group MLA
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose
KV offloading for MLA models + TP need only offload KV values from one TP rank. 
This is controlled by replicated_layout determination in `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/config.py`

Building on top of @almogtavor 's work https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50667 (which was eventually closed) , this PR expand the replicated_layout check to include, 
 - SlidingWindowMLASpec
 - Multi-group MLASpec / SlidingWindowMLASpec
 models. 
 
Notably, 
- deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash
- deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp and 
- zai-org/GLM-5.3
fall in this category. 

### Changes:
 - in the replicated_layout check, 
   * Unwrap `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` and check that the internal layer specs are MLA
   * Check if all the layer_spec in all the Attention groups are in [MLAAttentionSpec, SlidingWindowMLASpec]
   * Additionally, check that the advertises `num_kv_heads = 1`, indicating TP sharding of KV heads is not possible. 
   * Remove the existing size check 
   ```
        and worker_kv_bytes_per_block
        == single_group_spec.page_size_bytes
        * len(kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups[0].layer_names)
   ```
    this is critical and loosens the existing conditions on `main` . This is because the KV cache groups are flattened in the Scheduler process here https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/038cb14bd7874030e98bb6edc4b6f4efe649fff7/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py#L2376 . 
    Specifically, the realization of the comment, 
    ```
            # All layers in the UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs have the same type,
            # so use an arbitrary one to initialize the scheduler.
    ```
    makes it impossible to compute the correct size from the KVCache groups to correctly effect this "size" sanity check. Groups such as

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][NIXL] Shard a GQA draft's KV by head under an MLA target
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #58470.

NIXL P/D mis-handles a draft model's KV when **all three** hold:

1. **The target is MLA** (e.g. GLM-5.3), so NIXL maps every KV region as replicated: `total_num_kv_heads=1`, `rank_offset_factor=0`.
2. **The draft is not MLA** (e.g. DFlash2, 8 KV heads), so its KV is actually split by head across TP.
3. **Prefill TP ≠ decode TP** (e.g. a DEP8 prefill with attention TP1 feeding a TP8 decoder), so each decode rank needs a different head slice.

Drop any one and it works: an MLA draft (MTP), or equal P/D TP. `_is_region_replicated` already marks the draft regions SPLIT, but three places still use the model-wide MLA answer:

| where | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| handshake size check (`model_replicated = self.use_mla or …`) | rejects the correct geometry, accepts an unscaled draft block | checks draft regions as SPLIT |
| read offset (`_build_fa_remote`) | every decode rank reads draft head 0 | rank *r* reads head *r* |
| hetero-TP layout guard | skipped when `use_mla` | requires the same block-contiguous layout on P and D |

**Fix.** When the target is MLA and the draft isn't, build a second `TPMapping` from the draft's KV head count (`compute_tp_mapping(..., head_sharded_kv_heads=...)`). The draft's SPLIT regions use it for reads, size checks and the layout guard; MLA regions are unchanged. Prefill TP > decode TP and DCP are rejected with `NotImplementedError` for such drafts. Mamba, CSA-linear and MLA drafts behave as before.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR touches this. Related:
- #49230 (merged): checks that P and D speculative configs match; they do here.
- #54926: Gemma 4 MTP draft groups are not transferred at all.
- #57309: moves helpers out of `tp_mapping.py`; a refactor only.

## Test Plan

       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py

title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Skinny GEMM dispatch for tiny-M decode projections
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

At tiny M (1–4 rows) the dense projections on DeepSeek-V4.1's decode path are dispatch-mismatched: MXFP8 CuTeDSL and BF16 cuBLAS kernels sized for bulk traffic run weight-bound rounds. This PR adds a shape-keyed skinny dispatch table (SM100/B200 only, TP8 shapes) that swaps in the measured winners exactly where they win — a Triton SIMT GEMM for the three MXFP8 projections, CuTe skinny for the BF16 indexer/lm_head projections, and ll_bf16 dotprod for the FP32 compressor scores, 20 (shape, M) cells in total.

Semantics are preserved exactly: MXFP8 candidates keep the per-32-element E8M0 activation scale and FP8 rounding (`round_mx` in the SIMT kernel reproduces the baseline MXFP8 quantization), and FP32 compressor outputs stay FP32. Everything falls back to the original kernels off-table, off-device, non-BF16 input, with LoRA attached, with a bias, or under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`. The dispatch runs at model init for the three unquantized BF16 modules (K3/GLM-5.2 quant-method replacement precedent) and at the model-layer call sites for the fused/wo_a/compressor paths, so module forward and any wrappers are untouched off the table.

## Test Plan

Deployment (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 8xB200, TP8/EP, MegaMoE+SP, FlashInfer sparse MLA, FP8 KV, C1/C4/C16 client suites, `vllm bench serve`, seed 42, ignore-EOS, tokenizer trusted):

title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] kpool corruption with speculative decoding
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

This patch is the result of hunting down random corruption in long GLM-5.3-Flash traces.

Rejected pool-completing drafts can end up subtly corrupting the pool selection logic: When a pool-completing draft is rejected, the drafts stashed behind it have already overwritten that pool's committed keys. A pool of 4 generated tokens gets an incorrect summary key, so the indexer may skip those tokens or pick a less useful pool.

This affects any speculative method with `num_speculative_tokens >= 2`. 

Only pools built during decode (the model's own output) are affected, and only once the context exceeds `index_topk` (2048), where pools compete for selection.

The most likely place it hurts is long reasoning traces, where later thinking refers back to earlier thinking, as slightly worse long-range self-reference. This _may_ be causing specific failures in re-transcription from memory.

The ring now holds `kpool * cdiv(kpool + num_spec, kpool)` slots, and the seed and decode kernels address it by `pos % RING`. The tail slot mapping already uses the spec's block_size, so it follows. 

Encountered this locally, fix based on work in #55219 by @ivanium. This is only a surgical fix + test for this particular issue.

## Test Plan

Tests included.

Also, a standalone repro that isolates the specific bug and corruption:

| kernel | ring | pool vs reference |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 4 (current sizing) | wrong: 106 of 128 fp8 key bytes differ |
| `main` | 8 | `AssertionError` (ring must equal `kpool`) |
| this PR | 8 (`4 * cdiv(4 + 3, 4)`) | identical

title: [Bug]: KDA/gated-delta-rule chunked-scan buffers are outside memory profiling — runtime OOM at large --max-num-batched-tokens
bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

The chunked-scan buffers in the gated-delta-rule (KDA) path scale linearly with
`--max-num-batched-tokens`, are allocated transiently inside the forward pass, and are **not
covered by vLLM's startup memory profiling**. The KV cache is therefore sized as if that memory
were free, and above a certain chunk size the engine dies at runtime — mid-request, after having
served traffic.

### Observed

GLM-5.3-Flash (45 layers: 34 KDA linear-attention + 11 sparse MLA), 1× MI350X (gfx950),
ROCm 7.2.3, TP1, MXFP4 weights, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.93`.
16 concurrent requests of ~38k tokens each.

| `--max-num-batched-tokens` | successful | failed | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 192 … 65 536 | 16 / 16 | 0 | stable across 3 runs each |
| **81 920** | **5 / 16** | **11** | engine shut down |
| **131 072** | **4 / 16** | 12 | engine shut down |

```
(Worker) ERROR  File ".../flash_linear_attention/ops/chunk_delta_h.py", line 357,
                  in chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h
(Worker) ERROR    v_new = torch.empty_like(u) if save_new_value else None
(Worker) ERROR  torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.25 GiB.
                  GPU 0 has a total capacity of 287.98 GiB of which 0 [bytes is free]
(APIServer) INFO [shutdown] EngineCore process manager: using 15.0s ROCm cleanup grace
                  after immediate request abort
```

Startup reported no problem — `GPU KV cache size: 6,940,947 tokens` at 81,920, and the memory
profiling line looked healthy.

### Mechanism

`chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` allocates two buffers proportional to the token count in the batch:

```python
B, T, Hg, K, V = *k.shape, u.shape[-1]
H  = u.shape[-2]
BT = chunk_size                      # FLA_CHUNK_SIZE = 64, hard-coded in ops/utils.py:31
...
N, NT = len(cu_seqlens) - 1, len(chunk_indices)
h     = k.new_empty(B, NT, H, V, K)          # NT = ceil(T / 64)  -> linear in T
v_new = torch.empty_like(u) if save_new_value else None
author: stefanskiasan

title: [Bugfix] Stop allocator fragmentation from shrinking the KV cache during memory profiling
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Wrap the memory-profiling forward pass in `Worker._scoped_allocator_max_split(max_split_size_mb=20)`, the same scoped allocator setting #41268 applies around weight loading.

During `profile_run`, workspaces such as the MoE workspace grow in steps, and each step frees the previous, smaller buffer. With PyTorch's default (unlimited) `max_split_size_mb`, a later small allocation can be carved out of one of those freed multi-GiB blocks. That live block keeps the whole segment reserved through the `empty_cache()` in `memory_profiling`. The profiler measures consumption from free device memory, so the stranded segment is counted as consumed and taken out of the KV cache.

How much gets stranded depends on allocation order, so it varies per rank. With context parallelism the worst rank in each group sets the group's KV size, so the loss compounds. With a split limit, blocks above the limit are never split, so they stay whole and `empty_cache()` releases them. The limit is restored when the profiling pass exits, before `memory_profiling` measures, so serving and KV cache allocation run with the original allocator settings.

`PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` also avoids the stranding. But vLLM rejects it alongside a KV connector such as NIXL unless `--enable-cumem-allocator` is also set, and in the deployment below that combination raised baseline consumption by ~2.9 GiB on every GPU. The scoped split limit keeps the default `cudaMalloc` allocator throughout.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py::test_scoped_max_split_keeps_freed_large_blocks_releasable` (needs CUDA). It frees a 512 MiB buffer and then allocates a 2 MiB tensor. Without the scope, the tensor pins the 512 MiB segment through `empty_cache()`. Inside `_scoped_allocator_max_split(20)`, the segment is released.

  ```
  pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py -k scoped_max_split
  ```

- End to end: GLM-5.2-FP8, DP4 × PCP8 (DCP8), TP1, EP32 on 4 × 8 H10

title: [Bugfix][GLM] Invalidate merged KDA convolution weights after refit
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55087.

GLM-5.3 KDA lazily merges the q/k/v convolution weights into a single cached tensor for the fused causal-conv path. During online RL or refit workflows, the underlying q/k/v convolution weights can be updated after warmup, but the derived merged tensor may remain stale. Subsequent inference can then continue using old or dummy weights even after the model weights have been refreshed.

This change:

- adds explicit invalidation for the merged KDA convolution-weight cache
- invalidates the KDA cache before GLM-5.3 model weight loading
- covers both the direct model-loading path and the top-level CausalLM loading path
- keeps the merged-weight cache for normal inference when weights are unchanged
- retains version/storage checks as additional protection against direct tensor mutations
- preserves the hot-path behavior by rebuilding only when needed

This PR is a follow-up to #53906, which introduced the GLM-5.3 implementation.

## Root cause

The KDA layer builds a single merged q|k|v convolution weight tensor and caches it in `_merged_conv_weight`. That cache was not always invalidated when the source q/k/v conv weights were replaced. In online-RL refit/update flows, this allowed stale merged weights to persist across reloads and be reused in later inference steps.

## Fix

- add invalidate_merged_conv_weight() / invalidate_kda_conv_weight_caches() methods to manually clear the stale cache
- invoke invalidation before every load_weights() call so refits always rebuild from fresh weights
- add explicit invalidation hooks for the merged KDA cache
- invoke cache invalidation before GLM-5.3 weight loading so the next access rebuilds from fresh weights

title: [Bugfix] Don't sync-police or retry FlashInfer all-reduce workspace creation in eager mode
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix a nightly regression from #58197 ("[Core] Disable JIT warmup in eager mode").

With `--enforce-eager` the V2 `warmup_kernels` dummy forward is now skipped. The standalone FlashInfer all-reduce (`FlashInferAllReduce`, enabled by default through `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=1`) creates its workspace lazily. The profile run uses large tensors that are above the FlashInfer size cap (e.g. 0.5 MB at TP8 or 2 MB at TP4 on H200), so it never touches the workspace. As a result, the workspace is first created inside the first real `execute_model`, which runs after `enable_gpu_sync_check()`. In CI (`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`), `flashinfer_comm.create_allreduce_fusion_workspace(...)` then raises `RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected` part-way through a collective. The failure is caught and returns `None`, and `get_fi_ar_workspace` does not remember it. The mnnvl attempt fails, the trtllm fallback fails, and the collective creation keeps getting retried. Each retry leaks partially created buffers, which leads to CUDA OOM, then a deadlock, then `TimeoutError: RPC call to sample_tokens timed out` and `EngineDeadError`.

Evidence (nightly build 90589):
- H200 LM Eval DeepSeek V3.2 TP8 (`--enforce-eager`): https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90589#01a0ccda-d861-443c-bcb5-9c8b22260601. At 11:45:56 it logs `Failed to initialize FlashInfer All Reduce workspace: GPU<->CPU sync detected`, followed by repeated `Failed to initialize FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=trtllm`. OOM follows by 11:46:18 and the RPC timeout at 11:50:53.
- B200 HiSparse (GLM-5.2-NVFP4 TP4), job `01a0cd35-9fed-4cff-a2be-b8c4ea5fb773` in the same build, fails the same way.
- Passing build 90513 (before #58197) logs `Initialized FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=mnnvl` during warmup.
- This is likely also behind the H100 Fault Tolerance E2E failure (`rank 0 did not report UNHEALTHY within 45s`) that #58318 is bisecting. That link is not verified.

title: [ROCm] Enable Hisparse on ROCm : Sparse MLA Hot-Buffering
bodyExcerpt:
# [ROCm] HiSparse: host-resident sparse-MLA hot-buffering on gfx950

## Purpose

Enables HiSparse (#53781) on AMD ROCm, verified on gfx950 (MI350X, CDNA4).

HiSparse keeps the bulk of the sparse-MLA KV cache in pinned host memory and
pulls only the indexer-selected rows back just in time, so long-context agentic
sessions stop getting preempted. #53781 landed it CUDA-only.

**Draft.** bf16 KV is complete and benchmarked; `fp8` KV plus HiSparse still
faults on ≥16k prefills (last bullet under Limitations). That is being fixed,
and this PR stays in draft until it is.

## Changes

### 1. Route HiSparse attention through the int64-safe Triton kernel (`rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`)

HiSparse points attention at
`PagedCacheView.attention_cache`, a view over the **whole multi-layer KV slab**,
so the row indices it emits scale with the total block count rather than with
one layer's page table. Off HiSparse the same model emits a max row index of 33;
on HiSparse it reaches 7.5 million. AITER's decode kernel computes
`row_index * row_width` in int32, so on GLM-5.3 (`row_width=576`) it wraps above
row 3,728,270 and answers with approximately zero — no NaN, no assert, no
kernel error.

The backend already carries a Triton ragged path that promotes the slot index to
`tl.int64`, so it is immune past that point. Under HiSparse it becomes
unconditional: `use_hisparse_triton_attn` is set from
`isinstance(index_group, HiSparseMLAIndexGroup)` at construction, and the prefill
call additionally passes `allow_aiter_opus=False` so the dispatcher inside
`rocm_sparse_attn_prefill` cannot fall back into the OPUS ASM kernel, whose KV
addressing width is likewise unverified. No flag, no env var — HiSparse on ROCm
is always on the int64 path.

### 2. ROCm backend wiring (`rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`)

Every CUDA HiSparse backend consumes a **dense** `[tokens, topk]` index tensor
plus `valid_counts`; AITER's tuned decode kernel consumes a **ragged** flat list

title: [Bug]: NIXL P/D mis-transfers a GQA draft's KV (e.g. DFlash) under an MLA target with prefill TP < decode TP
bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `main` @ `711fc55c10` (`0.30.1rc1.dev29+g711fc55c1`); the same code is in v0.30.0.
- 2 × 8×H200, NIXL over UCX/InfiniBand.
- Target `zai-org/GLM-5.3` (MLA, FP8); draft `incoai/GLM-5.3-DFlash2` (`method: dflash`, 8 KV heads, k=4).
- Prefill: `--data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel` (attention TP1). Decode: `--tensor-parallel-size 8`.
- Both sides: `NixlConnector`, `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LBHNC`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

When the **target is MLA** and the **draft is GQA** (e.g. DFlash on GLM-5.3), NIXL P/D with prefill TP < decode TP cannot transfer the draft's KV correctly.

`compute_tp_mapping` builds one `TPMapping` per remote engine from the model-wide `TransferTopology`. For an MLA target that mapping has `total_num_kv_heads=1` and `rank_offset_factor=0`: every rank is assumed to hold identical, replicated KV. That is right for the MLA layers but wrong for the draft, whose KV is split by head across TP. `_is_region_replicated` already classifies the draft's regions as SPLIT, but three places still use the model-wide MLA answer for them:

1. **Handshake size check** (`_validate_remote_agent_handshake`): `model_replicated = self.use_mla or ...` makes every region "replicated", so the correct geometry is rejected. P TP1 holds 8 draft heads per block and each D TP8 rank holds 1:

   ```
   AssertionError: KV cache sizes must match between P and D when replicated
   (region 1: local=2048, remote=16384, bsr=1)
   ```

   A draft block that is *not* scaled by the head ratio is accepted instead.

2. **Read path** (`_build_fa_remote`): the draft regions use `plan.rank_offset_factor == 0`, so every decode rank reads draft head 0 of the prefill block. Output stays correct, because the target verifies every drafted token, but the draft attends to the wrong head on 7 of 8 ranks and acceptance drops.

title: [Perf][Pooling] Avoid blocking seq_lens GPU-to-CPU copy for pooling in FlashInfer metadata builder
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose
FlashInfer's metadata builder needs per-request sequence lengths on the CPU to plan paged KV metadata. For V2 model runner, `seq_lens` live on the GPU, so the builder fetches them with `common_attn_metadata.seq_lens.cpu()`. For pooling models this copy is avoidable; pooling models have no speculative tokens, so `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` maintained by the model runner is exact, not optimistic. The pooling runner already relies on this (`pooling_runner.py`: ["Pooling has no speculative tokens, so this CPU upper bound is exact"](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/pool/pooling_runner.py#L142)). 

This results in a measured performance boost of about 1.35%.

AI assistance (locally hosted GLM 5.3 and Kimi K3 as well as GPT-6 Astra) was used for implementation and analysis. All changed lines were reviewed and validated end-to-end.

title: [KVConnector][NIXL] Opt-in per-layer overlapped WRITE-push for disaggregated KV transfer
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary / motivation

The stock `NixlConnector` transfers KV as a single, monolithic READ at the end of
prefill, so KV transfer does **not** overlap with prefill compute. On
disaggregated (P/D-split) inference this leaves throughput on the table versus
push-style transports.

This PR adds an **opt-in, per-layer overlapped WRITE-push** path: the prefill
side pushes each layer's KV to the decode worker as soon as that layer is
computed, overlapping KV transfer with the tail of prefill and closing the
throughput gap against push-style connectors — while staying on the open,
standard UCX/NIXL path.

Design notes / rationale live in the commit message and inline docstrings in
`push_worker.py` (module docstring describes the event-driven push pipeline).

## Design

- **Per-layer save hook** (`save_kv_layer`): records a CUDA event per layer and
  enqueues **one RDMA WRITE per KV region off-thread**, so the forward thread is
  never blocked on transfer.
- **Seal** (`wait_for_save`): finalizes the request. A model-agnostic
  **"completeness sweep"** at seal time writes any KV regions **not** covered by
  a per-layer hook (e.g. the GLM-5.1 DSA indexer caches), guaranteeing no stale
  KV is left on the decode side.
- **Scheduler bookkeeping** (`push_scheduler.py`): producer/consumer tracking
  suppresses the monolithic WRITE when layer-wise mode is on, and holds the
  engine loop open until the per-layer WRITEs complete.
- **D-side robustness fixes** (small, independently useful):
  - Seed `remote_*` params on the abort/reject recv path so an aborted/rejected
    request no longer `KeyError`s the EngineCore.
  - Handle `num_external_tokens <= 0` (full prefix-cache hit / no external
    tokens) by flipping `do_remote_prefill` off instead of staging an unseeded
    recv.

## Opt-in & safety

- Gated entirely by env var **`VLLM_NIXL_LAYERWISE_PUSH`** (plus
  **`VLLM_NIXL_LAYERWISE_DEFER_TIMEOUT`** for the deferred-write watchdog).
  Both are declared in `vllm/envs.py` alongsid

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve DeepSeek's unclosed final tool parameter
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Addresses the DeepSeek V4, V3.2, and V4.1 part of #57827. When a tool call ends without closing its final DSML parameter tag, final conversion drops that parameter. An unfinished `string="false"` value can also be dropped when it is not yet valid JSON.

This change preserves the trailing parameter in final conversion. During streaming, it defers invalid partial JSON until its type is stable, so later chunks cannot invalidate arguments already sent to the client.

Adds regression tests for streaming and non-streaming calls with string, numeric, and invalid JSON values.

Together, this PR, #58349 (MiniMax M2), and #58418 (GLM-4.7 MoE) cover all three parser cases reported in #57827. The issue should be closed once all three PRs have merged. This PR is distinct from #57707, which fixes Qwen3, and #53739, which changes the shared streaming engine.

AI assistance was used to develop this change.

## Test Plan

Run the DeepSeek parser suites:

`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/parser/engine tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v32.py tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py -q`

Run the repository's pre-commit hooks on the four changed files.

## Test Result

- 148 DeepSeek parser tests passed. The run emitted 14 Torch JIT deprecation warnings.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed when run directly on the staged files.
- No model inference evaluation was run. This is deterministic post-generation parsing, covered by CPU-only parser tests.

title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Add AITER topk backend for decodes
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash indexer dispatches to `torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_decode` during decode. This leads to two calls to HIP kernel `topKPerRowDecode512DeviceLengthAware` which is quite slow for this model. We instead allow dispatching to an AITER kernel through the SparseIndexerTopk abstraction.

Enable with `--sparse-indexer-topk-backend aiter`.

Benchmarking suggest to use this AITER kernel whenever ctx>=64k.

Models like DSv4 keep their old path, because DSv4 uses a different tuning (see `dsv4_indexer_prefers_native_top_k`)

**Perf: -1-5% ITL on 64k+ ISL.** 

## Test Plan

### 1. GSM8k vs main on gfx950 for GLM-5.3-Flash and DSv4-Flash

### 2. GLM-5.3-Flash perf diff on vllm bench serve sweep (MI350)

```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-num-seqs 512 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE  
  --sparse-indexer-topk-backend aiter
```

Check where the aiter kernel is beneficial:

python3 benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_top_k_per_row.py \
  --phase decode --dist indexer --rows 1 4 8 \
  --lens 1024 2048 4096 8192 16384 32768 --capacity 262144 --top-k 512
```

title: [V1][Perf] Skip the block-table H2D copy when no row changed
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`BlockTable.commit_block_table()` in the V1 model runner re-uploads the whole
active `[num_reqs, max_num_blocks_per_req]` block table host→device on every
step, for every KV-cache group, even when no row changed since the last upload.

A row only changes when a request is admitted, moved, removed, or crosses a
KV-block boundary. This PR tracks a conservative interval of rows changed since
the last commit that covered them and skips the copy when that interval lies
outside `[0, num_reqs)`. When it does copy, it is the same single contiguous
bulk transfer as today.

Model Runner V2 already avoids this (`StagedWriteTensor`), and #47936 (same
idea, per-row scatter) was closed for that reason. The V1 runner is still the
**default** on ROCm for `DeepseekV32ForCausalLM`, `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` and
`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` (`ROCM_DEFAULT_MRV1_ARCHITECTURES`, added after #47936
was closed in #53155), and on every platform when V2 is declined (ngram /
draft-model / suffix / medusa spec decode, elastic EP, DBO, SP at TP>1,
`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, ...). If V1 is going away soon enough that this
is not worth carrying, say so and I will close it.

**Expected impact is small and I am not claiming a throughput win.** The whole
`commit_block_table` is ~58 µs of a 21–44 ms DeepSeek-V4-Flash step, so the
ceiling is ~0.06 % (50 concurrent) to ~0.22 % (3 concurrent) of step time. What
it removes is per-step CPU work and a host→device copy on the compute stream
that scales with `max_num_reqs × max_model_len / block_size` per group.

### Details

- `append_row` / `clear_row` / `move_row` / `swap_row` widen the dirty interval
  (`add_row` goes through `append_row`). `move_row` marks **both** rows: since
  #49757 it also zeroes the vacated source, and a later padded dummy-run commit
  must upload that zeroed row.
- `commit_block_table(num_reqs)` only transfers `[0, num_reqs)`, so rows dirtied
  at or beyond `num_reqs` stay dirty (`[num_reqs, hi]`) until a commit wide
  enou

title: [Feature] Restore concurrent partial prefill limit (max_concurrent_prefills) in V1 scheduler
bodyExcerpt:
Reviving #55256's clean threshold-independent `max_concurrent_prefills` limit for the V1 scheduler to fix the exact head-of-line blocking issue reported in #57413.

As detailed in #57413, without a cap on concurrent partial prefills, long-context RAG workloads (e.g. 100k+ tokens) completely stall V1's scheduling queue. Short requests are forced to wait for many iterations until massive partial prefills finish.

This reintroduces `max_concurrent_prefills` directly into the V1 scheduler's `WAITING` loop. By bounding how many requests can simultaneously hold partial prefill state, we allow interleaving and dramatically reduce tail TTFT (as validated by the community on 4x B200 / GLM-5.3-Flash).

Original patch credit to @fululi12 in #55256. Rebased and verified against main.

Fixes #57413.

title: [RFC]: KVPP (KV pipeline parallel, LayerSplit) for vLLM
bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation.

This proposal is inspired by **Section 4, “LayerSplit,”** of Z.ai's [*Scaling Pain of Coding Agent Serving: Lessons from Debugging GLM-5 at Scale*](https://z.ai/blog/scaling-pain). LayerSplit introduces layer-wise ownership of KV-cache storage and makes the cache available to the other ranks when a layer runs. This RFC describes how to express that idea in vLLM's KV-cache planning and model-execution lifecycle.

An experimental implementation already exists in [vllm-ascend's KVPP design](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/main/developer_guide/Design_Documents/kvpp/) and [feature guide](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/main/user_guide/feature_guide/kvpp/).

### Terminology: why “KV-PP”

The existing implementation calls this feature **KVPP**, short for **KV pipeline parallel**. We propose writing the same name as **KV-PP** when explaining the parallelism axis. If vLLM's Decode Context Parallelism (DCP) is viewed, at the KV-storage level, as **KV-CP**—partitioning a sequence's KV tokens across ranks—then KV-PP is the complementary **layer-axis** partition: ranks persist different layers' KV caches and obtain a complete layer before using it.

| Conceptual axis | Persistent KV ownership | Access during attention |
| --- | --- | --- |
| KV-CP analogy (DCP) | Different token or context portions of a layer | Distributed attention uses the rank-local context and combines results. |
| KV-PP (this RFC) | Different complete layers | The layer owner makes its cache available to all computing ranks before cache access. |

### Goals

- Increase the logical cache-block capacity when replicated, persistent KV storage is the limiting resource.
- Keep scheduler block IDs, prefix-cache semantics, and request admission based on one complete logical KV-cache specification.
- Allow a device backend to choose layer owners, physical layouts, and a collective transport without teaching the scheduler about those details.
- Define synchronization and connector ru

title: [Bugfix] Skip FP8-dequant fast paths for PP-missing layers in GLM-5.3-Flash load
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55725. GLM-5.3-Flash crashes at weight load on multi-node (2×8 H100) with `KeyError: 'layers.11.self_attn.fused_qkv_a_proj.weight'` on every second-node worker, while single-node runs fine.

## Root cause

With 2 nodes the run is pipeline-parallel (PP=2), so layer 11's params exist only on stage-0 ranks. The attached log (`layer11.log`) shows all `Worker_PP1_TP0..7` crashing; PP0 is clean. The normal load path guards every weight with `is_pp_missing_parameter` (glm5next/common/model.py), but the two FP8-dequant fast paths bypass it and index `params_dict` directly:

- `_try_load_fp8_attn_proj` → `params_dict[target_w]` (the traceback in the issue)
- `_try_load_fp8_indexer_wk` → `params_dict[fused_name]` (same class of hole)

On a PP rank that doesn't hold the layer, `params_dict` has no such key → KeyError before the normal path ever gets a chance to skip the weight.

## Fix

In both fast paths, return `False` when the target param is absent from `params_dict`, so the weight falls through to the normal path, which skips it via `is_pp_missing_parameter`. The indexer-wk guard is placed *before* buffering, so PP ranks also don't accumulate fp8 tensors that nobody loads. Behavior on ranks that hold the layer is byte-identical.

## Verification

No multi-node GPU here, so verified by driving both functions directly with the exact crashing weight names, on the MI350X pod against the patched module:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| PP1-style params_dict (layer 11 absent), fp8 `q_a_proj` weight + scale | not consumed, nothing loaded → falls to normal skip path (was: KeyError) |
| PP0-style control (BF16 `fused_qkv_a_proj` present) | consumed + loaded, unchanged |
| PP1, indexer `wk` weight + scale | not consumed → normal skip |
| PP0 control, indexer `wk` | consumed + loaded, unchanged |

Pre-commit: all hooks pass. Single-node (TP-only) behavior is untouched — the guards only trigger when the target param is missing.

title: [Bugfix] Invalidate KDA merged conv-weight cache on weight reload
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55087. GLM-5.3 KDA merges the q/k/v short-conv weights into one cached tensor (`_merged_conv_weight`), built lazily on first forward. Online-RL workflows warm up with dummy weights (cache built), then refit `q_conv1d`/`k_conv1d`/`v_conv1d` — but the cached merge is never invalidated, so inference silently keeps using the pre-refit convolution weights.

## Approach

Weight loading dispatches on the param's stamped `weight_loader` (`getattr(param, "weight_loader", default_weight_loader)` in `AutoWeightsLoader`). So the cache can be invalidated at exactly the point the weights change: in `Glm5NextLinearAttention.__init__`, wrap each conv weight's stamped loader so any write clears `_merged_conv_weight`. The next forward rebuilds it from the current params. No new hooks, no changes to the reload machinery.

## Coverage / limitations

- ✅ Initial load (loaders run before first forward; cache built after anyway)
- ✅ Checkpoint-format refit: `reload_weights` → `model.load_weights` → stamped loaders → cache cleared
- ✅ Layerwise reload: re-dispatches through the same stamped loaders
- ❌ Kernel-format refit (`param.copy_` bypass) writes params without loaders — the cache is NOT invalidated there. That path also skips every other derived-weight rebuild in the tree (same class of limitation); noted for follow-up if it matters in practice.

A `_version`-based approach was considered and rejected: the default loader writes via `param.data.copy_`, which bumps neither `param._version` nor `param.data._version` (verified on torch 2.10/ROCm), so version tracking cannot see the main refit path.

## Verification

Ad-hoc functional test on MI350X against a real `Glm5NextLinearAttention` (gloo TP1, minimal `Glm5NextConfig`):

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Build layer, populate merge cache | OK |
| Refit `q_conv1d` through its real stamped weight loader | cache **invalidated** |
| Next merge uses refit values | OK |
| No refit → cache persists (no spurious invalidation

title: [Perf][HiSparse] Allow full graphs for P/D prompt-token replay
bodyExcerpt:
A successful HiSparse P/D full-prompt import still replays the final prompt token to produce logits. Model Runner V2 marks that token as logical prefill, which currently disqualifies an otherwise single-token decode batch from FULL CUDA graphs. A new P/D arrival can consequently send the whole batch through the fallback graph path.

This patch records successful full-prompt imports in scheduler/request state and carries the imported length to MRV2. Graph dispatch treats the last-token replay as decode-shaped when HiSparse is enabled, the query length is one, and PCP is absent. Logical prefill state is retained for input preparation and HiSparse loading. Genuine prefills, partial imports, failed transfers, preempted requests, and speculative/multi-token replay retain their existing classification. The marker is reset on preemption and each receive completion.

Based on main `82daf9f5`. Main now has a separate sliding-window bounded-replay path; that path is explicitly excluded when recording this marker. No connector transport, model math, scheduler-overhead optimization, Rust frontend fix, or configuration change is included.

The equivalent patch has run on B300 with GLM-5.3 NVFP4 (`RadixArk/GLM-5.3-NVFP4`, revision `11af4cba759e6559eda70358a5778bd1bddddd78`), 1 EP8 prefill node and 1 EP8 decode node, FP8 KV, HiSparse, index cache, NIXL, Mooncake, DeepEP LL decode, and FULL_AND_PIECEWISE breakable graphs. title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] "Fit kpool top-k indices to AITER" with a single Triton kernel
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

The existing kernel is implemented in pytorch and leads to **18** elementwise kernel launched per forward. We replace it with a single triton kernel.

**Perf: -5% ITL, +3-5% out tok/s**

## What it does

GLM-5.3-Flash's indexer selects `topk + kpool_tail` tokens, where the tail size is <kpool=4 and depends on the number of tokens in the request. AITER expects a fixed topk value independent of request length. Hence we use `fit_kpool_indices_to_aiter` to select the a fixed topk tokens from history and tail respectively, and disregard any extras. 

The kernel prioritizes selecting the tokens from the tail, and then selects the highest prio tokens from the history, until topk tokens are chosen.

title: [Bugfix] GLM-5.3-Flash: fp8 plan dtype on SM90 sparse MLA, and right-size the indexer prefill workspace
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55221.

Two independent fixes for GLM-5.3-Flash, both live on `main` after #53906 landed.

**1. `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` cannot start on the SM90 sparse MLA backend.** An fp8 KV
cache is allocated as `uint8` storage and `run()` views it as `float8_e4m3fn`, but
`plan()` was handed the storage dtype, which the FlashInfer wrapper rejects:
`ValueError: MLA kv_data_type torch.uint8 is not supported`. One-line dtype fix in
`FlashInferMLASparseSM90Builder`.

**2. The indexer prefill workspace is sized in the wrong unit.**
`get_max_prefill_buffer_size()` returns a token count (`max_model_len * 40` entries of
132 bytes), but this indexer's KV is pool-granular: the spec carries
`compress_ratio == index_kpool`, and `split_indexer_prefill_chunks()` is fed compressed
sequence lengths. `deepseek_v4/attention.py` already divides at the same call site.
At `--max-model-len 1048576` with `index_kpool = 4` this locks ~5.16 GiB per GPU during
the memory profile, straight out of the KV budget. Reported by @nood-co1 in #53906.

## Not a duplicate

- #51252 divides the *builder's* chunk budget by `compress_ratio` for DeepSeek; this is

title: [Bugfix] Scale sliding-window block size in packed KV cache grouping
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`_get_packed_kv_cache_groups` returns before `unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size`, so plain `SlidingWindowSpec`s keep the smallest kernel block size (16) while the packed block is sized by the widest group. Each 16-token sliding-window block then takes a whole packed block.

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 + DFlash, `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLNHC`, max_model_len 262,144, 40 GiB KV on one GB10: 442,705 KV tokens, with the draft sliding-window group at block size 16 and attention at 592. The default layout gives 1,043,626. This scales unpadded `SlidingWindowSpec`s to the largest attention block size before bucketing, as unification does on the uniform-page path. The same config then gives 1,538,467 tokens in 5 groups.

No open PR or issue covers this. #58207 changes the uniform-page width selection, which this path bypasses. #56983 rescales draft sliding-window blocks only in the GLM-5 grouping path.

title: [Bug] `ep_gather` output store overflows int32 with DeepEP v2 expanded layout (IMA in `_fwd_kernel_ep_gather`)
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

`_fwd_kernel_ep_gather` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/deep_gemm_utils.py` computes the output row offset as `cur_token * output_tensor_stride0` in int32. With hidden size K = 6144, this wraps once the output has more than 2^31 / 6144 = 349,525 rows. The store then lands out of bounds and faults with `cudaErrorIllegalAddress`.

#53914 (fe284ea17d) fixed the matching **input** read (`source_token_index_i64 * input_tensor_stride0`). The **output** store is still int32 on main (9ed81581, line 410):

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9ed81581a896a5bf0448b26d43f52486a435f799/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/deep_gemm_utils.py#L405-L413

```python
        tl.store(
            output_tensor
            + cur_token * output_tensor_stride0   # int32 * int32
            + cur_block * BLOCK_D
            + off_d,
            ...
```

With the DeepEP v2 all2all backend, the gather receives an **expanded** layout: `recv_topk_ids` is `(rows, 1)`, with one row per (token, local expert) pair. So the output has as many rows as the permuted input, and both offsets hit the same limit. When `topk_ids` is `(tokens, topk)`, the output has one row per received token and normally stays far below the limit, which is presumably why this hasn't shown up before.

## Setup

- GLM-5.2-FP8 (K = 6144, 256 experts, top-8), `--moe-backend deep_gemm`, `--all2all-backend deepep_v2` (hybrid mode)
- 4 nodes × 8 × H100, DP4 × PCP8 (DCP8), TP1, EP32, eager
- vLLM from #57075 at bf0dca88, with the #53914 `ep_gather` input fix applied on top
- `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096` (8192 fails the same way, sooner)

## Evidence

With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, the first memory-profiling forward (`determine_available_memory` → `profile_run`) faults in the gather on the busiest EP rank:

```

  → _fwd_kernel_ep_gather
RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered

title: [Perf][Spec Decode] Drop the per-request .item() from the ngram_gpu draft-trim loop
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

With `ngram_gpu` speculative decoding, `update_scheduler_for_invalid_drafts()` runs on
the host once per engine step. It waits for the draft-count D2H copy and then trims each
request's spec slots to its valid draft count. It read each count with

```python
valid_k = int(num_valid_draft_tokens_cpu[req_index].item())
```

`Tensor.__getitem__` allocates a fresh 0-d tensor per request before `.item()` unwraps
it, and that allocation dominates the loop's cost.

This PR:

- takes one `.numpy()` view of the CPU buffer outside the loop and indexes that. It is
  zero-copy, because the buffer is already a CPU tensor;
- returns early when `scheduled_spec_decode_tokens` is empty. The scheduler omits
  requests without draft tokens from that dict, so an empty mapping means every loop
  iteration would be skipped, and the event does not need to be awaited;
- looks up `scheduled_spec_decode_tokens` before `req_id_to_index`, so requests that did
  not speculate skip one dict lookup;
- adds unit tests for the function, which had none.

Behaviour is unchanged: `total_num_scheduled_tokens`, `num_scheduled_tokens` and
`scheduled_spec_decode_tokens` come out identical to main's.

Scope: this is host-side bookkeeping in the V1 runner. `ngram_gpu` currently forces the
V1 runner (it is in `_get_v2_model_runner_unsupported_features`), so every model that
runs `ngram_gpu` calls this once per step. The function sits in `_update_states`, which
runs outside CUDA graphs, so it executes under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` as well. It does not
touch any kernel, the n-gram matcher, or acceptance.

Related PRs:
- #44056 and #52097 both make this function return a `dict` of trimmed counts. They
  compose with this change; whichever lands second needs `return {}` on the early-return
  path.
- #40704 ports `ngram_gpu` to the V2 runner. After it lands, this path remains the
  default only for `ROCM_DEFAULT_MRV1_ARCHITECTURES` (DeepSeek-V3.2/V4, GLM-MoE-DSA) or
  with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`.

title: [Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Batch paired KDA gate projections (f_b_proj/g_b_proj) into one bmm
bodyExcerpt:
## What

`f_b_proj` and `g_b_proj` in the GLM-5.3-Flash KDA layer are two same-shape
BF16 GEMMs (`[M, 128] x [128, 1024]` per rank at TP8) applied to adjacent
`head_dim`-wide shards of the merged `in_proj_qkvbfg_a` output. Run them as
one batched GEMM:

- the paired weight is stacked in `process_weights_after_loading`, which runs
  on every load/refit — the stack cannot go stale and no allocation happens
  inside the captured forward;
- inputs are read in place via `as_strided` on the existing projection
  buffer — no copies, no layout change;
- non-BF16 weights keep the two-Linear path.

## Benchmarks (H20, BF16, CUDA graph replay)

Paired f_b+g_b per KDA layer per step: 5.4 -> 4.4 us for M=1..64
(-17% to -22%, decode and spec-verify shapes); no regression at large M
(within 1% at M=8192). Numerics: bit-identical to the two-Linear path
(max_abs_diff = 0, M=1..256).

## Test

- `pytest tests/models/glm5next/` — 15 passed on H20, including the new
  `test_kda_paired_projection.py`: bit-identical vs the two Linears
  (M=1/5/64/256), paired weight rebuilt on re-run of
  `process_weights_after_loading`, disabled for non-BF16 weights.
- Greedy e2e smoke (12 prompts x 256 tokens, temp=0, spec decode on):
  coherent outputs.

Related: #56298 fixes the stale lazy cache for the merged conv weight — this
change builds its paired weight in the post-load hook instead of caching it
in forward. #57318 speeds up a GDN projection with FlashInfer; different op.
No open PR covers pairing these two projections.

## What

`fused_recurrent_kda_fwd` uses a fixed launch config (BV=8, num_warps=1,

and `num_stages = 2` only when `N*HV <= 32` — large grids keep the default 3,
so non-H20 SM90 parts see no untuned stage change. num_warps stays 1, so the
reduction order is unchanged and outputs are bit-identical to the default
config. Non-SM90 platforms keep the defaults.

| n_req |   1  |   2  |   4  |   8  |  16  |  32  |  64  |

|   TP8 | +16.5% | +18.7% | +17.7% | +14.3% | +6.0% | +6.4% | +9.2% |
|   TP4 | +18.5% | +16.5% | +14.4% | +7.9%  | +6.4% | +10.4% | +13.0% |

title: [Bug]: minimax_m2 / glm47_moe / deepseek_v4 arg converters drop the last parameter when the model omits the closing tag (same class as #57699)
bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

- vLLM main (probed 2026-09-20; minimax_m2.py @ 24bfbd5d, deepseek_v4.py @ 39e33db7)
- Parser-only bug: reproduction needs no GPU, no model, no server.

### Describe the bug

#57699 describes a bug class for qwen3: when the model closes the tool call **without closing the last parameter tag**, the trailing value is dropped by the final (partial=False) conversion. #57707 fixes qwen3 only - but the same structure exists in three other converters, none of which are covered by that PR:

**1. minimax_m2 - vllm/parser/minimax_m2.py `_minimax_m2_arg_converter`**

`_PARAM_RE` only ends a value at the closing parameter tag or at the next parameter open tag. The trailing `_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE` extraction runs only under `if partial:`, so the final conversion drops the last parameter. With `stream_arg_deltas=True`, the streamed partial conversions have already emitted the value, and the flush at tool-call end produces a shorter JSON - the same client-visible divergence as #57699.

Model output:

```
<minimax:tool_call><invoke name="get_weather">
<parameter name="city">Seattle</parameter>
<parameter name="unit">celsius
</invoke></minimax:tool_call>
```

non-streaming: `arguments == {"city": "Seattle"}` - `unit` is silently lost.

**2. glm47_moe - vllm/parser/glm47_moe.py `_glm47_arg_converter`**

`_ARG_RE` requires the value close tag; the `_PARTIAL_ARG_RE` extraction is under `if partial:`. `stream_arg_deltas=True` is set. Same divergence: a tool call that omits the last closing arg_value tag yields non-streaming `arguments` without the trailing parameter.

**3. deepseek_v4 (inherited by v32/v41) - vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py `_dsml_arg_converter`**

Same `if partial:` structure. Additionally, the partial branch swallows JSON failures with `contextlib.suppress` and **drops the value entirely**, while the complete branch falls back to the literal text. title: [ROCm][Bugfix][Spec Decode] Add compact_topk_indices to the ROCm DSA MTP drafter
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

On ROCm, MTP speculative decoding crashes for every GLM-5.2 / GLM-5.3 checkpoint on
current `main`, out of the box:

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 -tp 4 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

```
File "vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py", line 613, in propose
    self.model.model.compact_topk_indices(token_indices_to_sample)
AttributeError: 'DeepseekV32MultiTokenPredictor' object has no attribute
'compact_topk_indices'
```

The engine starts, and the first draft step fails on every TP worker.

### Cause

GLM-5.x checkpoints set `index_share_for_mtp_iteration: true`. With that set, the legacy
proposer checks the drafter for `set_skip_topk` and then calls both methods:

```python
if self._share_mtp_indices and hasattr(self.model.model, "set_skip_topk"):
    self.model.model.set_skip_topk(True)
    self.model.model.compact_topk_indices(token_indices_to_sample)
```

On ROCm, `deepseek_v32` and `glm_moe_dsa` are dispatched to
`vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd/` (#51915). That module's `DeepseekV32MultiTokenPredictor`
implements `set_skip_topk` but not `compact_topk_indices`, which #47238 added only to the
generic drafter in `deepseek_mtp.py`. It is the only drafter on `main` with one method and
not the other. The generic, NVIDIA DSA, GLM-5-Next, HY-V4 and both Qwen4-Exp drafters
have both.

### Change

- `amd/mtp.py`: add `compact_topk_indices` to `DeepseekV32MultiTokenPredictor`. It
  follows the amd drafter's own layout: `topk_indices_buffer` lives on `self_attn`
  itself, where `set_skip_topk` already looks for `skip_topk`, not under

  silently leave the buffer uncompacted, and steps 1+ would reuse the wrong rows instead

title: [Bugfix][Model] Make Glm5NextMoE.forward rank-agnostic
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`Glm5NextMoE.forward` starts with:

```python
num_tokens, hidden_dim = hidden_states.shape
...
return final_hidden_states.view(num_tokens, hidden_dim)
```

which only works for the rank-2 `[tokens, hidden]` layout. Model runners that pass bucketed rank-3 `[1, T, hidden]` activations — the Intel Gaudi backend does — raise `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)` in every MoE layer.

The fix flattens on the way in and restores the caller's leading dims on the way out. It deliberately does not broadcast: `sequence_parallel_chunk`, `tensor_model_parallel_all_gather` and the `[:num_tokens]` slice inside the block all require tokens to live on dim 0.

No-op for rank-2 input.

Found while bringing up GLM-5.3-Flash on Intel Gaudi 2.

## Test Plan

`tests/models/glm5next/test_moe_input_rank.py`, CPU-only, no model weights needed. Exercises the block's shape contract for rank-2 and rank-3 input: the experts must see a rank-2 `[tokens, hidden]` view, and the caller must get its original shape back.

The test reads `Glm5NextMoE.forward` via `inspect.getsource` and asserts the flattening is present, so it tracks the implementation instead of silently drifting from a copy.

```bash
pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_moe_input_rank.py
```

## Test Result

With the fix:

```
3 passed
```

Against the unpatched code the same tests fail.

End-to-end, this was one of the changes needed to get GLM-5.3-Flash serving on Intel Gaudi 2 (TP=4); with it and the related mHC fixes the model produces correct output.

Follow-up to merged #55277: use compact 528-byte `fp8_ds_mla` rows for native NoPE on the FlashInfer SM120 backend. title: [Bugfix][SM120][MLA] Support NoPE sparse MLA (GLM-5.3-Flash) on the FlashInfer SM120 backend
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Enable native NoPE (`qk_rope_head_dim=0`) cache writes for GLM-5.3-Flash on `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`, without padding the query or allocating a synthetic RoPE tensor.

Rebased onto `a6131b0e656e18eeb3797b8856aa3dbc69efd8e5`. The former physical top-k capacity patch has been dropped: #53781 already implements it in the shared `_run_mqa_kernel`, including HiSparse paths. This PR now contains the cache-writer fix and regression tests only.

## Changes

- Accept `pe_dim` 0 or 64 for `fp8_ds_mla`.
- Preserve the existing 656-byte cache row: 512 bytes of FP8 latent, 16 bytes of FP32 tile scales, and 128 bytes of RoPE/reserved storage.
- For NoPE, do not read the empty `k_pe` tensor; zero the reserved tail. The 64-dimensional RoPE path is unchanged.
- Compare BF16 NoPE writes byte-for-byte with the existing zero-RoPE path at block sizes 64/256. Fixed slots cover a block boundary and an invalid token; explicit assertions check zero tails and untouched sentinel rows. Existing tests retain responsibility for quantization correctness.

title: [Quantization] Select per-token NVFP4 MoE backends explicitly
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Online `nvfp4_per_token` previously advertised the ordinary NVFP4 activation scheme even though execution uses per-token scales. This could select an incompatible backend. One-sided dispatch also sized its buffer for packed FP4 although the per-token path sends unpacked activations and quantizes inside the expert kernel.

- Add `kNvfp4DynamicToken` and use it for online NVFP4 MoE selection.
- Declare TRTLLM support and size modular expert workspaces for unpacked inputs.
- Size one-sided communication buffers with an optional `input_dtype` override. An explicit BF16/FP16 dtype reserves `hidden_dim * input_dtype.itemsize` activation bytes and zero scale bytes; `None` preserves quant-config-based sizing. Per-token NVFP4 supplies `moe_config.in_dtype`. This supports deferred quantization without relying on another BF16 layer enlarging the shared buffer.
- Cover both packed/deferred dispatch sizing, including BF16/FP16 dtype overrides and early rejection of FP32, FP8 E4M3, FP8 E5M2, and INT8 overrides. FlashInfer’s per-token NVFP4 quantizer accepts only BF16/FP16 activations; its FP32 per-token scales do not imply FP32 activation support.

title: [Attention] Portable Triton sparse-MLA fallback for SM12x (consumer Blackwell)
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

DSA models (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.2) currently have **no working sparse-attention backend on
consumer Blackwell** (SM12x: RTX 5090, GB10): the native FlashMLA sparse kernels
(`vllm._flashmla_C`) only build for sm90/sm100, and the sole SM12x option,
`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`, livelocks under sustained load — GPUs pin at 100 % with zero
output until the NCCL watchdog kills the server. Fixes #51921 (on SM12x).

This makes the `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` backend work on SM12x by binding portable **Triton**
implementations of `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` / `flash_mla_with_kvcache` when the native extension
can't serve the device. The kernels are from #49026 (@marksunner, validated there on
sm_121/GB10) — this PR is that work rebased onto current main as a first-class code path
instead of that PR's runtime monkeypatch, with its model-side diffs dropped (main already has
that content). Supersedes/continues #49026 — happy to hand back or co-drive.

## Scope

This path covers **DeepSeek-geometry sparse MLA** — `qk_rope_head_dim = 64`, i.e. the
512 NoPE + 64 RoPE = **576** head layout: DeepSeek-V3.2/V4.1 and GLM-5.2. The Triton kernels
and the `fp8_ds_mla` 656-byte per-token entry are built around that 576 layout
(`get_supported_head_sizes() == [576]`).

**Not covered:** NoPE MLA models (`qk_rope_head_dim = 0`, `head_size = 512`) such as
GLM-5.3-Flash. Those are correctly rejected at the head-size gate and need the `pe_dim != 64`
work in #55277 / #53969 *in addition to* this PR. Thanks to @haqishen for confirming this
boundary on real SM120 hardware (see comments).

Changes:
- `ops/flashmla.py`: `_use_triton_sparse_mla()` (auto on SM12x; `VLLM_TRITON_MLA_SPARSE`
  forces on/off) selects the Triton binding; `is_flashmla_sparse_supported()` reports True
  there; `get_mla_metadata` returns `(None, None)` (the Triton kernels self-schedule).
- New files: `sm12x_sparse_mla_attn.py`, `sparse_mla_kernels.py`, `sparse_mla_env.py`,
  `ops/deepseek_v4_ops/

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Fix SM90 sparse MLA IMA on >16k-row steps by chunking plan/run
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes a CUDA illegal-memory-access crash whenever a single scheduled step packs more than 16384 query rows on the SM90 sparse MLA backend (the GLM-5.3-Flash default), e.g. `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768` with a 28k-token prefill chunk, or 32k tokens scheduled across concurrent requests.

**Root cause (flashinfer 0.6.18.post1, the pinned version).** The SM90 batch-MLA plan hardcodes `max_total_num_works = 16384` and never checks it: the load-balancing schedule is `std::copy`'d into per-array regions sized for 16384 works, so a larger step silently overwrites neighboring schedule arrays, and the kernel then reads garbage `q_indptr`/`kv_indptr` (IMA in `BatchMLAPageAttentionHopper`). This backend feeds one varlen row per query token, so any step with more than 16384 scheduled tokens overflows. flashinfer 0.7.0 raised the limit to 65536 and added a hard error, but vLLM pins `flashinfer-python==0.6.18`. Small overflows (e.g. 16385 works) do not even fault — they run with a corrupted schedule.

**Fix.** When a step has more than `_MAX_PLAN_CHUNK_ROWS = 8192` query rows, plan and run the MQA as independent row chunks: the builder plans each chunk into its own `_SM90State` (a lazily grown pool), and `forward_mqa` runs each state's row range and concatenates. Each row is already an independent varlen query (causality is encoded in the top-k selection, `causal=False`), so chunking is exact. The bound is 8192 rather than 16384 so the work count stays provably under 16384 even with split-kv rows: works <= rows + total_kv_len / kv_len_limit, and `kv_len_limit` tracks total_kv_len / num_clusters. Steps at or under the limit keep the existing single-plan path unchanged, including CUDA-graph replay.

## Not a duplicate

- #56969 fixed a different OOB in this backend (mixed prefill/decode batches); it is in the tested tree and the crash still reproduces without this change.
- #55222 fixes the fp8 plan dtype and the indexer prefill workspace sizing; different call sites.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Implement get_top_tokens() on the generic MTP drafter
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`speculative_config.use_local_argmax_reduction` is unusable with the generic MTP
drafter: enabling it does not fall back to a slower path, it fails engine startup.

```
ValueError: use_local_argmax_reduction is enabled but draft model DeepSeekMTP
does not implement get_top_tokens().
```

The reduction itself already lives in core as `LogitsProcessor.get_top_tokens()` — each
TP rank argmaxes its own vocab shard and only `(value, index)` pairs are gathered. Both
opt-in sites probe the draft model for the method and raise without it:

- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py` (V2 model runner)
- `vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py`

`vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_mtp.py` has `compute_logits` but no
`get_top_tokens`, so every checkpoint that resolves to it raises. On current `main` that
is the `deepseek_v3` family — DeepSeek-V3 and R1 — on every platform:

| checkpoint `model_type` | architecture | resolved draft class | platform |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek_v3` | `DeepSeekMTPModel` | `deepseek_mtp.DeepSeekMTP` | all |
| `deepseek_v32`, `glm_moe_dsa` | `DeepseekV32MTPModel` | `deepseek_mtp.DeepSeekMTP` | XPU, CPU only |

`DeepSeekMTPModel` maps to `deepseek_mtp` in `registry.py` with no platform dispatch, so a
DeepSeek-V3 / R1 MTP drafter is this class on CUDA and ROCm alike. `deepseek_v32` and
`glm_moe_dsa` are dispatched in `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/__init__.py`: CUDA uses
`nvidia/mtp.py`, which already implements the method, and since #51915 ROCm uses
`amd/mtp.py`. So for the DSA family only XPU and CPU still fall back here. `amd/mtp.py`'s
own `DeepseekV32MTP` has the same gap, but it is a different file with its own pre-head
path and is out of scope for this PR.

This PR adds the two forwarding methods, mirroring the `compute_logits` pair already in
the file. The capability has been rolled out per model since the flag landed in #34049,
and `deepseek_v3` was never covered on any platform.

title: [PCP][DCP] Enable PCP+DCP on sparse-MLA models
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Enable DCP to run alongside PCP on sparse-MLA models, so a deployment can shard the KV cache for decode and still split prefill query work across ranks.

This change:

- gives the sparse indexer a DCP-gathered prefill path: this rank's KV shard is all-gathered across the DCP group
- gives the FlashMLA-sparse backend the matching prefill path, with a rank-major gathered KV workspace and a PCP-invariant chunk plan every rank derives identically without communicating;
- replicates prefills too short to fill all `2*PCP` chunks when DCP is on, which keeps the per-region row count identical on every rank — the invariant the gathered layout rests on;
- adds a MoE all-reduce fast path for steps whose rows are all PCP-replicated, replacing an unconditional all-gather + reduce-scatter that duplicated every decode row `PCP` times;
- relaxes the PCP CUDA graph restriction for PCP+DCP to everything up to `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, keeping only `FULL` over mixed batches rejected;

fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53573
Additionally
- fixes a pre-existing kernel/reference divergence: the top-k index kernel applied the block-table bound to prefill-workspace rows, while `_triton_convert_reference_impl` has always specified that only `-1` is invalid there. The existing test missed it because `token_indices[6, 150:160]` is an empty slice on a 128-column tensor;

## Test Plan

- NVIDIA GB200 x4
- GLM-5.3, NVFP4 weights
- TP=1, PCP=4, DCP=4

## Test Result

GSM8K, 1319 questions, TP1+PCP4+DCP4, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`. Seven runs across the

| Run | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---|---|
| TP4 | 0.830 | 0.000 |
| PCP4DCP4| 0.832 | 0.000 |

title: [Bugfix][Model][Spec Decode] Defer disposable GLM MTP head
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

- defer the GLM MTP `ParallelLMHead` that `load_eagle_model()` replaces with the target model's head
- keep `SharedHead`'s default behavior unchanged for other MTP models
- verify the quantized placeholder is not allocated

GLM MTP constructs a per-layer `ParallelLMHead` that `load_eagle_model()` replaces with the target model's head. That temporary head caused the load-time memory peak this PR originally addressed. #52501 subsequently initialized unloaded ModelOpt NVFP4 `weight_scale` parameters to a NaN sentinel and added a check that rejects an unoverwritten sentinel during quantization processing. Because the disposable head has no checkpoint scales to load, draft loading now fails inside `get_model()`, before `load_eagle_model()` can replace it.

Fixes #57532.

### Summary

Since #52501 (merged 2026-09-13) GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 cannot be served with MTP on `main`.
The engine fails while loading the draft model:

title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Run the dense MLP layers on the sequence-parallel shard
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash served with DP > 1, TP > 1 and `--enable-expert-parallel` (the configuration that turns on `use_sequence_parallel_moe`) sporadically emits a wrong first token, stray `</think>` tokens followed by a repeated reasoning block, and occasionally byte garbage such as `ԥԥԥԥ� Canadian French, ԥԥ�1ԥ…`. DP with TP=1 and TP-only serving are clean.

`Glm5NextModel` follows the DeepSeek-V4 sequence-parallel layout: the token dimension is sharded across the TP group once at the model entry (`sp_shard`) and every layer runs its mHC and MLP on that shard, gathering only for attention. Every non-MoE module on the shard therefore has to be sequence-parallel aware. The dense MLP of the first `first_k_dense_replace` (3) layers was still constructed as a standard TP MLP, so its `down_proj` all-reduce summed the partial outputs of *different* tokens held by the two TP ranks:

- multi-token batches (prefill, concurrent decode): rows of the first three layers are mixed pairwise, hence the wrong first token / garbage under load;
- single-token decode: the peer rank holds a zero padding row, so the real token only loses half of the intermediate dimension, which is why the model still looked mostly coherent and the bug went unnoticed.

The shared experts already pass `is_sequence_parallel` (replicated weights, `disable_tp`, no collective). This PR passes the same flag to the dense `Glm5NextMLP` and adds a unit test for the layout. TP-only and DP-with-TP1 deployments do not enter this branch and are unchanged.

Related but different: #50154 describes a sequence-parallel bug in the `deepseek_v2` path (GLM-5.2), where the SP boundary sits inside the MoE block; glm5next shards the whole model, so the fix lives in the dense layer construction instead.

## Test Plan

title: [Model] Add ZEDA-GLM-4.7-Flash-Dynamic (Glm4MoeLitePlusPlus) support
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose
Adds support for **ZEDA-GLM-4.7-Flash-Dynamic** (`Glm4MoeLitePlusPlusForCausalLM`), a dynamic MoE variant of GLM-4.7-Flash that introduces **Zero-Compute Experts (ZCE)**: the router gate emits logits for all experts (n_routed_experts + sum(zce_nums) = 64 + 32 = 96), but zero-compute expert slots are not executed as FFNs — they are remapped to expert 0 with weight 0 at the fused-MoE kernel level, avoiding a per-expert Python loop and keeping the whole path graph-compilable.

The vLLM side only makes vLLM **recognize** the model and **recreate the 96-dim gate**; the actual "skip" of zero-compute experts is handled by the companion vllm-ascend patch.

- The model uses sigmoid + `e_score_correction_bias` + group topk routing, so the gate **must** output 96 logits for topk selection to "see" the zero-compute slots. Keeping the inherited 64-dim gate makes ZCE routing silently inactive.
- The model uses DeepSeek-style **MLA**, so it must be added to the `is_deepseek_mla()` whitelist, otherwise it falls back to plain MHA and errors with `rotary 102 != 64`.
- Config is registered in `_CONFIG_REGISTRY` so the checkpoint loads **without `trust_remote_code`** (no need for a forked transformers).

New files:
- `vllm/model_executor/models/glm4_moe_lite_plus_plus.py` — thin override of `Glm4MoeLite`:
  - `Glm4MoeLitePlusPlusDecoderLayer`: after the parent builds the standard MoE layer, recreates `mlp.gate` as a `total_num_experts`-dim `nn.Linear`, creates a matching `e_score_correction_bias` Parameter, and sets `routed_experts.zero_expert_num` / `zero_expert_type` for the downstream fused-MoE kernel. title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Reuse decode topk global indices across consumer layers
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

On DeepSeek-V4.1, every compressed attention layer maps its index source's local top-k indices to global KV-cache slots on its own (`compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens`), although the indices and the block table are shared by every layer below the same index source. DSv4.1-Flash has 38 compressed layers reading 8 index sources, so one decode step launches the kernel 38 times for 8 distinct results — inside the target CUDA graph, ~2.2 µs of GPU time each (launch-bound, a few GB/s at decode shapes). A torch-profiler trace of bs=1 DSpark decode on 4×GB200 (TP4) shows 38× `_compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens_kernel` per step, 84 µs of GPU timeline.

## Change

Build the mapping once per (index source, compress ratio) and let the layers below read through (+53/−45 in `vllm/`, no kernel change):

- `DeepseekSparseSWAMetadata` gains `decode_global_topk_cache`, cleared alongside the existing per-step FlashInfer cache in `update_draft_decode_metadata`.
- `DeepseekV4Attention._decode_global_topk` fills that cache; the FlashMLA, mega-attention and FlashInfer SM120 decode paths call it instead of the kernel.
- The SM100 FlashInfer mixed sparse indices, already cached for SWA-only layers, now cache compressed layers under `c{ratio}a:{index source}` — the same shape the DSv4 backend uses (`swa_only` / `c128a`).
- Output-neutral by construction: consumers receive the very tensors the first layer of the step built.

Not a duplicate: #57434 does this for the ROCm backend only (`deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py`, ragged form) and leaves the NVIDIA paths untouched; #49678 is the same idea for GLM-5.2 in `v1/attention/backends/mla`; #41105 (draft) fuses the mapping into the DSv4 top-k kernel and keeps the per-layer recompute. Dup checks on 2026-09-19: `topk metadata across layers`, `reuse global topk indices`, `compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens`, `57434 in:body`. Orthogonal to #55744 / #55692 (kernel bounds fixes in `deepseek_v4/`).

## Summary

Port `vllm bench serve`'s timed-trace replay to the Rust `vllm-bench` client: the `timed_trace` dataset (Mooncake-style JSONL: `{timestamp, input_length, output_length, hash_ids}`) and `--self-timed` scheduling, so recorded request-arrival schedules can be replayed faithfully from Rust. ```bash
vllm-bench \

  --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --model glm-5.2-fp8 --tokenizer <tokenizer path> \

  --dataset-path trace.jsonl \
  --self-timed \
  --timed-trace-chunk-hash-size 16 \
  --timed-trace-sec-multiplier 0.001 \

Replays the shape of the traffic, not its content: arrival schedule, ISL/OSL, and prefix-sharing structure are preserved; prompt tokens are synthetic. Completions endpoint only. Complementary to #51104, which covers multi-turn HF datasets and intentionally excludes trace replay.

title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Keep batch x heads out of gridDim.z in the GLM-5.3-Flash fused recurrent KDA kernel
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix a start-up crash of GLM-5.3-Flash in data-parallel deployments (TP=1 per rank): `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel` was launched with `grid = (NK, NV, N * HV)`, and with 64 KDA value heads on one GPU the first CUDA-graph capture batch of 1024 sequences needs `1024 * 64 = 65536` programs — one over the CUDA `gridDim.z` limit of 65535 — so the launch fails with `Triton Error [CUDA]: invalid argument` and `--data-parallel-size 4` (with or without EP) cannot start. TP4 (16 heads per rank) is unaffected.

The kernel now carries `N * HV` in `gridDim.x` (limit 2^31-1) with the `program_id` mapping swapped accordingly. Scope (narrowed in review): only the NVIDIA GLM-5.3-Flash copy under `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/third_party/kda/` (`kernels.py`, `fused_recurrent.py`) and its test are changed. The same `grid = (NK, NV, N * HV)` pattern exists in the AMD GLM copy and in `third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/{fused_recurrent,fused_sigmoid_gating,kda}.py`; those are intentionally left unchanged here (no AMD reproduction available; the shared kernels serve other models and need their own validation) and are candidates for separate follow-up. The packed-decode kernel in the same GLM file already guarded this case (`split_batch_head_grid = B * HV > 65535`). The narrowed change serves every GLM-5.3-Flash TP configuration; the failure itself needs TP=1 per rank (DP) at the default capture sizes.

Fixes #56973

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Searched vllm-project/vllm open and closed PRs and issues (GitHub search, 2026-09-13 and 2026-09-15) for `fused_recurrent_kda`, `gridDim.z`, `65535`, `invalid argument` + GLM-5.3-Flash / KDA / DP: no report of this crash and no PR touching the launch grid of `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel`; the only related guard is the existing `split_batch_head_grid` check in the packed-decode kernel of the same file.

title: [Spec Decode] Enable GLM-5.2 DSpark under pipeline parallelism
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

Enable GLM-5.2 (`DeepseekV32ForCausalLM`) to support DSpark speculative
decoding under pipeline parallelism by extending the community #50514
`relay_aux_hidden_states` mechanism to the DeepSeek-V3.2 backbone.

## Motivation

#50514 introduced `supports_aux_hidden_states_over_pp` and the
`relay_aux_hidden_states` / `pack_local_aux_hidden_states` /
`collect_remote_aux_hidden_states` family to carry DSpark/EAGLE-3 aux
hidden states across PP stages. This covers DeepSeek-V4, Kimi-K3, Llama,
and Qwen2.

GLM-5.2 reuses the DeepSeek-V3.2 (`deepseek_v32`) backbone but does not
set `supports_aux_hidden_states_over_pp`, so DSpark under PP cannot relay
aux hidden states across stages — `collect_remote_aux_hidden_states`
returns `[]` and the draft never sees upstream aux. This PR fills that
gap.

## Modifications

All changes are in `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/nvidia/model.py` (+16, -5):

1. **Inherit `EagleModelMixin`**: `DeepseekV32Model` now inherits
   `EagleModelMixin` and sets `supports_aux_hidden_states_over_pp = True`,
   enabling the #50514 relay path for GLM-5.2.

2. **Fix `set_aux_hidden_state_layers` bypass**: The parent
   `DeepseekV2ForCausalLM.set_aux_hidden_state_layers` directly assigns
   `self.model.aux_hidden_state_layers = layers`, bypassing
   `EagleModelMixin._set_aux_hidden_state_layers` and leaving
   `_aux_slot_base_cached` at 0. This breaks
   `collect_remote_aux_hidden_states`. Override to call

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Cap the DynamicVideoBackend sampling fps
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`DynamicVideoBackend` (`vllm/multimodal/video.py`, registered as `opencv_dynamic`)
sizes its frame-candidate walk directly from the request-supplied `fps`, so the
amount of work is unbounded by anything in the video:

```python
fps = target.fps
...
if duration <= max_duration:
    n = int(math.floor(duration * fps))
    frame_indices_list = sorted(
        {min(max_frame_idx, math.ceil(i / fps * original_fps)) for i in range(n)}
    )
```

`n` scales with `fps`, but the *result* does not: the largest index reachable is
`duration * original_fps` regardless, and the set deduplicates at the end. So a
large `fps` buys nothing and costs CPU linearly.

This applies the same clamp the sibling backends in this file already use —
`_MAX_FPS: ClassVar[int] = 30` plus `fps = min(target.fps, cls._MAX_FPS)`, which
is verbatim what `QwenVLVideoBackend` (`:362`/`:373`, from the merged #56729) and
`GLMGAVideoBackend` (`:812`/`:839`) do.

## Reachability

`fps` is request-controlled through `media_io_kwargs`, and nothing strips it for
this backend:

1. `opencv_dynamic` is registered with `video_processor="Glm4vVideoProcessor"`,
   so it is the **default** backend on GLM-4V-family servers — a plain
   `POST /v1/chat/completions` with
   `"media_io_kwargs": {"video": {"fps": 100000}}` is enough, no override needed.
2. It registers with the default `requires_gpu=False`, so
   `VideoMediaIO.merge_kwargs` (`vllm/multimodal/media/video.py:60`) does **not**
   strip a request-level `video_backend: "opencv_dynamic"` either. The remaining
   `merge_kwargs` handling forwards `fps` verbatim.
3. It is also selected explicitly at
   `vllm/model_executor/models/nano_nemotron_vl.py:830`.

Only the `duration <= max_duration` branch is exposed. The `else` branch
self-bounds: `num_samples >= total_frames_num` short-circuits, and otherwise
`num_samples < total_frames_num`.

## Measured cost

Measured on a verbatim extraction of the function body (pure Python/numpy, so
the walk cost is real)

title: [Bugfix] Pin num_splits for the FA4 hd256 kernel in sparse MLA
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`SparseMLAAttention._run_masked_mha` calls `flash_attn_varlen_func` with `fa_version=4` but never pins `num_splits`. On Blackwell (SM100/SM110) with `head_size == head_size_v == 256`, FA4 dispatches its dedicated hd256 kernel, which asserts `not is_split_kv`. Once the batch is large enough for the split-KV heuristic to fire, that assertion trips and takes down the engine core.

This affects `glm_moe_dsa` models (GLM-5.2 / GLM-5.3 family), whose `v_head_dim` is 256.

## Symptom

```
assert not is_split_kv, "SM100 forward with head_dim=256 does not support SplitKV"
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed / engine core proc died
```

Reproduced on 4x B200 (TP=4), `max_model_len 32768`, GLM-5.2 NVFP4: serving is stable at low load and the engine dies once concurrency reaches roughly 32. Below that threshold the heuristic does not split, which is why this does not show up in small smoke tests.

## Root cause

The dense FA path already knows this kernel cannot split — `uses_fa4_hd256_kernel` exists in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/fa_utils.py` and is consulted in `flash_attn.py`. The sparse MLA call site is the one place that builds FA4 kwargs for the same kernel without the corresponding guard.

## Fix

Pin `num_splits = 1` when the hd256 kernel is in play, reusing the existing helper rather than hardcoding the head size:

```python
if uses_fa4_hd256_kernel(q.shape[-1], v.shape[-1]):
    kwargs["num_splits"] = 1
```

The helper already checks the device capability (major in `(10, 11)`), so this is a no-op on every other platform and on every other head size. No behaviour change outside the configuration that currently crashes.

## Test

Verified on `v0.29.0` with the equivalent guard applied to the same call site: the engine survives a concurrency sweep of 8 / 32 / 64 / 128 / 256 with zero failed requests, where the unpatched build dies at 32. The change in this PR is rebased onto `main` and switched to the existing helper; I do not have a Blackwell box

## Problem

  GLM-5.3-Flash already supports prefix caching. However, in

title: [Core][DP] Result-metric penalties and superlinear in-flight in DP lo…
bodyExcerpt:
## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Upstream survey (as of 2026-09):

- PR #47420 (rotating tie-break) and #49204 (stats publishing + in-flight floor) are already merged and are ** prerequisites this patch builds on**; they do not address the linear in-flight overtaking a frozen snapshot score mid-burst.
- PR #40795 (open, unmerged) extends scores with waiting/running **token counts** — orthogonal to this change, which adds **result metrics** (queue-wait, preemption rate) to the routing signal. No open PR or issue covers result-metric-driven DP routing.

## Problem (production evidence)

The internal DP load balancer (`DPLBAsyncMPClient`) balances on request counts only. Two failure modes were observed in production (DP=2, Ascend 910B3, Qwen3.5-27B / GLM-5.1-w4a8):

1. **Mid-flight inversion.** Decomposing the 100ms snapshot window shows `engine_inflight` is the only real-time quantity — it can grow ~155x while an overloaded engine's snapshot score stays frozen. The linear term `client_count * inflight` lets a healthy engine overtake the overloaded engine's score at only ~30 in-flight requests, so the LB keeps feeding the engine that is actively avalanching (TTFT gap 9x; KV usage 8% vs 92%, preempts 12 vs 0).
2. **Result metrics are absent.** Queue wait and preemption — the strongest overload signals — play no part in routing.

## What this PR does

Gated by `VLLM_DP_LB_RESULT_METRICS` (default **on**; setting `0` restores the exact pre-patch behavior — verified by regression tests):

### 1. Snapshot extension (3-tuple → 5-tuple)

- `SchedulerStats` gains two optional fields with defaults: `mean_queue_time` (average seconds queued requests have waited — an engine-side TTFT proxy: queued wait accrues directly into future TTFT) and `preempted_total` (cumulative preemption count). All existing constructors keep working.
