title: [Perf][Hybrid] Reserve Mamba speculative-decoding scratch per running request instead of per KV-concurrency slot
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

For a hybrid (Mamba / linear-attention) model with speculative decoding, `MambaSpec.max_memory_usage_bytes` charges each request `num_speculative_blocks` extra state pages per Mamba group. In `align` mode:

```python
return self.page_size_bytes * (
    2 + self.num_speculative_blocks + self.num_prefill_checkpoint_blocks
)
```

`get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config` then divides the whole block pool by that per-request footprint — so the drafting scratch is reserved **once per KV-concurrency slot**.

But scratch is not a per-request resident working set. `MambaManager` allocates it once, when a request first gets blocks, relocates it in place every step (`_relocate_speculative_block` moves the block within the request's block list rather than allocating a new one), and frees it with the request. Only a *running* request drafts, so at most `max_num_seqs` copies of the scratch exist at any instant — no matter how many requests the pool could hold.

On GLM-5.3-Flash at TP4 with MTP `num_speculative_tokens=3` (34 KDA linear-attention layers in 3 Mamba groups + 12 MLA groups), the per-request charge is 45 blocks, of which **9 are Mamba speculative scratch**, and that 9 was being multiplied by 19.4 concurrency slots although only 8 requests can ever speculate at once.

### The change

* New `KVCacheSpec.speculative_scratch_bytes(vllm_config)`, returning `0` by default. `MambaSpec` returns `page_size_bytes * num_speculative_blocks`; `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` aggregates it the same way it aggregates `max_memory_usage_bytes`.
* New helper `_pool_concurrency_limit(num_blocks, blocks_per_request, scratch_per_request, max_num_seqs)`: reserve `max_num_seqs * scratch_per_request` blocks **once**, then divide the remainder by the scratch-free per-request cost.
* Below the crossover — when the pool holds fewer than `max_num_seqs` requests — every resident request may also be running, so the old formula is kept. The two branches agree exactly at `all_running == max_num

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Fixed-width sparse indexer prefill logits so long prefills reuse allocator blocks (#55569)
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55569. Related: #56457 reports the same allocation pattern in the Qwen4Exp QSA indexer, with fixes proposed for that path in #56500 and #57105 (both open); #55572 (closed) lowered the default logits budget on integrated GPUs instead.

The dense sparse-MLA indexer (`sparse_attn_indexer.py`, and the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool variant under `models/glm5next`) scores each prefill chunk with DeepGEMM's `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits`, which allocates its `[M, N]` fp32 logits inside the C++ API. `N` is the request's compressed context so far, so every chunk of a long prefill asks for a tensor of a new, larger size: one launch per chunk of growing size while `M * N * 4` fits the `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` budget (512 MiB), and, once a chunk exceeds it (about 116k tokens at a 4,608-token chunk with kpool 4), several launches per chunk that are all close to the budget but never the same size twice. PyTorch's caching allocator serves a request from a cached block only if it fits, and returns segments to the driver only on `empty_cache` or an OOM-time release, so once the free space that happens to be around is used up, each chunk step adds a new segment for the rest of the prefill. On a discrete GPU this is reserved-but-idle memory; on unified-memory devices (DGX Spark / GB10) it comes out of the host's share, and the driver-level failure (`NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY`) arrives before the allocator's OOM retry can help, ending in the swap storms reported in #55569.

**Change.** Allocate the logits at a fixed width instead of the chunk's kv length, using the `max_seqlen_k` argument DeepGEMM already provides: the kernel still computes only `[cu_seqlen_ks, cu_seqlen_ke)` per row, `max_seqlen_k` is only the allocation stride, and DeepGEMM asserts `clean_logits=False` with it (verified at vLLM's pinned commit). title: [Perf][HiSparse] Avoid repeated prefix scans and residency updates
bodyExcerpt:
HiSparse's scheduler rescans the entire computed prefix on every materialization call, including pages already known to be durable. Each resident cache group also invokes the same shared materialization and residency operations. With 20 resident groups and hundreds of requests per rank, this consumed most of a scheduler CPU core and delayed workers before their DP collective.

This patch starts scanning at `max(ready_prefix_pages, importing_pages)` and invokes the shared operations only from the first resident manager. It preserves pending-write checks, holes beyond the durable prefix, spill budgets, import completion, and publication ordering. No serving configuration, routing, graph policy, or model math changes are included.

Two existing materialization tests now exercise both one and three resident groups, covering incomplete/out-of-order writes and per-step spill budgets.

### Performance evidence

B300, one EP8 prefill node and one EP8 decode node, 2,048-concurrent Scale-SWE agentic rollouts. GLM-5.3 NVFP4 (`RadixArk/GLM-5.3-NVFP4`, revision `11af4cba759e6559eda70358a5778bd1bddddd78`), FP8 KV, HiSparse 300 GiB/decode GPU, index cache, NIXL and Mooncake, Rust frontend, natural routing. Decode used DeepEP LL and FULL_AND_PIECEWISE breakable graphs; EPLB, DBO and speculative decoding were disabled.

The same loaded deployment switched between the original implementation, cursor only, and the full fix. No reload, cache reset, eval restart, or serving-configuration change occurred between phases. The first 30 seconds of each phase are excluded.

title: [Bugfix] Make disable_any_whitespace actually disable whitespace on xgrammar
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`disable_any_whitespace` does not disable whitespace on the xgrammar backend — it **makes whitespace mandatory**, and as a side effect masks out the token the model wants at every JSON value position.

xgrammar's `any_whitespace=False` selects a *fixed* JSON format rather than a whitespace-free one. Its docstring is explicit that the format follows `json.dumps()` conventions, and with `separators` left unset the default is `(", ", ": ")` — *with* spaces. `backend_xgrammar.py` never passes `separators`, so today the flag requires a space after every comma and colon.

The second-order effect is the damaging one. Because the space is mandatory, the bare `"` that opens a string value becomes illegal at the value position. Measured on the mask with a real GLM-5.3 tokenizer, immediately after `{"location":`:

| grammar config | allowed tokens | whitespace-leading | bare `"` | digit-leading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `any_whitespace=True` | 1450 | 719 | yes | 395 |
| `any_whitespace=False`, default separators — **today** | 268 | **268, all of them** | **banned** | 0 |
| `any_whitespace=False`, `separators=(",", ":")` — **this PR** | 703 | **0** | yes | 395 |

The middle row is what vLLM produces now: every legal continuation begins with a space. A model prompted for minified JSON wants the bare `"`; with it masked out, probability mass shifts to the whitespace-prefixed set, where `␣0`, `␣1`, `␣-` compete with `␣"`.

On a production GLM-5.3 deployment this corrupted **26.5%** of `response_format: {"type":"json_object"}` responses, returning a number where the first string value belonged:

```
{"location": 2,      "conditions": "cloudy", ...}
{"location": 0.2373, "temperature": 12, ...}
{"location": 0,      "temperature": 0, ... "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"}
```

Nothing errors — `finish_reason` and `usage` are normal, so the caller simply receives wrong types.

It is worth noting `json_schema` requests with typed properties were unaffected: a strict schema leaves only

title: [Bug]: keep-mode pause stops pending KV receive polling with HiSparse/NIXL
bodyExcerpt:
`pause_generation(mode="keep")` can stop decode-side KV completion polling before asynchronous receives finish. With HiSparse mixed DRAM/VRAM NIXL reads, this also prevents the decode worker from sending completion notifications to prefill, leaving prefill waiting for remote cleanup during its own pause.

The deployment that exposed this uses GLM-5.3, B300, DP/EP=8 per replica, NIXL P/D, HiSparse on decode, and MooncakeStore through MultiConnector. This was investigated on a patched v0.28.1 development runtime; the scheduler condition below is also present on main at `0bce411a`. A live patched restart is in progress; we do not yet have an end-to-end pause-time result.

### Confirmed mechanism

1. D has a request in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`, in `waiting` or `skipped_waiting`.
2. `pause(mode="keep")` sets `PAUSED_ALL`. `get_num_unfinished_requests()` returns zero; the waiting receive does not count as a finished request retained for cleanup either. With no other work, `Scheduler.has_requests()` returns false.
3. The engine stops issuing zero-token connector steps.
4. Mixed-memory NIXL reads create multiple transfer handles without `notif_msg`, then record `_pending_recv_notifs`. `get_transfer_results()` sends those notifications only after polling all handles complete.
5. Even completed transport handles therefore do not notify P if D stops polling. P can remain active solely to wait for delayed connector frees.

This differs from the ordinary NIXL READ path in v0.27, where `make_prepped_xfer(..., notif_msg=...)` attaches the notification to the transport. Mixed-memory software notification bookkeeping was introduced by #53780 and is exercised by the HiSparse path. The scheduler's delayed-free gate itself predates v0.27; it is not a newly introduced change.

title: [Kernel] persistent_topk: deterministic select, faster than the exact-topk workaround
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

A deterministic `persistent_topk` (the QSA / sparse-indexer block selection,
`csrc/libtorch_stable/persistent_topk.cuh`) that is **also faster than the exact-topk workaround**
people currently reach for. The kernel returns a different result for identical inputs from call to
call: the **order** always varies, and when more keys share the threshold value than the candidate
buffers hold, the selected **set** varies too. Cause: output slots are handed out by `atomicAdd` in
thread-arrival order, and exact-key ties at the last radix round are taken first-come.

### Motivation update (2026-09-21) — read this before the original framing below

This PR was opened as a determinism fix. **On the evidence since, that framing overstates the
case, and I am restating it rather than leaving the body arguing something the threads have
undermined.** Three independent readings:

1. **Ours.** We censused the top-k boundary on real traffic: **0 ties at the k-th value across 6,192
   selecting rows** at 16k context ([09-12](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55122#issuecomment-5602743511)).
   93 % of rows had fewer visible blocks than k, so selection was a no-op.
2. **The reporter of #51782.** @xueyangcs states the HPC-Ops TopK contract is **set-exact only** —
   with ties, any valid top-k set is permitted; set-stability was never guaranteed
   ([#51782, 09-09](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51782)).
3. **An independent field report.** @NNNtrance replaced the selection with an exact `torch.topk` on
   GLM-5.3-Flash across three DGX Sparks and got **9/6 bad turns vs 11/7 stock — within noise**,
   while `index_topk 8192` gives 2/3. Selection accuracy was not their cause
   ([#51782, 09-12](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51782)).

So **the tie-ordering defect is real at the kernel level but does not appear to be reachable on the
traffic that motivated it.** What survives is the performance argument, which is independently
measured: @k3dani fou

title: [Perf][Attention] Reduce GLM sparse MLA preparation overhead
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Reduce query packing and sparse-index preparation overhead around FlashInfer NoPE MLA attention.

The three commits:

1. Reuse a contiguous NoPE query when its rotary tail is empty, avoiding a redundant `torch.cat` before FP8 quantization. Preserve concatenation for nonempty rotary dimensions and strided queries.
2. Use one padded remap program per query for counted sparse capacities up to 4096. Initialize padding and reduce valid counts inside the remap kernel, removing separate fills and atomic accumulation. Preserve larger tiled cases and reusable buffers. Name the device entry point `sparse_mla_index_remap_kernel` for trace attribution.
3. Simplify empty-query handling: fuse dummy-entry preparation and safe-length calculation while preserving raw counts; skip preparation and masking for resident TP; mask only LSE for DCP and let its existing merge suppress zero-weight outputs, including NaNs. Preserve PyTorch output masking for HiSparse without LSE. There is no custom output-zeroing kernel.

Duplicate-work checks found no matching open PR. Related PRs #54258 (separate ROCm remap kernel), #38354 (DeepSeek pre-attention GEMM/RoPE fusion), and #57161 (GLM kpool/indexer scheduling) address different kernels or stages. No existing issue is being claimed or closed.

## Correctness

Prior TP validation on the experiment stack used GLM-5.3-Flash, TP8+EP8, all custom ops enabled, eager execution, no prefix cache, and exactly 32768 input tokens with either 1 or 16 generated tokens. Across 12 repeatability requests, all 8976 sparse-layer calls across eight ranks had positive valid counts (minimum 1). title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Support FP8 KV cache for NoPE sparse MLA
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

- route rope-free sparse MLA to the ROCm Triton implementation for every KV-cache dtype
- dequantize FP8 KV rows in the Triton ragged-prefill kernel using the layer KV scale while keeping Q in model dtype
- use 64-bit query-row offsets so wide, long-context prefills cannot overflow 32-bit pointer arithmetic
- preserve custom MLA geometry and FP8 cache dtype in the attention benchmark harness

## Problem

AITER precompiled sparse MLA kernels assume the DeepSeek cache-row geometry: 512 latent elements plus 64 RoPE elements. GLM-5.3-Flash is rope-free and stores a 512-element row. FP8 NoPE requests currently reach the AITER path, whose 576-element assumption can read past the cache row and cause a ROCm GPU memory fault.

The existing Triton ragged path already handles the NoPE geometry. This change makes its routing geometry-based instead of BF16-only, adds scaled FP8 KV dequantization, and avoids FP8-quantizing Q for that path.

## Duplicate-work check

No open PR found addresses ROCm NoPE FP8 sparse-attention KV rows. #39168 overlaps the ROCm ops file but changes the separate FP8 indexer-cache MQA path; the open GLM-5.3 NoPE FP8 PRs target NVIDIA backends. The previously bundled SharedTopkIndicesBuffer no-op was dropped because #57252 already landed ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl.record_logical_topk_ready().

## Validation

Rebased onto main@63d9ad0a. Head: ae5cad3d.

Hardware validation used a full ROCm wheel from the previous head (73860da5) on the GLM-5.3-specific ROCm base image. The rebase kept the same kernel/backend/benchmark hunks and only resolved a header-constant conflict with the new upstream FP8_DTYPE plus dropped the now-redundant top-k no-op.

- pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_glm5next_sparse.py: **23 passed** on the pre-rebase validated image

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Auto-enable fp32 weights for the gfx950 router GEMM in GateLinear
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55351. The gfx950 low-M FP32 router GEMM added in #54845 never runs: `GateLinear` call sites (deepseek_v2, glm5next, deepseek_v4 nvidia/amd/cpu/xpu) pass the router dtype as `out_dtype` only, so the gate weight stays in the model dtype (bf16) and `allow_fp32_router_gemm` — which requires `self.weight.dtype == torch.float32` — is never true. The kernel is unreachable for the exact shapes it was instantiated for, e.g. DeepSeek-family `(6144, 256)`.

## Approach

Rather than updating every call site to pass `force_fp32_compute` (only nemotron_h does today), self-enable inside `GateLinear`: when `is_gfx950 and (input_size, output_size) in ROCM_FP32_ROUTER_GEMM_SUPPORTED_SHAPES and not bias`, set `force_fp32_compute = True` so the existing logic stores fp32 weights. One-site fix; the eligibility flags then light up through the normal path.

## What does NOT change

- CUDA paths (Hopper/Blackwell specialized kernels, bf16×bf16→fp32 epilogue): `is_gfx950` is false, guard inert.
- Unsupported shapes on gfx950 (e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash's `(4096, 288)`): `is_rocm_fp32_shape` false, clean fallback.
- Biased gates: guard excludes bias (kernel/torch.mm path has no bias term).

## Verification

No GPU locally, so verified by simulation of the exact decision tree in `GateLinear.__init__`:

| Case | weights | fp32 kernel |
|---|---|---|
| gfx950, (6144, 256), no bias (issue repro) | fp32 | **enabled** (was: unreachable) |
| gfx950, (4096, 288) (GLM-5.3-Flash) | bf16 | unchanged fallback |
| CUDA H100, (6144, 256) | bf16 | unchanged |
| gfx950, biased gate | bf16 | unchanged |

`tests/kernels/test_gate_linear_rocm_dispatch.py` covers these flags with mocked platforms but requires a CUDA-built torch to instantiate `nn.Linear`; happy to run it on a gfx950 box if CI doesn't pick it up.

title: [Spec Decode] GLM-5.3-Flash DFlash2 aux hidden-state capture
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Enable DFlash2 speculative decoding for GLM-5.3-Flash by implementing aux hidden-state capture on the target model. Related: #55423 (same goal, different aux-materialization path — see below; comment posted there with the structural analysis).

## Problem

#55423 materializes aux states as `hidden + residual`. GLM's mHC residual is a deferred-fusion structure: at each layer boundary the decoder holds a 4-tuple `(x, residual, post, comb)`, and the layer-k output is only completed by `MHCPostOp` (`mhc.py`), whose mixing weights live inside the `post/comb` tensors. A plain `hidden + residual` therefore captures an intermediate state, not the completed output of layer k that the draft was trained against. We believe this may explain the unisolated output divergence reported in #55423.

## Solution

Capture before layer k+1, materializing aux via `hc_post(x, residual, post, comb)` followed by `hc_contract` — structurally identical to the last-layer epilogue. KDA/non-mHC boundaries fall back to `hidden + residual`. Sequence-parallel gather skips the dense stages. The multimodal wrapper (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`, the architecture of the official `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` checkpoint) declares `SupportsEagle3` and delegates to the inner text model, so the protocol unpack through `language_model.model` works natively.

Semantics adapted from SGLang `xinyuan/glm-5.3-flash-support` (#36507/#36708), Apache-2.0.

## Test plan

- [x] New suite `tests/models/glm5next/test_dflash2_aux_capture.py` (9 passed, 2 GPU-gated skipped): bit-exact vs independently materialized fp64 reference, KDA/residual-None fallback, adjacent-boundary enumeration, capture-on/off return shapes, next-layer tuple purity, wrapper `supports_eagle3` flag
- [x] Regression: `tests/models/test_registry.py` (379 passed), glm5next registry imports, `test_dflash_causality.py` (13 passed), mhc kernel + transformer-utils glm5next suites — all green

title: [CPU] Add KDA backend for GLM5Next
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

This PR adds a correctness-first CPU execution path for GLM-5.3-Flash / GLM5Next KDA for #57346.

The path is deliberately feature-local:

```text
GLM5Next common KDA layer
  -> CPU platform dispatch
  -> CPU state helpers and causal convolution
  -> CPU KDA recurrence/chunk contract
  -> optional _C_AVX512 recurrent operator
```

It does not implement #57345 (CPU sparse MLA / KeyPool), Kimi K3 support, a generic GDN refactor, or a new GLM CPU model hierarchy. The two GLM5Next CPU PRs are intentionally separate so that KDA and sparse MLA can be reviewed and tested independently.

## Self-review / Implementation notes

### Scope and design

The initial source audit showed that CPU support required more than changing the two KDA imports. The common layer also reaches causal-convolution and state gather/scatter boundaries that have GPU-oriented implementations. I therefore kept the change at the GLM5Next KDA execution boundary and preserved the existing common projection, metadata, and routing code.

I did not add `glm5next/cpu/model.py` or a new backend registry. The hardware-specific difference is limited to KDA execution, so a model-level fork would add review and maintenance cost without solving a concrete blocker.

The related CPU GDN implementation was used as a reference for stateful CPU integration, but it was not treated as a drop-in KDA implementation. KDA differs in safe-gate semantics, beta handling, V-major state layout, and speculative state routing.

### KDA semantics preserved

The CPU backend keeps the existing GLM KDA contract:

* q/k normalization and query scaling;
* bounded safe gate using per-head `A_log` and per-head/key-dimension `g_bias`;
* V-major recurrent state `[slots, heads, V, K]`;
* separate chunk-prefill and recurrent-decode state semantics;
* chunk beta timing versus recurrent sigmoid-beta handling;
* 1-D ordinary decode slots and 2-D speculative accepted-token slots;
* NULL-slot skipping and in-place state writeback.

bodyExcerpt:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
PLEASE FILL IN THE PR DESCRIPTION HERE ENSURING ALL CHECKLIST ITEMS (AT THE BOTTOM) HAVE BEEN CONSIDERED.

## Purpose

Adds support for **ZEDA-GLM-4.7-Flash-Dynamic** (`Glm4MoeLitePlusPlusForCausalLM`), a dynamic MoE variant of GLM-4.7-Flash that introduces **Zero-Compute Experts (ZCE)**: the router gate emits logits for all experts (n_routed_experts + sum(zce_nums) = 64 + 32 = 96), but zero-compute expert slots are not executed as FFNs — they are remapped to expert 0 with weight 0 at the fused-MoE kernel level, avoiding a per-expert Python loop and keeping the whole path graph-compilable.

The vLLM side only makes vLLM **recognize** the model and **recreate the 96-dim gate**; the actual "skip" of zero-compute experts is handled by the companion vllm-ascend patch.

**Why:**

- The model uses sigmoid + `e_score_correction_bias` + group topk routing, so the gate **must** output 96 logits for topk selection to "see" the zero-compute slots. Keeping the inherited 64-dim gate makes ZCE routing silently inactive.
- The model uses DeepSeek-style **MLA**, so it must be added to the `is_deepseek_mla()` whitelist, otherwise it falls back to plain MHA and errors with `rotary 102 != 64`.
- Config is registered in `_CONFIG_REGISTRY` so the checkpoint loads **without `trust_remote_code`** (no need for a forked transformers).
- The 96-dim `e_score_correction_bias` must be synced onto the **router** as well as the gate/experts, otherwise the Ascend `moe_gating_top_k` C++ kernel fails its dimension check (`bias_size[0] != expert_num`).

**Changes (6 files, +249 lines):**

New files:
- `vllm/model_executor/models/glm4_moe_lite_plus_plus.py` — thin override of `Glm4MoeLite`:

title: [GLM-5.3-Flash] Rework kpool compress and dual-stream indexer scheduling
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Supplements vLLM's `Glm5Next` sparse-MLA kpool indexer with the kpool optimizations

What changes in vLLM:

- `vllm/models/glm5next/{nvidia,amd}/ops/kpool_compress.py`: `_kpool_softmax_rotate_write_cache_kernel` switches from a two-pass to an **online softmax** (each pool's gate scores are read once instead of twice) and takes a (row stride, slot stride, row offset) triple so one kernel serves both the pooled `[n_pools, kpool, D]` layout (`row_offset = 0`) and the **flat token layout** (`row_offset = kpool - 1`: row `i` pools tokens `i - kpool + 1 .. i`, SGLang's "assemble" kernel shape). Rows whose slot is negative, or too early in the batch to own a full pool, return before any load — replacing the `write_mask` mechanism. The prefill and decode kernels share one `_hadamard_quantize_fp8` helper; the decode/verify kernel also uses the online softmax (matching SGLang's verify-side kernel).
- `vllm/models/glm5next/{nvidia,amd}/sparse_indexer.py`: the prefill insert becomes a single launch of the new `kpool_compress_tokens_and_write_cache` on the prefill slice (was: `arange`/`clamp`/`>=`/`&`/index tensors + `k[idx]`/`gate_score[idx]` gathers + int64 conversion = 12 launches per indexer layer per prefill step). title: [Attention][MLA] fp8_ds_mla for rope-free NoPE models (head_dim 512) on SM90 via zero-padded-rope envelope
bodyExcerpt:
## 🚀 Description

Enables `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache for rope-free NoPE sparse-MLA models (`qk_rope_head_dim=0`, head_dim 512, e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash) on **SM90/Hopper** via the FlashMLA sparse backend, served through a zero-padded 576/656B envelope.

Today on H200, GLM-5.3-Flash must either use bf16 KV (~2x memory) or the plain per-tensor-fp8 `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` backend, which returns no LSE and therefore cannot run DCP (decode context parallel) or compose with the MTP fused-draft path. The only SM90 sparse-MLA backend with `fp8_ds_mla` support (`FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, #47090) hard-rejects head_dim 512 because the FlashMLA kernels assume the fixed 576 geometry.

**Approach**: keep the 656B packed row layout unchanged and zero-pad the rope section:
- The rope bytes [640:768] of every cached token are written as bf16 zeros, and the query-side `q_pe` is zero-padded to 64 dims. Since RoPE is baked into the cache at write time, `q_pe · 0 = 0` exactly in IEEE arithmetic — the padding contributes nothing to any logit. This was verified end-to-end with a standalone kernel probe on H20 (SM90): output rel-err vs a bf16 NoPE-512 reference matches the fp8 block-quant noise floor (~2.5e-2), and a garbage-rope control diverges, proving the test has teeth.
- `FLASHMLA_SPARSE.get_supported_head_sizes()` → `[576, 512]`; `supports_combination` accepts 512 **only** for quantized DS-MLA dtypes (`fp8_ds_mla`/`nvfp4_ds_mla`), so bf16 NoPE-512 traffic keeps flowing to the FlashInfer/TRITON backends.
- A shared helper in `mla_attention.py` promotes the rope dims of rope-free MLA layers to the padded 576 geometry when the effective KV dtype is quantized DS-MLA on `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, emitting persistent zero buffers (CUDA-graph capture stable). Models with rope dims > 0 are untouched.
- `SparseMLACommonMetadataBuilder` now derives its MLA dims from the instantiated runtime layers instead of the raw HF config, so the chunked-prefill workspace is sized from the promoted (576) geometry — without th

```

`_run_flashinfer_autotune_dummy_runs()` → the fp8 sparse decode kernel.

title: [Bugfix] Fix Whisper engine crash on audio clips longer than 30s
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Offline `LLM.generate` with Whisper and an audio clip longer than 30 s kills the engine on main and on v0.29.0:

```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (1750) must match the size of tensor b (1500) at non-singleton dimension 0
```

Every later request then fails with `EngineDeadError`. v0.26.0 accepts the same input and truncates the clip to 30 s, which is what the HF feature extractor does by default.

The cause is the same as in #56912 (Qwen2-Audio). Since #53275 the multimodal processor passes `truncation=False` to the HF processor so that the placeholder text is not cut. `WhisperProcessor` forwards the same kwarg to `WhisperFeatureExtractor`, which then stops truncating audio to its 30 s window. A 35 s clip becomes 3500 frames, which is 1750 positions after the conv, and the encoder has 1500.

The fix is the same line as in #56912: `WhisperMultiModalProcessor._get_hf_mm_inputs` passes `truncation=True`. Clips of up to 30 s are processed exactly as before.

`/v1/audio/transcriptions` and `/v1/audio/translations` are not affected, because the server splits audio into chunks of at most 30 s before it reaches the processor, and Whisper does not serve the other endpoints. Only offline use with a longer clip hits this.

I did not find an existing issue or PR for this (searched for whisper truncation, whisper 30s, and the error message). Of the other audio models I could load, GLM-ASR and Qwen3-ASR handle long clips correctly and Qwen2-Audio is already fixed. I have not checked the rest.

Repro:

```python
import numpy as np
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

sr = 16000
t = np.arange(sr * 35) / sr  # 35 s, longer than Whisper's 30 s window
audio = (0.1 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 440 * t)).astype(np.float32)

llm = LLM("openai/whisper-small", max_model_len=448, limit_mm_per_prompt={"audio": 1})
out = llm.generate(
    {
        "prompt": "<|startoftranscript|><|en|><|transcribe|><|notimestamps|>",
        "multi_modal_data": {"audio": (audio, sr)},
    },

title: feat(chat): support OpenAI 'file' content parts by inlining documents as text
bodyExcerpt:
## Motivation

OpenAI-compatible clients (e.g. coding agents) attach documents to chat messages as `file` content parts. Current `MM_PARSER_MAP` does not recognize `file`, so such requests fail with:

```
Unsupported chat content part type: 'file'. Supported types: ...
```

## Changes (`vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py`)

1. Add a `_parse_file_part` parser registered as `"file"` in `MM_PARSER_MAP`:
   - accepted payloads: `{type:"file", file:{file_name, file_data: <data URI>}}` and `{type:"file", data, mediaType}`
   - text-like files (txt/md/code/csv/json/yaml/xml/html/...) are inlined verbatim
   - PDF text is extracted via pymupdf, falling back to pypdf; scanned PDFs degrade to a notice
   - docx text is extracted from `word/document.xml`
   - undecodable binary payloads degrade to a notice string so the conversation continues instead of returning HTTP 400
2. Add `"file"` to the text-branch tuple in `_parse_chat_message_content_part`.

## Testing

- Offline parser test: text/plain data URI and a real PDF (pymupdf-generated) both inline correctly.
- Production smoke test (GLM-5.3-Flash-AWQ, TP4): `text`, `file` (txt), `file` (pdf) and `image_url` requests all return 200; PDF content QA answers correctly.

Same change also submitted to the vllm-backport fork: wtdcode/vllm-backport#95.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Stop dummy draft decode steps from writing KV through stale block-table rows
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix a KV-cache corruption in Model Runner V2 speculative decoding under data parallelism: an idle DP rank's dummy batch runs the drafter's multi-step decode, which computes real slot mappings through the *persistent* per-slot block tables using `idx_mapping = arange(num_reqs)` (real request-state slots whose rows are stale), and writes drafter-layer K/V into offsets `1..k-1` of the first block of whatever request last occupied those slots. Those blocks are typically already registered in the prefix cache, so every later request that hits them reads corrupted drafter K/V while the target model's K/V stays intact.

Observed on GLM-5.2 (glm_moe_dsa, MTP k=5, DP=4 EP, prefix caching) as a per-request, exactly-zero MTP acceptance (`p0 = 0.0000`, `acc_len = 1.0`, `drafts == max_tokens`) that latches onto a conversation and disappears after `POST /reset_prefix_cache`; the poisoned rows were NaN (fp8 `0x7F`) in `model.layers.78.self_attn.attn`, with the target layers and indexer cache of the same block clean. On current main the same stale write still happens on every idle step (the written values happen to be finite there, so acceptance is unaffected), i.e. the write path is latent.

#49757 protected the read side (`get_dummy_block_tables` zeroes `input_block_tables`) and the target's dummy slot mappings are PAD (`prepare_dummy_attn`), but `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` reads `block_table_ptrs` (the persistent tables), which neither protection covers.

## Fix

- `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel`: a row with `idx_mapping < 0` (dummy or CUDA-graph padding request) emits `PAD_SLOT_ID` and never dereferences a negative block-table row.
- `AutoRegressiveSpeculator.propose(dummy_run=True)`: mark every dummy row with `idx_mapping = -1` (already the speculator's convention for padded rows, ignored by `gumbel_sample`).

The guard lives in the kernel rather than in Python because the fused multi-step path re-runs `compute_slot_mappings` inside the captured CU
author: ivanium

title: [Bugfix][Determinism] Refuse batch-invariant mode on the sparse indexer
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` looks like it works on DSA / sparse-indexer models. It
does not: the indexer's top-k has no batch-invariant backend, so which keys a
row attends to can change with the rest of the batch.

Every path is batch-dependent:

| backend | what makes it batch-dependent |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` | switches kernels at `AUTO_COOPERATIVE_MAX_ROWS` (64) rows — `indexer_topk.py:_resolve_auto` |
| `per_row` | picks among three algorithms from the **padded column count**, i.e. the batch's longest sequence (`sampler.cu`, `kSortingAlgorithmThreshold` / `kSplitWorkThreshold`); on gfx950 it also splits a row across blocks by row count |
| `persistent` | sizes its cooperative launch from occupancy and the batch's max sequence length, and falls back to `per_row` when the launch does not fit (`topk.cu`) |
| `cooperative` | only applicable under the 64-row cap, so it is by definition batch-conditional |

None of this changes the logits. It changes tie-breaking and therefore the
selection — and a different sparse selection is a different forward pass, not a
rounding difference.

The failure mode is silent: output drifts with concurrency instead of raising,
which is exactly what #53257 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash non-deterministic at
temperature=0, rate scales with concurrency) and #54521 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
greedy decoding non-deterministic from `persistent_topk`) describe.

This PR refuses at construction, naming the batch-dependent inputs, instead of
serving results the flag promises are batch-invariant.

## Why this matters beyond a debug flag

The GLM-5 tech report attributes an RL training collapse to exactly this class
of mismatch: a non-deterministic sparse selection "caused drastic performance
degradation during RL after only a few steps, accompanied by a sharp drop in
entropy." Rollout/training mismatch in sparse selection is not cosmetic, and a
flag that claims to eliminate it while not doing so is worse than no flag.

title: [Bugfix][Reasoning] Split leaked GLM think blocks out of content when extraction is disabled
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #54744.

With `--reasoning-parser glm45`/`glm47`, passing `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}` (or `thinking: false`) disables the parser's reasoning extraction. For GLM-4.5/4.6 that is correct, because their templates honor the kwarg and the model emits no think block. GLM-5.3-family templates read neither kwarg, so the model thinks unconditionally, and the raw scratchpad plus a dangling `</think>` lands in `message.content`:

```json
{"role": "assistant", "content": "Simple question.</think>2 + 2 = **4**\n\n..."}
```

The fix is output-driven: when extraction was disabled but the output still carries a think block, split it with the thinking-armed engine config instead of passing it through. Tag-free output (a template that genuinely honored the switch) passes through byte-identically, so GLM-4.5/4.6 behavior is unchanged. The request-scoped engine keeps the unarmed config, so the streaming and id-space paths (`is_reasoning_end`, `extract_content_ids`) are untouched.

Scope boundary, stated plainly: the streaming path still cannot auto-detect this case, because by the time a dangling `</think>` arrives the scratchpad has already streamed. Auto-detection there would require buffering content for models that legitimately disabled thinking, which is worse than the leak. Operators hitting this should drop the ignored kwarg for GLM-5.3 deployments; the non-streaming leak this PR closes is the verified repro from the issue.

Relationship to existing work: #43728's alias work fixes models whose template reads one of the two kwarg names; it cannot cover GLM-5.3, which reads neither. #52410 is the same parser-template agreement class from the other direction.

## Test plan

`tests/reasoning/test_glm4_moe_reasoning_parser.py` gains three pins: kwarg-disabled with a dangling end tag (the leak shape, now split), kwarg-disabled with explicit tags, and kwarg-disabled tag-free pass-through (GLM-4.5/4.6 preserved). The tagged cases also assert the

title: [Bug]: minimax_m2 / glm47_moe / deepseek_v4 arg converters drop the last parameter when the model omits the closing tag (same class as #57699)
bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

- vLLM main (probed 2026-09-20; minimax_m2.py @ 24bfbd5d, deepseek_v4.py @ 39e33db7)
- Parser-only bug: reproduction needs no GPU, no model, no server.

### Describe the bug

#57699 describes a bug class for qwen3: when the model closes the tool call **without closing the last parameter tag**, the trailing value is dropped by the final (partial=False) conversion. #57707 fixes qwen3 only - but the same structure exists in three other converters, none of which are covered by that PR:

**1. minimax_m2 - vllm/parser/minimax_m2.py `_minimax_m2_arg_converter`**

`_PARAM_RE` only ends a value at the closing parameter tag or at the next parameter open tag. The trailing `_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE` extraction runs only under `if partial:`, so the final conversion drops the last parameter. With `stream_arg_deltas=True`, the streamed partial conversions have already emitted the value, and the flush at tool-call end produces a shorter JSON - the same client-visible divergence as #57699.

Model output:

```
<minimax:tool_call><invoke name="get_weather">
<parameter name="city">Seattle</parameter>
<parameter name="unit">celsius
</invoke></minimax:tool_call>
```

non-streaming: `arguments == {"city": "Seattle"}` - `unit` is silently lost.

**2. glm47_moe - vllm/parser/glm47_moe.py `_glm47_arg_converter`**

`_ARG_RE` requires the value close tag; the `_PARTIAL_ARG_RE` extraction is under `if partial:`. `stream_arg_deltas=True` is set. Same divergence: a tool call that omits the last closing arg_value tag yields non-streaming `arguments` without the trailing parameter.

**3. deepseek_v4 (inherited by v32/v41) - vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py `_dsml_arg_converter`**

Same `if partial:` structure. Additionally, the partial branch swallows JSON failures with `contextlib.suppress` and **drops the value entirely**, while the complete branch falls back to the literal text. title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Skip non-prefix-cacheable groups in SimpleCPUOffload (GLM-5.3-Flash kpool tail and QSA)
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash carries a kpool-tail scratch group (`KpoolTailSpec`, `prefix_cacheable=False`, `block_size=index_kpool=4`) next to prefix-cacheable groups that hash at 1152 tokens on this box (MLA 1152, 4× Mamba 1152 in `align` mode). Core (`resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes`, `HybridKVCacheCoordinator`, `KVCacheManager`) and the `MooncakeStore connector` already skip such groups. `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` did not, and treated every KV cache group as offloadable:

- `_select_eager_blocks_to_store` views the request hashes at each group's block size to build `BlockStored` metadata. For the tail group that is `resolve_block_hashes(hashes, hash_block_size=1152, block_size=4)`, which trips the divisibility assert as soon as `--kv-events-config` enables KV cache events. The engine dies on the first prefill store.
- `update_state_after_alloc` maps external (CPU-hit) tokens onto the scratch group and asserts alignment against its block size, although the coordinator never returns hit blocks for it.

This PR records which groups take part in offloading (`prefix_cacheable`) and skips the rest in eager store selection and in load pairing. Scratch blocks never carry a hash, so nothing is stored or loaded for them either way; the scratch slot in the per-group hit tuple stays empty, exactly as the coordinator leaves it.


## Duplication check

Two open PRs touch the same code path: #55033 (draft since 2026-09-02, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA ring, also adjusts `_estimate_lazy_target_blocks`) and #56404 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, gates `resolve_block_hashes` in the store path only, currently conflicting). This PR is scoped to the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool-tail layout and adds what neither of them covers: a regression test for the actual crash trigger (`enable_kv_cache_events=true`, `BlockStored` emitted for cacheable groups only) and an end-to-end store/load + accuracy check on GLM-5.3-Flash. Happy to fold the test into #55033 instead if the maintainers prefer to land that one.

title: [Perf][GLM] Fuse the kpool tail slot mapping into one Triton kernel
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash sparse-MLA models keep a one-block-per-request circular tail cache (kpool). Every decode step — twice per step with MTP, once for the target model and once for the drafter — `KpoolTailMetadataBuilder.build()` maps each token to its request's tail ring with a chain of small torch ops (`arange` + `searchsorted` + `clamp` + `index_select` + `remainder` + `copy_`): 12 kernel launches and ~250 us of CPU enqueue time per build.

This PR replaces the chain with a single Triton kernel driven directly by `query_start_loc`, including the CUDA-graph padding rows. The CPU-tensor path keeps the torch implementation, and the emitted values are bit-identical to it.

With #57317 the generic `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` no longer runs for `KpoolTailSpec`, so `compute_kpool_tail_slot_mapping` is now the only slot-mapping path for the tail group — this fusion covers all of it. It composes with #57477 (the seed-kernel stride fix): this PR only produces the logical slot ids (`block * kpool + pos % kpool`) that consumers decompose with `// kpool` / `% kpool`; physical addressing of the padded tail view is untouched, and the kernel reads the block table through its real `stride(0)`.

Not a duplicate: #56562 covers the sparse-indexer decode expansion and the token→request mapping (an earlier revision of this PR had similar pieces and was rescoped); #57161 reworks the kpool *compress* kernel and #57458 the NoPE query packing — neither touches the tail slot mapping.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_native_next_n.py
```

title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Address kpool tail blocks by the padded indexer stride in the NVIDIA prefill seed kernel
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix silent indexer-cache corruption for GLM-5.3-Flash on NVIDIA: the kpool prefill tail-seed kernel addresses tail blocks with a dense stride while the tail cache is stored with the indexer's padded block stride.

**How the tail cache is laid out.** `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` pads the `KpoolTailSpec` page to the indexer page (`page_size_padded = idx_page`; 38016 B for the default `block_size=1152`: 288 pool rows x 132 B), and `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` places every indexer layer's tail tensor at the *same offset* as that layer's indexer tensor with `block_stride = idx_page`. Tail block `b` is therefore the first 2048 B (`[2, kpool=4, 128]` bf16) of indexer block `b`; the two never collide because both groups draw distinct block ids from one pool. `create_kv_cache_views` builds the view with `as_strided`, so `tail_kv_cache.stride(0) == 19008` elements instead of the dense 1024.

**The bug.** `_kpool_tail_seed_kernel` in `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/kpool_compress.py` computed

```python
base = (blk * 2 * KPOOL + t % KPOOL) * HEAD_DIM   # dense 2048 B block stride
```

so for every prefill it (a) left the request's own tail block unseeded and (b) wrote 2048 B of raw bf16 K / gate rows at byte `blk * 2048` of the layer's indexer region, i.e. into indexer block `blk * 2048 // 38016` at offset `blk * 2048 % 38016` — fp8 key rows or the fp32 scale region of whatever request owns that block. The decode kernel (`TAIL_BLOCK_ELEMS` / `KPOOL_HEAD`) and the AMD seed kernel already address the tail through `stride(0)` / `stride(1)`; only the NVIDIA seed kernel did not, and the existing regression test for exactly this layout was `skipif(not is_rocm)`.

**Why it shows up as "the cached system prompt is broken".** Only indexer blocks with id below `num_blocks * 2048 / 38016` (~5% of the pool) can be hit, and those are the ids handed out first after startup, i.e. the blocks of the first prefix-cached prompt, typically a long-lived system prompt. title: [Draft][CPU][GLM5Next] Add sparse MLA / KeyPool backend
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

This PR adds a correctness-first CPU sparse MLA / KeyPool execution path for GLM5Next for #57345.

The implementation keeps the common GLM5Next model graph and adds only the GLM-local CPU indexer, KeyPool lifecycle, metadata, and sparse MLA adapters required for execution. It is independent of the CPU KDA work in #57496.

## Self-review / Implementation notes

### Why a GLM-specific path

The existing dense CPU MLA backend does not match the GLM5Next sparse contract. The DeepSeek CPU implementations were useful structural references, but GLM5Next has distinct KeyPool compression, gate-score pooling, pool-level top-k, pool-to-token expansion, incomplete-pool tails, index-cache representation, and request-local pool boundaries.

For that reason this PR does not copy a complete DeepSeek attention object graph and does not introduce a generic sparse framework. The feature-local flow is:

```text
GLM5Next common attention
  -> CPU indexer metadata
  -> KeyPool compression/tail/cache lifecycle
  -> selected-row sparse MLA
  -> existing latent/value/output projections
```

I intentionally did not add `glm5next/cpu/model.py`. The existing model hierarchy remains usable; only sparse indexer/MLA execution and the minimum platform/backend injection differ on CPU.

### KeyPool lifecycle

For complete pools, the CPU path preserves the intended sequence of pooling, BF16 round-trip, Hadamard transform, FP8 quantization, and index-cache write. For incomplete pools it preserves raw K/gate tail state. Decode reads the request-local tail before adding the new token, then performs pool completion, cache write, top-k selection, and token expansion in that order.

The metadata builder carries pool-granular lengths, block tables, slot mappings, request expansion, and physical-page addressing rather than reconstructing those values heuristically inside the backend.

title: [Feature]: [CPU][GLM5Next] Add native sparse MLA / KeyPool indexer support for GLM-5.3-Flash

## Motivation

GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` / `glm5next`) is now supported in vLLM, but its native sparse MLA / KeyPool attention path is not implemented for the CPU backend.

This is different from #54018 / #54029.

Those address the older `glm_moe_dsa` path and provide a way to disable sparse attention and fall back to dense MLA on CPU.

For GLM-5.3-Flash, I would like to request **native CPU execution of its sparse MLA + KeyPool/KeyPoolIndexer path**, preserving the model's sparse-attention behavior rather than converting it to dense MLA.

## Current state on `main`

The generic CPU attention selector still rejects sparse attention:

```python
if attn_selector_config.use_sparse:
    raise NotImplementedError("Sparse Attention is not supported on CPU.")
```

At the same time, CPU support has recently progressed significantly: DeepSeek-V4 now has its own x86/AMX CPU sparse-MLA/indexer implementation, including CPU kernels for the sparse attention/indexing pipeline.

`vllm/platforms/cpu.py` explicitly documents the DeepSeek-V4 CPU kernels under:

```text
csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/
├── flash_mla
├── store_cache
├── compressor
├── paged_mqa_logits
└── topk
```

and configures DeepSeek-V4 separately with its required block size.

This makes GLM5Next support seem like a useful next target rather than requiring CPU sparse attention infrastructure to be created entirely from scratch.

## GLM5Next-specific gap

GLM-5.3 uses a different sparse-indexing scheme from DeepSeek-V4.

The current GLM5Next sparse-indexer dispatcher is effectively:

```python

    from .amd.sparse_indexer import SparseAttnIndexerKpool
else:
    from .nvidia.sparse_indexer import SparseAttnIndexerKpool
```

There is no CPU branch.

Therefore a CPU build falls into the NVIDIA implementation rather than a CPU implementation.

author: ixcans

title: [Bugfix] fused_qk_norm_rope: partial rotary neox path shuffled from a divergent branch
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`fused_qk_norm_rope` with `rotary_dim < head_dim` (partial rotary, e.g. GLM-4 / GLM-4.5 with `partial_rotary_factor=0.5`) only lets `rotary_lanes = rotary_dim / elems_per_lane` lanes into the RoPE branch. The neox path then calls `__shfl_xor_sync` / `__syncwarp` inside that branch with a full-warp mask, i.e. from a divergent branch where the mask names lanes that never arrive. That is undefined behaviour. With the single-head kernel it happens to produce the right values; with the N-token-heads kernel (`token_heads_per_warp > 1`, auto-selected on SM90 once `num_tokens * (num_heads + num_kv_heads) >= 10240`) it returns garbage or NaN on H200 for such layers.

## Changes

Do the warp exchange once before the lane guard with the whole warp participating; only the rotary lanes use the exchanged values. Same for both kernels. The `__syncwarp()` calls around the shuffle are no longer needed (the shuffle itself synchronises the participating lanes).

## Test plan

Standalone build of this file on H200 against a vLLM 0.28.0 install, compared with that install's `fused_qk_norm_rope`:

- full rotary (`rotary_dim == head_dim`) and all gptj/interleaved cases: bitwise identical to the shipped kernel before and after (bf16/fp16, head_dim 64/128/256, 1–8192 tokens, `token_heads_per_warp` 1/2/4/8).
- partial rotary, neox, e.g. hq32/hkv8/d128 with `rotary_dim=64`: shipped kernel at 300 tokens differs from the fp32 reference by up to 2.9, and is NaN at 2048/8192 tokens; the fixed kernel is finite and matches the fp32 reference at every size (and is still bitwise identical to the shipped kernel wherever `token_heads_per_warp == 1`).

title: [Bug]: NIXL P/D disagg silently corrupts output when hybrid-attention layers share a storage base with different block lengths (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash)
bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash served via NIXL PD disaggregation (2P×TP8 + 2D×TP8, 2×H200 nodes, RDMA) produces garbled output (nonsensical characters, or empty content/reasoning fields) with no errors or crashes — silent data corruption. The same image serves a single-full-attention model (GLM-5.3) correctly in the same topology. Mooncake, CUDA graphs, and MultiConnector were ruled out.

### Root cause

In `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py`, region registration deduplicates transfer regions by `base_addr` alone, and the collapsed branch only refreshes `block_len/stride/num_blocks` when `is_mla_region` is true.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's `layers.2.attn.compressor.state_cache` (`CircularBufferSpec`, needs block_len=32768) shares its storage base address with `layers.0.attn.swa_cache` (MLA, block_len=19008). It folds into region 0 without updating block_len, so its compressor state is transferred with only 19008 bytes per block and offsets computed from the swa view — truncated and misaligned. `layers.2.attn.indexer.k_cache` hits a second instance of the same base-address conflict.

Diagnostic signature: the affected region simultaneously shows `rgid=-1` (shared), `scratch=True`, and `is_mla=True` — three mutually contradictory attributes. After the fix, `num_regions` grows 12 → 14.

### Fix

Deduplicate by `(base_addr, block_len)`: regions with distinct transfer geometry stay separate; identical-geometry aliases still fold as before. A PR follows.

### Verification

- Cluster (2×8 H200, P/D disagg): before the fix — all-garbled short completions, 200-token generations fully corrupted, Chinese chat returns empty content/reasoning; after the fix — normal English/Chinese output, 0% garble rate over 200-token generations, clean output across 6 concurrent streams.
- Unit tests: new regression test fails on HEAD and passes with the fix; the existing NIXL unit test failure set is byte-identical before/after (no regressions).

title: [Feature]: [CPU][GLM5Next][KDA] Add CPU KDA backend for GLM-5.3-Flash
bodyExcerpt:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Motivation

GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) is a hybrid model containing both:

* sparse MLA layers
* KDA (Kimi Delta Attention / gated delta-rule) linear-attention layers

Even if GLM5Next's sparse MLA / KeyPool path is made CPU-compatible, the model still cannot execute end-to-end on CPU without a KDA backend.

I would like to request native CPU support for GLM5Next KDA.

## Current state

The GLM5Next KDA implementation currently lives under the accelerator-specific path:

```text
vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/kda.py
```

and uses GPU-oriented Flash Linear Attention / Triton operators such as:

```text
chunk_kda_with_fused_gate
fused_recurrent_kda
```

There does not appear to be a corresponding:

```text
vllm/models/glm5next/cpu/kda.py
```

or other CPU KDA execution path for GLM5Next on current `main`.

This makes KDA an independent CPU blocker from sparse MLA / KeyPool support.

GLM-5.3-Flash has a large number of KDA layers, so this cannot reasonably be worked around by supporting only the sparse-MLA portion of the model.

## Related CPU infrastructure already exists

The CPU backend already has substantial support for related linear-attention/state-space workloads.

In particular, current CPU platform code contains an accelerated GDN path using:

```text
AMX tiles
or
AVX-512 BF16 / VDPBF16PS
```

and vLLM already has CPU machinery for stateful hybrid models, including:

* recurrent state caches
* convolution state
* chunked prefill
* decode
* hybrid KV/state-cache management

KDA is not identical to GDN, but they are closely related enough that it may be possible to reuse much of this infrastructure.

## KDA-specific work

As I understand it, GLM5Next KDA needs CPU equivalents for the KDA-specific operations around the existing gated-delta/state machinery, including:

```text
Q/K/V short convolution
        │
        ▼
KDA gate computation
        │
        ▼
chunked gated-delta prefill

bodyExcerpt:
## Describe the bug

`zai-org/GLM-OCR` MTP speculative decoding fails at startup on vLLM 0.29.0 (stable, PyPI aarch64 wheel) due to two independent defects. Both are reproducible on an NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121, aarch64) with torch 2.13.0+cu130; defect 1 is architecture-independent (pure weight-name handling).

### Defect 1 — MTP weights silently dropped: loader classifies before rewriting the prefix

`GlmOcrMTP.load_weights()` (`vllm/model_executor/models/glm_ocr_mtp.py`) classifies each incoming weight with `get_spec_layer_idx_from_weight_name()` **before** `_rewrite_spec_layer_name()` strips the checkpoint's `model.language_model.layers` prefix:

```python
else:
    spec_layer = get_spec_layer_idx_from_weight_name(self.config, name)  # checks "model.layers.16."
    if spec_layer is None:
        continue                    # <-- drops every MTP tensor here

title: [Feature]: Production evidence for restoring concurrent partial prefill limits (max_num_partial_prefills / max_concurrent_prefills) in V1 scheduler
bodyExcerpt:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Motivation

We operate a production vLLM deployment (GLM-based MoE model, TP=4, 4x NVIDIA B200,
V1 engine) serving a workload dominated by very long prompts (RAG/long-context,
median ~100k-180k prompt tokens per request, generation typically <1k tokens).
Under this workload we consistently observe severe TTFT tail latency caused by
head-of-line blocking in prefill scheduling, and we believe this is a strong
real-world case for reviving #49075 / #55256.

## Problem

With `--enable-chunked-prefill` and `--max-num-batched-tokens` set to a
reasonably high value (tested 8192 and 16384), a single long-prompt request
still needs many scheduler iterations to complete its prefill
(prompt_tokens / max_num_batched_tokens ≈ 7-12 iterations for our 100k-180k
token prompts). Because the V1 scheduler currently has **no cap on concurrent
partial prefills**, any request queued behind one of these long prefills must
wait for it to fully finish before its own prefill can start — there is no
way to interleave multiple partial prefills to give newer/shorter requests a
fair share of the per-step token budget.

We attempted to mitigate this with `--max-num-partial-prefills 4` (docs suggest
this exists as a `SchedulerConfig` field), which immediately fails:

vllm: error: unrecognized arguments: --max-num-partial-prefills 4

Digging into this, we found the flag was intentionally removed from
`vllm/config/scheduler.py` in #49244 (V0 cleanup, July 2026) as "dead config"
because it had no V1 consumer, and issue #39737 confirms the same failure mode
on an earlier vLLM version (`NotImplementedError: Concurrent Partial Prefill
is not supported`) with no maintainer response since April 2026. #49075
attempts to restore and properly enforce these fields in the V1 scheduler but
is currently open, unrebased, has an unresolved CodeRabbit finding on the
WAITING-loop admission check, and has never had CI run. #55256 proposed a
simpler, threshold-independent `m

title: [Bugfix] GLM-5.3-Flash: keep FP8 weight/scale pairs across load_weights calls
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`Glm5NextModel.load_weights` (GLM-5.3-Flash) dequantizes the block-FP8 `q_a_proj`, `kv_a_proj_with_mqa`, `q_b_proj`, `o_proj` and `indexer.wk` tensors to BF16 once both the weight and its `weight_scale_inv` have been seen, parking the first half in a pending dict (`_pending_wk_fp8`). That dict is a local of one `load_weights` call.

For more details on repro and where the code comes from, see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56583

**Fix.** Persist the pending dict on the model instance (`self._pending_fp8_pairs`), mirroring #46168. Completed pairs are already popped by the helpers, so the dict is empty again after a full load. The single-call path is unchanged.

Related: #43163 / #43464, #41749 / #42244, #38991, sgl-project/sglang#37369 (the sglang loader's version of the same problem), https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash/discussions/23 (vLLM on H100, resolved by disabling distributed streaming).

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56583

title: kv-cache: honor scheduler lookahead in mamba align-mode allocation
bodyExcerpt:
## Problem

In mamba align cache mode (mamba-hybrid models with prefix caching), `MambaManager.allocate_new_blocks` and `get_num_blocks_to_allocate` discarded all lookahead tokens by resetting `num_tokens` to `num_tokens_main_model`. When the scheduler schedules lookahead capacity beyond a main-model sequence that ends exactly on a page boundary, this corrupts the recurrent state in two ways.

## Root cause

A mamba state table row is page-indexed: the worker's running-state column is `cdiv(main_end, bs) - 1`.

1. **Missing next page.** When a chunk ends exactly on a page boundary and lookahead tokens extend beyond it, the next page was not materialized with the current schedule. The boundary token's state write then targeted a block-table entry that still held a recycled stale block — the recurrent state is corrupted from that point on (one-step NaN followed by a repetition lock at every page boundary).

2. **Displaced running-state column.** If a page was materialized for the lookahead, the null padding was derived from the inflated `num_tokens`, so the reserved page displaced the real running-state column. The worker's running-state index (0 for a chunk ending at the first page boundary) pointed at the null slot; the next chunk's state pre-copy chained from the null slot and spec-decode acceptance collapsed to zero permanently for that request.

## Diagnosis

Reproduced on a 4-node Arm (Thor SM110) cluster serving GLM-5.3-Flash (mamba-hybrid + MTP + prefix caching) with deterministic single-turn probes: prompts whose prefill chunk ends exactly on a page boundary produced 0% spec-decode acceptance from the first decode step, while boundary-crossing-free prompts were healthy. The failure moved with cache layout across boots, and per-request scheduler dumps of the mamba state-table rows showed the displaced null column exactly at the worker's running-state index. The corruption was confirmed to chain through the state pre-copy (pre-copy source = the null slot).

title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3-Flash (glm5_next, qk_rope_head_dim=0 / NoPE MLA) crashes — concat_and_cache_mla requires pe_dim==64
bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

vLLM cannot serve `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (or its NVFP4/FP8 quants, e.g. `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`). The model's MLA is **NoPE** (`qk_rope_head_dim = 0`), but `glm5_next`'s only attention backend, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`, uses the `fp8_ds_mla` / `nvfp4_ds_mla` KV-cache format, whose `concat_and_cache_mla` kernel hardcodes DeepSeek geometry (`pe_dim == 64`, `kv_lora_rank == 512`). It loads, wires up TP, and profiles the KV cache successfully, then dies in MLA warmup:

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'concat_and_cache_mla, csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu:939, pe_dim must be 64 for fp8_ds_mla'
```

### Why it's not just the assertion

`concat_and_cache_ds_mla_kernel` launches `block(96)` = 64 threads for the 512-wide NoPE part + threads 64–95 copying exactly 64 RoPE elements into a fixed 656-byte entry. For `pe_dim=0` there is no RoPE section, so relaxing the `STD_TORCH_CHECK(pe_dim == 64, ...)` would make the RoPE threads read nonexistent `k_pe` and write a bogus rope region → silent corruption. Supporting NoPE MLA needs a dedicated kernel variant + entry layout + format routing. The same `pe_dim == 64` requirement exists in the `nvfp4_ds_mla` path, and both are still present on `main` (`csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu`).

### Repro

```
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --distributed-executor-backend ray \
  --trust-remote-code --enforce-eager
```

title: [Multimodal] Split video metadata in VideoProcessorItems
bodyExcerpt:
### What does this PR do?

HF video processors take `videos` and a parallel `video_metadata` kwarg. vLLM's parser instead bundles metadata into each item as `(frames, metadata)` so it travels with the video through hashing and caching. Nothing in between reconciles the two, so every model that needs metadata unzips the tuples itself, and each does it differently:

| file | behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `glm4_1v.py` | converts to `VideoMetadata`, hoists `do_sample_frames` (last one wins) |
| `ernie45_vl.py` | gated on `supports_video_metadata`, warns and unwraps for old processors |
| `molmo2.py` | asserts the tuple shape, reads `frames_indices` for timestamps |
| `llava_onevision2.py` | recovers a codec file path from a private marker key in the metadata dict |

This does the split once, in `VideoProcessorItems.get_processor_data`, and updates those four to read the two keys. Models that build their own processor input in `_call_hf_processor` (Qwen3-VL, Gemma 4, Nano Nemotron VL) are untouched, as are models without video metadata, which keep emitting only `videos`.

`#57441` adds a fifth copy in the Transformers backend, including a `do_sample_frames` agreement check. That is not on `main` yet, so it is not touched here; its override simplifies once both land.

This is close to line neutral, not a line-count win: `parse.py` gains 16 lines and the four consumers shed 20, for a net of -4 outside tests. The argument for it is that the `(frames, metadata)` to `videos`/`video_metadata` contract gets one definition rather than four divergent ones.

`do_sample_frames` is a per-request processor kwarg that travels inside per-item metadata, so every consumer reconciles it differently. Models that call HF once per video (Molmo 2, Qwen3-VL, GLM-4.1V's item-wise path) legitimately support different values per video. title: [ROCm][Model][DCP] Default Kimi-K3's DCP combine to a2a
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Kimi-K3 leaves `dcp_comm_backend` unset, so it gets the `ag_rs` default: `allgather(lse)` + `reduce_scatter(out)`. The `a2a` combine is a single `all_to_all_single` and is faster at every token count measured.

Wall ms per combine call, MI355X (gfx950, 8-rank xGMI):

| tokens | `ag_rs` | `a2a` | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 5 | 0.107 | 0.095 | 1.13x |
| 48 | 0.111 | 0.097 | 1.15x |
| 144 | 0.136 | 0.101 | **1.35x** |

The margin grows with T, and combine runs **per MLA layer per decode step**, so it multiplies by the layer count. Cosine similarity against `ag_rs` was **>= 0.999994** across the sweep.

`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` already does exactly this through the same `set_dcp_defaults` hook, added in #50382. This applies the same treatment to Kimi-K3.

Three deliberate limits on scope:

- **ROCm only.** The hook returns early off ROCm. `a2a` is one `all_to_all_single` against `allgather(lse)` + `reduce_scatter(out)`, so which side wins depends on the interconnect, and the numbers above are MI355X (gfx950, 8-rank xGMI). No other platform's default is moved by this change. Both branches are covered by tests.

- **`q_replicate` is not set.** `GlmMoeDsa` pairs `a2a` with `q_replicate=True`; that changes weight loading and is an independent question we have not measured, so it is left alone.
- **This changes only the default.** `set_dcp_defaults` fills options the user left unset, so an explicit `--dcp-comm-backend` still wins. A test pins that, because a "default" that silently overrode the flag would be worse than no default at all.

### Note on prefill context parallelism

`a2a` has a known caveat under PCP: #56677 pins `--dcp-comm-backend ag_rs` for a GLM-5.2 PCP4+DCP4 eval config, and GLM already defaults to `a2a`. title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Fix GLM-5.3 kpool indexer block sizes
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

  Fixes #54359: GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer overwrites its own KV cache.

  On ROCm, GLM-5.3-Flash compresses one indexer state from every
  index_kpool tokens. However, the generic ROCm indexer backend currently
  advertises the following kernel block-size support in token units:

  [1, MultipleOf(16)]

  This allows the complete KV manager block to be selected directly as the
  kernel block size.

  For index_kpool=4 and a 640-token manager block, this selects 640 tokens,
  which represents 160 compressed states. The paged-MQA kernels operate on
  pages of 32 or 64 states, so the block table is not split at the granularity
  used by the kernel.

  As described in
  #54359, this can cause
  multiple logical indexer pages to address the same physical cache slots,
  silently corrupting the indexer cache and degrading long-context retrieval.

  ## Changes

  - Add a cached kpool-aware indexer backend.
  - Scale paged-MQA state page sizes by index_kpool when advertising
    supported kernel block sizes.

  - Use the kpool-aware backend only for Glm5NextIndexerCache on ROCm.
  - Keep the non-ROCm path unchanged.
  - Keep the generic DeepSeek indexer backend unchanged.
  - Add regression coverage for both the 32-state and 64-state page cases.

  For index_kpool=4, the kpool-aware backend advertises:

  32 states × 4 tokens/state = 128 tokens
  64 states × 4 tokens/state = 256 tokens

  This causes the existing hybrid block-table implementation to split the
  manager block into correctly sized virtual kernel pages.

  ## Scope

  This change only affects the attention-backend metadata selected by the
  GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer on ROCm.

  It does not change:

  - KV cache allocation size;
  - model weights or model computation;
  - CUDA backend selection;
  - generic DeepSeek indexer behavior;
  - GPU kernels;
  - deployment or serving parameters.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Attention] Add missing record_logical_topk_ready to sparse MLA impls
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper.forward_native` calls `self.mla_attn.impl.record_logical_topk_ready()` on every sparse MLA layer ([`vllm/model_executor/layers/mla.py:235`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/mla.py#L235)). The hook only exists on `SparseMLACommonImpl`; `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` and `XPUMLASparseImpl` inherit `MLAAttentionImpl` + `SharedTopkIndicesBuffer` directly, so serving GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) on ROCm crashes at model load:

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error ''ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl' object
has no attribute 'record_logical_topk_ready''
```

The hook records an event for HiSparse host-resident top-k prefetching via the optional `SparseMLAIndexGroup`. Neither affected backend ever receives an index group (GLM-5.3-Flash allocates only the shared `topk_indices_buffer`; no builder is passed to ROCm/XPU impls), so the correct semantics for them is a no-op — the same default `SparseMLACommonImpl` already provides when `self.index_group is None`.

## Changes

- Add a no-op `record_logical_topk_ready` default to the `MLAAttentionImpl` base class (next to the existing `prepare_for_batch` no-op), so every current and future sparse MLA implementation satisfies the interface.
- Drop the now-redundant `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` at both call sites (`mla.py`, `deepseek_v32/attention.py`).
- `SparseMLACommonImpl` keeps its index-group-aware override (asserted by a test).

Duplicate-work check: no open PR addresses this (`gh pr list --search "record_logical_topk_ready"` is empty; `fwht`/`glm5next` searches return unrelated refactor #55358, which moves files but does not touch the hook or fp8 dtype).

title: [Security] Bound OpenCV video decode frame walks
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary
The default OpenCV video decoder walks every source frame up to the last sampled index via sequential `cap.grab()`. Uniform sampling always includes that last index, so decode CPU tracks container frame count rather than the small number of returned frames. A long, highly compressible video stays under the download-size cap and can occupy a media worker for the full walk. This adds `VLLM_MAX_VIDEO_DECODE_FRAMES` (default 36000, `0` disables) and rejects over-budget walks before either OpenCV grab loop starts.

## Changes
- `vllm/envs.py`: add `VLLM_MAX_VIDEO_DECODE_FRAMES`.
- `vllm/multimodal/video_decoders/base.py`: reject walks above the cap.
- `vllm/multimodal/video_decoders/opencv.py`: enforce the cap in `read_frames` (covers recovery and non-recovery paths).
- `docs/usage/security.md`: document the new decode-size guard.
- Tests for under-limit, over-limit (both recovery modes), disable-with-0, and the `VideoMediaIO` entry point.

## Codepath coverage
- Chat / messages / responses / batch / `/invocations` / gRPC / offline `LLM.generate` all reach `VideoMediaIO` → OpenCV `read_frames`: covered.
- `video/jpeg` base64 and TorchCodec / PyNvVideoCodec / DeepStream do not use this grab loop: N/A.
- GLM-5.1 seek-based `read_frames` override does not use the sequential grab loop unless `frame_recovery=True` (then it calls the shared `read_frames`): covered on that recovery path.

## Duplicate-work check
Searched open, draft, and recently merged PRs for OpenCV `read_frames`, `cap.grab`, video decode frame/duration limits, and `video_decoders/opencv`. #55582 speeds GLM sampler index selection; #46836 adds an encoded-file size guard; #51969 clamps request `num_frames` for `video/jpeg`. None of those bound the OpenCV sequential grab loop.

## Tests
- `test_opencv_decode_frame_limit_respected`
- `test_opencv_decode_frame_limit_rejected` (frame_recovery false/true)
- `test_opencv_decode_frame_limit_disabled`
- `test_video_media_io_decode_frame_limit_rejected`

title: [Frontend] glm47 tool parser: required-first schema order in prompt rendering and strict structural tags
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix a tool-calling failure mode of the glm47 parser family (GLM-4.5/4.6/4.7/5.x, incl. GLM-5.3-Flash): **the model omits a required property of a nested object when a bulky optional property precedes it in the schema**.

A request (a `collect_preferences` tool whose `items[]` objects require `prompt` + `tag`, with an optional `choices` array declared between them) fails 50-66% of the time on vLLM with GLM-5.3-Flash: the emitted `items[]` objects are missing `tag`. The same failure reproduces on sglang at the same rate (46-60%), so this is a model-behavior boundary issue, not a stack bug.

Mechanism (measured with prefix logprob probes on `/v1/completions`):

- GLM renders tool schemas verbatim into the prompt and tends to emit argument keys following the schema's property order.
- The first key of each item object is a near-tie between the content fields (`p(choices)=0.62` vs `p(prompt)=0.38`, `p(tag)~=0` — the model never opens an object with the label field). Once it starts with the optional `choices` array, the object "feels complete" after `prompt` and `tag` is skipped (`p(tag)` after choices ≈ 0.0002; after prompt ≈ 0.9998). At temp=0 the outcome is still non-deterministic — kernel noise flips the near-tie.
- The coupling is stack-independent (vLLM: prompt-first → 65/65 keep tag, choices-first → 78% lose it; sglang: 11/11 vs 77%).

Fix (two commits on this branch):

1. **`reorder_tool_schema_required_first`**: render each object schema's `properties` with `required` fields first (declaration order), recursing into nested object/array schemas. JSON Schema property order is not semantically meaningful, so validation and clients are unaffected. Opt-in per tool parser; enabled for the glm47 parser family. The reorder runs in `OnlineRenderer` right after the per-request tool dicts are built — the parser's `adjust_request` hook runs *after* chat-template rendering, which is too late to affect the prompt.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Alias SparseAttnIndexerKpool.forward_cuda to forward_native (GLM-5.3-Flash boot crash)
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #57424. `SparseAttnIndexerKpool` on the AMD/ROCm path (`vllm/models/glm5next/amd/sparse_indexer.py`) defines only `forward_native`. `CustomOp.dispatch_forward` routes *enabled* ops to `forward_hip` on ROCm, and `forward_hip` falls back to `forward_cuda` — which doesn't exist → `NotImplementedError` at the first forward of the indexer op.

On the `v0.29.1rc0.dev265+g0bfc7a15d` ROCm nightly, serving GLM-5.3-Flash crashes at `profile_run` with:

```
File "vllm/model_executor/custom_op.py", line 149, in forward_hip
    return self.forward_cuda(*args, **kwargs)
File "vllm/model_executor/custom_op.py", line 145, in forward_cuda
    raise NotImplementedError
```

because the resolved `compilation_config.custom_ops` contains `'all'` there, enabling every registered op — including `sparse_attn_indexer_kpool`.

## Why

The NVIDIA `SparseAttnIndexerKpool` defines both `forward_native` and `forward_cuda`; the AMD one is native-only but was never given the alias the ROCm dispatch requires. This blocks GLM-5.3-Flash boot on current ROCm nightlies entirely.

## Test results

- New unit test `tests/models/test_rocm_sparse_indexer_forward_cuda.py`: fails on the unpatched file, passes with the fix (run with `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`).
- End-to-end on 8×MI350X (TP8, GLM-5.3-Flash fp8, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-0bfc7a15d` + this patch in-place): engine boots Ready with 57 FULL + 106 PIECEWISE cudagraphs captured; chunked-prefill repro (20K prompt, 16K chunks) plus a long-context ladder 32K→524,212 tokens all pass with zero memory access faults, engine healthy after.

AI assistance was used in preparing this PR; the change was reviewed and hardware-validated end-to-end by the submitter.

## Related

- #57227 — original gfx950 16K-chunk memory access fault; root-caused by #57317
- #57317 — kpool tail slot-mapping OOB fix (the root cause of #57227)
- #57248 — nightly GLM-5.3-Flash ROCm boot regressions (`record_logical_topk_ready` + jit-warmup)

File "vllm/model_executor/custom_op.py", line 149, in forward_hip
    return self.forward_cuda(*args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
File "vllm/model_executor/custom_op.py", line 145, in forward_cuda
    raise NotImplementedError
NotImplementedError
```

raised from `SparseAttnIndexerKpool` (`vllm/models/glm5next/common/attention.py:392` → `self.indexer_op(...)`).

### Root cause

`CustomOp.dispatch_forward` routes **enabled** ops to `forward_hip` on ROCm, and `forward_hip` falls back to `forward_cuda`. The AMD implementation of `SparseAttnIndexerKpool` (`vllm/models/glm5next/amd/sparse_indexer.py`, registered as `sparse_attn_indexer_kpool`) defines **only `forward_native`** — no `forward_cuda` — so any run where the op is enabled raises `NotImplementedError` at the first forward.

On this nightly the resolved `compilation_config.custom_ops` contains `'all'` (seen in the engine init log), which enables every registered op and triggers this deterministically.

The NVIDIA implementation (`nvidia/sparse_indexer.py`) defines both `forward_native` and `forward_cuda`; the AMD one is missing the alias the ROCm dispatch requires.

### Proposed fix

Alias at class level:

```python
SparseAttnIndexerKpool.forward_cuda = SparseAttnIndexerKpool.forward_native
```

(or define `forward_cuda` as a method calling `forward_native`), mirroring the NVIDIA implementation.

title: [Bugfix][KV Cache][GLM-5.3-Flash] Disable slot mapping kernel for the kpool tail buffer
bodyExcerpt:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57227.

GLM-5.3-Flash crashes with MAF when sending 500k ISL prompts.  This is caused by out of bounds indexing in the default `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` applied to the Kpool tail buffer. The kpool tail buffer has a fixed size for each request and anyway uses its own slot mapping kernel `compute_kpool_tail_slot_mapping`, and hence should not use the default kernel.

**Alternatively: make KpoolTailSpec inherit from CircularBufferSpec instead of the SW spec.**

## Why

The KpoolTailSpec is a ring buffer with one block per requests, and is addressed by `pos % kpool` (bounded). The generic slot mapping kernel `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` addresses by `pos // kernel_block_size` (unbounded), and it's used to be enabled for all kv specs except for `CircularBufferSpec`. 

#53781 refactored what kv specs should use this generic slot mapping kernel to instead those specs declaring `uses_slot_mapping: true`. However, KpoolTailSpec inherits from SW and not the circular buffer spec, meaning it still deemed to use the generic slot mapping kernel even though it's a ring buffer. Since that kernels addressing grows unbounded with sequence length (`pos // kernel_block_size`) while the actual KpoolTail buffer is fixed in size, this eventually triggered a MAF at long enough requests.

This PR fixes is it by excluding not using this generic slot mapping kernel for KpoolTailSpec. Instead it just relies on its tailored `compute_kpool_tail_slot_mapping` inside the metadata builder.

## Test Plan

#### 1. Expect no crash with 500k prompt request

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-num-seqs 512 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
    --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE --max-num-batched-tokens 16384
```
```bash
vllm bench serve \
