title: [Bugfix][ROCm][KV Offload] Use private pinned tensors for CPU KV offload
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Native CPU KV offload stalled during startup on an 8x MI308X node with TP8 and a 500 GiB offload pool. Six ranks reported `cudaHostRegister failed (code=1)`, and the engine never became ready.

`_uses_shared_region()` includes ROCm through `is_cuda_alike()`, so each worker registers the entire shared mmap region. Exclude ROCm to use the existing private per-rank pinned tensor allocator instead. The CUDA path is unchanged; ROCm no longer uses shared-region replicated KV deduplication.

Unlike #51081 (chunked registration) and #52296 (coordinated registration), this change bypasses shared mmap allocation on ROCm.

## Test Plan

Tested with vLLM 0.29.0 and ROCm 7.2.3 on two 8x MI308X hosts, running GLM-5.3 with TP8, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, and:

    --kv-offloading-size 500 --kv-offloading-backend native

Check startup and generation, then evict a cached 32K prompt from GPU KV cache using distinct filler prompts and replay it.

## Test Result

- Both hosts completed startup and served generation requests.
- Transfer counters confirmed CPU-to-GPU KV reload after eviction.
- The tested 32K gold-answer prompt returned the expected answer on both the cold request and the post-eviction replay.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Model] Quantize GLM-5.3-Flash indexer query with platform fp8 dtype
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`fwht128_quant_fp8` hardcodes `float8_e4m3fn` for the GLM-5.3-Flash indexer query and a 448 absmax clamp inside the Triton kernel. The function is called unconditionally from `Glm5NextAttention.forward` — including on ROCm, where the query flows into `rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`:

- On gfx942, AITER's flydsl `fp8_mqa_logits` kernel takes the `convert_q_fn` path for a `float8_e4m3fn` query and crashes at kernel emission:

```
AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute '_CAPIPtr'
  File ".../aiter/ops/flydsl/kernels/mqa_logits/fp8_mqa_logits.py", line 242, in kernel
    row_a[mi][kk] = _fn_to_fnuz_i64(raw) if convert_q_fn else raw
```

  Any request with chunked prefill (e.g. a 40K-token prompt) kills the worker and the engine crash-loops. Reproduced standalone: `flydsl_fp8_mqa_logits` with an FN-dtype query crashes at compile on gfx942.

- The 448 clamp is the e4m3fn max; e4m3fnuz's max differs, so rows whose absmax lands above the fnuz max would encode NaN/inf even where the FN path compiles.

The K-cache side already quantizes with `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` (`indexer_k_quant_and_cache_triton` IS_FNUZ; the AMD kpool ops module does the same via its `FP8_DTYPE` constant) — the query side is the odd one out.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Cap glm5next video sampling knobs
bodyExcerpt:
Fixes #55726

## Purpose

`glm_sample_frame_indices` walks `duration * target_fps` candidates and
deduplicates only at the end, so `Glm5NextVideoBackend` sizes that walk from the
requested fps rather than from the clip. On a 2-frame, 1-second source it spends
857 ms and 156 MiB to return 2 indices.

This clamps `target.fps` to `source.original_fps`. No sampling rate above the
source rate can return frames the container does not hold, so the walk becomes
bounded by the frame count while the sampled indices stay identical.

## Why not a fixed ceiling

An earlier revision copied GLMGA's `_MAX_FPS = 30` / `_MAX_FRAMES = 2048`. As
@JaredforReal pointed out, that ceiling has no basis in the GLM-5.3-Flash video
processor: its `processor_config.json` sets only `fps: 2` as the default
interval. A fixed 30 would also halve sampling for a legitimate 60 fps request.

Clamping to the source rate needs no magic number, and it makes the `max_frames`
ceiling unnecessary: with fps bounded, `extract_t` cannot exceed the frame count,
so `max_frames=100_000` keeps returning 10_000 indices exactly as on main.

## Measurements

Serving image, calling the backend directly, 2-frame 1-second clip, `fps` and
`max_frames` set to the same value:

| requested | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 200 000 | 11.9 ms, +1 MiB | 3.1 ms, +0 MiB |
| 2 000 000 | 87.4 ms, +18 MiB | 0.0 ms, +0 MiB |
| 20 000 000 | 857.5 ms, +156 MiB | 0.0 ms, +0 MiB |

Output is unchanged in every case: 2 indices for the 2-frame source, 900 for a
900-frame 30 fps clip, 2048 for a 10 000-frame one, and the default interval
still yields the same 60 indices as the bare sampler.

## Not a live exposure

Per-request `mm_processor_kwargs` do not reach the video loader today;
`chat_utils.py` still carries `TODO: Support per-request mm_processor_kwargs`.

title: [Bug][ROCm] Nightly af1c01499: GLM-5.3-Flash cannot boot — ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl missing record_logical_topk_ready + jit-warmup tilelang crash
bodyExcerpt:
## Nightly `af1c01499` (2026-09-16): two boot regressions for GLM-5.3-Flash on ROCm — model cannot start

Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-af1c01499b289be555c475669ba50a88e96d846e` (`vllm 0.29.1rc1.dev187+gaf1c01499`), 8×MI350X, TP8, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, serving `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`.

### Regression 1: `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` missing `record_logical_topk_ready`

```
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/mla.py", line 235, in forward
    self.mla_attn.impl.record_logical_topk_ready()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
AttributeError: 'ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl' object has no attribute 'record_logical_topk_ready'
```

`mla.py:235` calls the new `record_logical_topk_ready()` API (defined on the base sparse impl in `sparse_mla_attention.py:717`), but `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py:756`) doesn't implement or inherit it. Engine dies at first forward.

Workaround: add a no-op `record_logical_topk_ready` to `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl`.

### Regression 2: JIT kernel warmup crash — `'function' object has no attribute 'compile'`

```
File "vllm/model_executor/warmup/jit_warmup_tilelang_helper.py", line 141, in launch
    compiled = jit_impl.compile(*args, **kwargs)
AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'compile'
```

The new `--kernel-config` jit-warmup subsystem (on by default, `enable_jit_warmup: bool = True`) crashes in the tilelang helper on this path. All 8 workers die at `JIT kernel warmup starting`.

Workaround: `--kernel-config '{"enable_jit_warmup": false}'`.

With both workarounds the model boots and serves (and for us it also carried the `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` fix for the 16K-chunk fault in #57227). Both regressions block any GLM-5.3-Flash ROCm serving on the nightly.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Add record_logical_topk_ready to ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl (GLM-5.3-Flash boot crash)
bodyExcerpt:
## Why this is not duplicating #56604

#56604 (open since 2026-09-12) fixes the same crash class by adding a **default no-op `record_logical_topk_ready` on the `MLAAttentionImpl` base class** in `vllm/v1/attention/backend.py`, so every backend silently inherits it.

This PR instead adds the method **on `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` itself**, mirroring the existing `SparseMLACommonImpl` contract (`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/sparse_mla_attention.py:717`): impls that participate in sparse-MLA index groups implement the hook with real semantics; impls that don't declare an explicit no-op at their own site.

Trade-off: the base-class default in #56604 is broader (also covers any other backend that skips `SparseMLACommonImpl`) but weakens the interface — a new sparse backend that *should* implement index-group notification would silently no-op instead of failing loudly. This PR keeps that failure loud and fixes the one backend that currently crashes (ROCm AITER sparse MLA, GLM-5.3-Flash on MI350X). Either fix resolves the boot regression in #57248; happy to withdraw this in favor of #56604 if maintainers prefer the base-class default.

## Description

`MLAAttention.forward` calls `impl.record_logical_topk_ready()` on every sparse layer (`vllm/model_executor/layers/mla.py:235`). `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` inherits `SharedTopkIndicesBuffer` directly (not `SparseMLACommonImpl`) and never gained the method, so serving GLM-5.3-Flash on ROCm (gfx950, `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`) crashes at the first forward with `AttributeError: 'ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl' object has no attribute 'record_logical_topk_ready'`.

This impl shares the top-k indices buffer via `SharedTopkIndicesBuffer` but does not participate in `SparseMLAIndexGroup` host-side prefetching, so the correct implementation is a no-op.

title: [Bugfix][KV Cache][MLA] Align packed block strides for V3.2 sparse MLA
bodyExcerpt:
## Problem

Ordinary V3.2 sparse MLA and its indexer can resolve to `BLHNC` even when the packed block stride is not a whole number of every segment's physical rows. Binding/warmup then asserts; sparse row indexing requires the same invariant. This addresses the ordinary native-64-row allocation problem in #55431 and the geometry prerequisite discussed in #55434.

## Root cause

The allocator sums logical page bytes without encoding sparse consumers' row-addressing requirements. Physical rows include format metadata: 656 bytes for DS-FP8, 352 for DS-NVFP4, and 132 for the FP8 indexer. A heterogeneous sum need not divide by each row width.

## Fix

Declare `MLAAttentionSpec.block_stride_alignment_bytes` from the physical row widths and align the total packed block stride to their LCM. Carry that stride through allocation, capacity checks, overrides, auto-fit, and PP re-planning; merge requirements by LCM.

Preserve logical page sizes, integer-row index units, and layer-compact behavior. Declare BLHNC alongside existing supported layer-compact layouts; retain rejection of other unvalidated block-outermost layouts and unsupported manager/kernel splitting. No kernel, NIXL, or OffloadingConnector implementation changes.

## Padding / capacity cost

Padding is inventory-dependent and bounded by one alignment quantum. For a **synthetic 51-MLA / 50-indexer inventory**, native 64-token blocks, and a fixed **64 GiB** allocation budget:

| MLA format | Content bytes/block | Aligned stride | Tail bytes | Usable-capacity loss |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| BF16 | 4,182,528 | 4,194,432 | 11,904 | 0.2861% |
| Ordinary FP8 | 2,302,464 | 2,306,304 | 3,840 | 0.1675% |
| DS-FP8 | 2,563,584 | 2,576,112 | 12,528 | 0.4887% |
| DS-NVFP4 | 1,571,328 | 1,571,328 | 0 | 0% |

The comparison disables/enables only the row-alignment requirement and subtracts the reserved null block from usable capacity. This inventory is not a measured production GLM configuration. Smaller inventories can cost mo

title: [Bugfix] Release stale FlashMLA workspace views after growth
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Release obsolete FlashMLA scratch storage when another layer grows the shared workspace.

`FlashMLASparseImpl` keeps constructor-time tensor views in `q_concat_buffer`, `prefill_bf16_workspace`, and, with PCP+DCP, `gathered_kv_workspace`. When `WorkspaceManager` grows its allocation, those views keep the old storage alive. Both buffers remain allocated, reducing the memory available for KV cache.

This change stores shapes and dtypes, reserves capacity during initialization, and reacquires simultaneous views from the current workspace when used. Workspace sizing, tensor layout, and the manager's locking policy remain unchanged.

### Observed impact

We reproduced this on GLM-5.3 with DP/EP64, TP1, MTP1, automatic KV/context sizing, and a 0.95 GPU memory target, using a vLLM 0.29.0-based deployment. Allocator snapshots showed a 5,904 MiB FlashMLA workspace retained alongside a new 6,144 MiB MoE workspace on 18 of 64 ranks. The new allocation was traced to `FusedMoEKernelModularImpl._allocate_buffers` during profiling.

The corresponding fix on that deployed version produced these startup measurements:

| Measurement | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ranks retaining both allocations | 18 | 0 |
| Minimum KV capacity per rank | 490,816 tokens | 603,904 tokens |
| Total KV capacity across 64 ranks | 36,934,975 tokens | 38,971,455 tokens |

Total allocated memory recovered was **103.78125 GiB**. These are startup allocation measurements, not throughput or model-accuracy results. This PR ports the fix to current upstream and also covers its PCP+DCP gather buffer.

### Duplicate check

Searched open PRs for `flashmla workspace` and `workspace memory leak`, and checked issue #51743 and its linked open PRs. The closest workspace PR, #42856, changes workspace bounds for SM120; it does not release retained views after growth. Issue #51743 concerns runtime padded-Q allocation rather than this retained-storage case. No matching lifetime fix

title: WIP: fix(decode bench): remember zero-token prefix fills
bodyExcerpt:
DecodeBenchConnector currently records a request as filled only when the
  synthetic prefill contains at least one external token. A one-token prompt has
  a zero-token synthetic prefill, so a later preemption causes the connector to
  treat generated output as a new prompt and offer it as externally computed KV.

  With HiSparse, that false import can reach the host-only path at an arbitrary
  token offset and terminate the engine with:

  ValueError: A host-only HiSparse import must end on a cache-block boundary.

  refilled after preemption while preserving retries after failed allocation.

  DecodeBenchConnector composed with HiSparseConnector, one input token, 10,624
  requested output tokens, and 128 fixed requests per GPU. The failure occurred
  when GPU KV pressure first caused requests to be preempted and readmitted.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Keep GLM-5.3 (GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM) on MRV2
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #54924.

#53155 added `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` to `ROCM_DEFAULT_MRV1_ARCHITECTURES`, which
switches the default model runner for that architecture from MRV2 to MRV1 on
ROCm. GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 share this architecture string, so the change also
moved **GLM-5.3** onto MRV1, where it generates corrupted output: GSM8K 5-shot
accuracy drops from 91.6% to 14.9%.

This drops the architecture from the MRV1 carve-out so it stays on MRV2 by
default. The breakable-cudagraph default introduced by the same PR is left
untouched, since accuracy is unchanged with it on or off (see #54924).

Note that the MRV1 preference is intentional on ROCm (cf. #52488, #52866,
#52644). If GLM-5.2 genuinely needs MRV1 there, a discriminator finer than the
architecture string is required, because the GLM-5.3 checkpoint carries no
version field to tell the two apart. Restoring correctness for GLM-5.3 seems
the better default in the meantime.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][GLM-5.3-Flash] Apply deferred tilelang.jit already on attribute access
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Required to run GLM-5.3-Flash on MI350, otherwise errors during warmup with:

```bash
File "vllm/model_executor/warmup/jit_warmup.py", line 969, in compile_many
  self.compile(compile_key)
File "vllm/model_executor/warmup/jit_warmup_tilelang_helper.py", line 141, in launch
  return compile_tilelang(jit_impl, *args, **call_kwargs)
File "vllm/model_executor/warmup/jit_warmup_tilelang_helper.py", line 104, in compile_tilelang
  compiled = jit_impl.compile(*args, **kwargs)
AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'compile'
```

### Why

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51159 added lazy import of tilelang and made the `tilelang_jit` decorator return a **regular function on ROCm** instead of a `tilelang.jit.JITImpl`. On ROCm, this function would create and return the JITImpl when **called**. That's fine as long as you just _call_ the kernel the first time you need it, which is how warmup was previously done.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50178 refactored the warmup logic of tilelang mHC kernels. Previously the warmup was done by literally calling/running the mHC layers. After that PR, warmup now runs `.compile(...)` on the kernel to compile it, and later caches the compiled kernel manually. That's ok on CUDA where the kernel is a JITImpl, but not on ROCm where it's a regular function.

Hence the assumption that the tilelang kernel will be _called_ the first time it's used is no longer true. It's no longer launched during warmup, just `.compiled()`. This PR ensures that the first time we touch the (lazily created) kernel we convert it into a JITImpl to be compiled.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][ROCm] Fix MoRI-IO KV block-offset for speculative decoding (MTP)
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary
`compute_block_transfer_offsets` in the MoRI-IO KV connector raised `ValueError: local_block_ids longer than remote_block_ids` whenever the producer's local block count exceeded the consumer's. Under **speculative decoding (e.g. MTP)** with `block_size=1`, the prefill (producer) KV-cache manager reserves `num_speculative_tokens` lookahead slots that the decode (consumer) side does not allocate, so `local` exceeds `remote` by exactly the spec-token count (e.g. **8003 vs 8000** at n=3). This crashed the first prefill→decode KV write and made MTP unusable over MoRI-IO PD-disaggregation.

## Fix
Block order is positional (`block_size=1`), so the prompt KV is the prefix and the extra local blocks are empty lookahead scratch. Clamp `local_block_ids` to `local[:len(remote)]` and transfer only the prompt prefix — symmetric with the existing shorter-local handling already documented in the same function.

## Tests
`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_kv_layout.py`:
- Replaces the now-obsolete longer-local *raise* test with **clamp-to-prompt-prefix** tests for both the interleaved (`transfers_per_block=1`) and separated split-KV (`transfers_per_block=2`) layouts, asserting the result is identical to transferring `local[:len(remote)]`.
- Adds a shorter-local regression guard (pre-existing READ-mode partial transfer unchanged).

## Validation
GLM-5.3-FP8 WideEP **1P1D / 1P2D PD-disagg** (vLLM v0.27.1 + AITER v0.1.19), MTP n=3:
- KV transfer succeeds (clamp fires, e.g. `8003 -> 8000` / `8 -> 5`); no more ValueError.
- Coherent output, **0 token-0 (`!`) corruption**, FULL cudagraph engaged.
- 8k/8k decode-heavy shows the expected MTP TPOT win (1.36–1.45×) at low concurrency.

## AI assistance
This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Cursor). All changed lines and tests were reviewed, and the behavior was validated end-to-end by the submitter on GLM-5.3-FP8 WideEP PD-disaggregated serving (1P1D/1P2D). Attribution is recorded via the `Co-authored-by: Cursor` commit tr

bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Let the FlashInfer MLA prefill backend serve `(head_dim_qk=256, head_dim_vo=256)` by widening
its dimension whitelist and asking FlashInfer for `backend="auto"` instead of pinning
`"cutlass"`.

Today that shape cannot reach this backend at all, and the two reasons are coupled:

1. **`supported_mla_dimensions` lists exactly one entry**, DeepSeek-V3's
   `(qk_nope 128, qk_rope 64, v_head 128)`. `MLAPrefillBackend.supports_mla_dimensions()`
   rejects anything outside a non-empty list, so `FlashInferPrefillBackend` is filtered out
   before backend priority — or an explicit `mla_prefill_backend` override — is consulted.

2. **Both `BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper` constructions pin `backend="cutlass"`.**
   CUTLASS FMHA's dispatch (`DISPATCH_head_dim` in FlashInfer's `csrc/fmha_cutlass_sm100.cu`)
   accepts exactly `(192,128)`, `(128,128)` and `(64,64)`; `(256,256)` falls through to
   `return false`. Measured on GB300:

   ```
   RuntimeError: Check failed: (dispatched) is false:
   Unsupported head dimensions: head_dim_qk=256, head_dim_vo=256
   ```

   slowly.

The two are consistent — the whitelist was drawn around what the pinned CUTLASS backend can
serve — so widening one without unpinning the other just moves the failure later.

`backend="auto"` resolves per shape inside FlashInfer: cuDNN for `(256,256)`, and still CUTLASS
where CUTLASS fits.

title: [CI] Raise DSv4-Flash disaggregated engine readiness timeout to 1800s
bodyExcerpt:
## Root cause

The `:nvidia: (H200) DSv4-Flash Disaggregated DP EP` step (`dsv4-flash-disaggregated`) fails on main: both API servers die with

```
TimeoutError: Timed out waiting for engine core processes to start. ... Waited 900s (configured by VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S).
```

Failing job: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89444#01a0ac07-f462-419d-a09e-726a5bb8ec48 (build 89444, commit e0705731be04aac90838f318fcdae15c56a53080)

Timings verified from the job log:

- API servers started at 02:11:08; both frontends raised the TimeoutError at 02:26:25 (~900s budget hit).
- Engine cores were healthy but slow: model loading took 656-739s per worker (37.8-43.05 GiB/worker), then the JIT kernel warmup (244 compile keys, dominated by `MhcPreBigFuseTileLangKernel` at ~52-78s/kernel) took another 320-329s, finishing at 02:30:01 — ~1133s total, ~3.6 min after the frontends gave up.

The 900s budget was set by #56735 (merged 2026-09-15), but the DSv4 mHC TileLang kernel migration (#50178, merged 2026-09-13) added hundreds of seconds of JIT warmup on top of the slow weight load, blowing the budget again.

## Fix

Raise `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` for the `dsv4-flash-disaggregated` step from 900 to 1800, following exactly the pattern of #56735. 1800s = observed worst case (~1133s) + ~670s margin, and stays within the step's 60-minute `timeout_in_minutes` budget.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for: `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S dsv4`, `dsv4-flash-disaggregated timeout`, `DSv4-Flash Disaggregated`, `engine ready timeout`, `disaggregated timeout 1800`, `kernel warmup timeout`. The closest match is #56761 (`[Perf] Parallelize TileLang mHC JIT warmup for GLM-5.3-Flash`), which is a perf optimization for a different model and does not touch this step's config — even if it lands, the 900s budget for DSv4-Flash would remain marginal (model loading alone is ~740s). title: [Bugfix][Parser] GLM-4.7: stray arg tags must not leak into tool-call argument keys
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes a tool-call corruption in the GLM-4.7 parser: stray `arg_key` markup leaks into the parsed argument **key**, so the client rejects the call.

Observed in production against a GLM server run with `--tool-call-parser glm47`:

```
list_dir({"path</arg_key>": "/Users/user/Desktop/project"})
-> client error: "must have required property 'path'"
```

The client rejects the call, the agent loses the step, and the model retries with an invented path.

**Root cause.** `_glm47_arg_converter` matched the key with an unbounded non-greedy group:

```python
r"<arg_key>(?P<key>.*?)</arg_key>\s*<arg_value>(?P<value>.*?)</arg_value>"
```

`.*?` is non-greedy but it is *not* bounded by the delimiter it is scanning for. If the stream contains a repeated or stray `arg_key` tag, the engine backtracks past the first `</arg_key>` because that is what it takes to reach the following `<arg_value>`, and the extra markup ends up inside the key. On

```
<arg_key>path</arg_key></arg_key><arg_value>/tmp/x</arg_value>
```

the old code yields `{"path</arg_key>": "/tmp/x"}`, reproducing the observed string exactly. The mirrored `<arg_key><arg_key>path…` case yields `{"<arg_key>path": "/tmp/x"}`.

**Fix.** Match runs of non-`<` text so the key group cannot cross its own delimiter, and accept a run of closing tags so a duplicate is skipped rather than shifting the key:

```python
_ARG_KEY = r"<arg_key>(?P<key>[^<]*+(?:<(?!/?arg_key>)[^<]*+)*+)(?:</arg_key>\s*)+"
```

Both `_ARG_RE` and `_PARTIAL_ARG_RE` are built from it, so the streaming path gets the same guarantee.

The unrolled possessive form is deliberate rather than the simpler tempered dot `(?:(?!</?arg_key>).)*`. `_compute_arg_delta` re-runs the converter over the whole accumulated buffer on every argument chunk, so the common streaming case is a *failing* match against a partial buffer — precisely where a tempered dot backtracks per character. Measured on an unterminated buffer:

| buffer | tempered dot | possessive (ship

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Poolside: stray arg_key tags must not leak into tool-call argument keys
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`PoolsideV1ToolParser.func_arg_regex` captures the argument key with a plain
`.*?`:

```python
self.func_arg_regex = re.compile(
    r"<arg_key>(.*?)</arg_key>\s*<arg_value>(.*?)</arg_value>", re.DOTALL
)
```

A non-greedy `.*?` guarantees only the *shortest match consistent with the
rest of the pattern*, not that it stops at the first literal `</arg_key>`.
If `\s*<arg_value>` fails to match right after that first occurrence, the
engine backtracks and lets `.*?` cross the boundary to reach a *later*
`</arg_key>`, silently absorbing a stray `<arg_key>`/`</arg_key>` tag into
the parsed key.

This is the identical defect class and identical fix shape as the GLM-4.7
leak fixed in #54971 (reviewer Manny7717 flagged this exact call site in
that PR's review, at `vllm/tool_parsers/poolside_v1_tool_parser.py:82`).
The fix bounds the key to runs of non-`<` text, so the capture group can
never cross its own delimiter:

```python
self.func_arg_regex = re.compile(
    r"<arg_key>([^<]*+(?:<(?!/?arg_key>)[^<]*+)*+)(?:</arg_key>\s*)+"
    r"<arg_value>(.*?)</arg_value>",
    re.DOTALL,
)
```

This file uses the third-party `regex` module (`import regex as re`), not
stdlib `re` — `regex` has always supported possessive quantifiers (`*+`)
regardless of interpreter version, so (unlike a stdlib-`re` site) no
non-possessive fallback is needed here. The repo's `requires-python` floor
is `>=3.10,<3.15`; the dev venv used for testing runs 3.13.15, and a
20,000-case randomized differential check (see Test Result) against the
old pattern found no divergence on well-formed input and no leaked `<` in
malformed input.

### Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs against `poolside`/`arg_key`/`tool_parsers` before
starting. The only overlapping PR is #54678
("[Bugfix][Security] Fix catastrophic backtracking in the poolside_v1 and
dots tool-call regexes"), which is **not** a duplicate of this fix: it
targets a different defect class (ReDoS/timing) in the *same file*'s
`func_detail_regex`,

title: [Bugfix] Drop unhonored SupportsPP on Glm5NextForCausalLM
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

`Glm5NextForCausalLM` declares `SupportsPP` but never wires `make_empty_intermediate_tensors`. `SupportsPP in mro` makes `supports_pp()` return True, so `is_pp_supported_model()` returns True and `verify_with_parallel_config` accepts `--pipeline-parallel-size > 1`. The engine then hits an `AttributeError` on the first non-first PP rank at [vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L515](vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L515):

\`\`\`python
self.intermediate_tensors = self.model.make_empty_intermediate_tensors(
    batch_size=self.max_num_tokens,
    dtype=self.model_config.dtype,
    device=self.device,
)
\`\`\`

The class already carries an inline note saying PP is \"gated off\" — the developer's intent is that PP is disabled. This PR makes that intent actually take effect at config-validation time.

## Why remove SupportsPP rather than wire make_empty

`Glm5NextModel.forward()` has a non-last-PP-rank branch (see [common/model.py:733](vllm/models/glm5next/common/model.py#L733)) that emits `IntermediateTensors({\"hidden_states\", \"residual\"})` — but the developer's own comment there says the mHC layer's `post`/`comb` deferred state \"would need to propagate them, but for now they are dropped\". So wiring `make_empty_intermediate_tensors_factory([\"hidden_states\", \"residual\"], hidden_size)` would silence the AttributeError but silently give wrong outputs (a receiving rank's first layer would fall back to standalone pre state). That trade — silent incorrectness vs. loud config-time rejection — is exactly the reason PP was gated off.

- Remove `SupportsPP` from `Glm5NextForCausalLM`'s base class list and drop the now-unused import.
- Update the two inline comments (in `Glm5NextModel.forward` and `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration.__init__`) to point at the new mechanism.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Enable pipeline parallelism for GLM-5.3-Flash (materialize deferred mHC state; load MTP drafter embedding)
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Two independent bugs kept GLM-5.3-Flash from running usefully under pipeline parallelism. Both fixes are hardware-agnostic (pure Python model/loader code, no kernels touched).

### 1. Pipeline parallelism was gated off (`vllm/models/glm5next/common/model.py`)

`Glm5NextModel` shipped without `make_empty_intermediate_tensors`, so `supports_pp()` was `False` for `Glm5NextForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` and `--pipeline-parallel-size > 1` was rejected. The in-tree comments spelled out why: *"PP is gated off for GLM-5.3-Flash (no make_empty_intermediate_tensors)"*.

The obstacle is mHC (manifold-constrained hyper-connections). Each token carries `config.mhc_num_residual_streams` (4) residual streams, and every decoder layer **defers** its `hc_post` mix into the *next* layer's fused post+pre kernel, returning `(x, residual, post, comb)` (`Glm5NextDecoderLayer.forward`). At a stage boundary there is no next layer to fuse with, so the deferred `post`/`comb` had nowhere to go and were simply dropped.

This PR resolves the deferred state at the boundary rather than propagating it:

* `Glm5NextModel.__init__` now installs `make_empty_intermediate_tensors`. For mHC it is the new `_make_empty_mhc_intermediate_tensors`: a single `"hidden_states"` key of shape `(batch, mhc_num_residual_streams, hidden_size)` — the residual streams themselves, token dim leading so the runner's per-batch slicing works. For non-mHC configs it is the standard `make_empty_intermediate_tensors_factory(["hidden_states", "residual"], hidden_size)`.
* `Glm5NextModel.forward` materializes the pending `hc_post` on the **sending** rank, through the last active layer's `hc_post()`, before constructing the `IntermediateTensors`. Only the residual streams cross the boundary. Under sequence parallelism the streams are flattened, all-gathered and reshaped (collectives expect 2-D), mirroring what the last rank already does before its final norm.
* On the **receiving** rank `residual`

`canonical_layout: true` gives certified MLA+DSA configurations a topology-free storage namespace, but secondary transfers still use the full aligned primary-tier row. That row can change size with TP, so compatible canonical payloads fail P2P connection validation or filesystem promotion.

title: [BugFix][KV Connector] Fix Deadlock with KVConnector + MTP under KV Pressure
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Scheduler can deadlock under KV memory pressure with MTP + KV connector --- encountered in production deployment of GLM5.2

### Example

- 2 requests A (needs 4 blocks + 1 for mtp), B (needs 3 blocks + 1 for mtp)
- Total blocks 7

#### Step 1 — A and B arrive and get added to `skipped_waiting` queue

A is admitted (4 blocks), popped from `waiting` -> `skipped_waiting`, `status → WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`
B is admitted (3 blocks), popped from `waiting` -> `skipped_waiting`, `status → WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`

- result: 
```
skipped_waiting = [A, B]
waiting = []

A.status = WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KV
B.status = WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KV
```

#### Step 2 — A's transfer lands. 

Schedule the `skipped_waiting` queue first. Peek `skipped_waiting` → A.

`_is_blocked_waiting_status(WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS)` is True → `_try_promote_blocked_waiting_request(A)` succeeds → `A.status=WAITING` 

Then, schedule A. Need to allocate for the MTP blocks [these are only allocated after async load]. We need 1 block, but there is 0 left. `allocate_slots` returns None and we `break` (end attempting to schedule.

- result:
```
skipped_waiting = [A, B]
waiting = []

A.status = WAITING
B.status = WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KV
```

As we can see, the queues are in the same state as before this step, and will continue to be in this state (trying to schedule A, asking to allocate blocks) forever.

#### Step 3 onward — Same cycle

Peek `skipped_waiting` → still A, now status WAITING. _is_blocked_waiting_status(WAITING) is False, so no promotion branch; straight to allocation; fails; break. Spin forever.

## Root Cause

Async KV load is allocated without lookahead slots (see `limit_lookahead_tokens`), and `_request_remaining_blocks()` -- which backs the `_inflight_prefill_reserved_blocks()` admission gate -- does not count them either.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Keep the AITER allreduce compile range within AITER's runtime cutoff
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55344.

`vllm/config/vllm.py` derives the compile range of the fused allreduce+RMSNorm
pass from `AiterCustomAllreduce.effective_max_size()`, which only looks at
`MAX_SIZE`. AITER's runtime eligibility check is `min(_car_max_size, max_size /
2)`, where `_car_max_size` comes from `AITER_CUSTOM_AR_MAX_SIZE` and defaults to
a fixed 64 MiB that does not grow with the registered pool.

When the two disagree, the pass is compiled for message sizes AITER rejects.
`custom_fused_ar_rms()` then returns `None`, and
`_rocm_aiter_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_impl` asserts on it — the server fails to
start with a bare `AssertionError` instead of falling back to RCCL. An env var
meant to *narrow* custom-AR usage should not prevent startup.

This makes `effective_max_size()` return what AITER will actually accept, so the
pass is never compiled for sizes that get rejected.

## Test Plan

MI355X (gfx950), TP4, GLM-5.3 (`hidden_size=6144`, bf16),
`--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, AITER custom AR and `fuse_allreduce_rms`
enabled. Same image, same model, same flags in both runs — only the env var and
this patch differ:

```
AITER_CUSTOM_AR_MAX_SIZE=1048576 vllm serve <model> -tp 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192
```

## Test Result

Before (unmodified tree):

```
compile_ranges_endpoints: [5461, 8192]
ERROR _aiter_ops.py:956 in _rocm_aiter_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_impl
      assert result is not None
AssertionError
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed.
-> died after 160 s
```

After:

```
compile_ranges_endpoints: [85, 8192]      # 1 MiB / (6144 * 2) = 85 tokens
-> serving after 340 s, zero AssertionErrors
GSM8K 49/50 = 98.0 %
```

The range now matches the cutoff exactly, which is the intended behavior: with a
1 MiB cutoff the fusion is simply out of scope for realistic batch sizes, and
those fall back to RCCL as they should.

No change with the default (`AITER_CUSTOM_AR_MAX_SIZE` unset): `min(MAX_SIZE //
2, 64 MiB)` is `min(64 MiB, 64 MiB)`, i.e. the previous valu

title: [ROCm] Add HiSparse Support on ROCm
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Enables HiSparse (#53781) on AMD ROCm/CDNA3+, tested on gfx950 (MI355X).

HiSparse keeps the bulk of the sparse-MLA KV cache in pinned host memory and
pulls only the indexer-selected rows back just in time, so long-context agentic
sessions stop getting preempted. #53781 landed it CUDA-only.

This PR enables for ROCm.

It also fixes **one bug in shared, platform-neutral code** that affects CUDA
equally — see *Platform-neutral fixes* below. That fix is the reason GLM-5.3
produces coherent output rather than garbage, and it is not ROCm-specific.

## Changes

### 1. HIP kernel port (`csrc/`)

The four fused HiSparse cache ops now build and run on ROCm. The port is
mechanical — vectorized copy widths, `__nv_bfloat16` → `hip_bfloat16`, and
warp-primitive shims added to `csrc/cuda_compat.h`. No algorithmic change; CUDA
codegen is unaffected.

### 2. ROCm backend wiring (`rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`)

The substantive work. Every CUDA HiSparse backend consumes a **dense**
`[tokens, topk]` index tensor plus `valid_counts`; AITER's tuned decode kernel
consumes a **ragged** flat list plus an indptr. Bridging that is the core of
this change:

- `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` accepts an `index_group_builder` and registers with
  it, which is what makes `mla_attention.py:575` pick up `hisparse_cache` and
  drive KV mirroring.
- Decode: `convert_decode_logical_to_physical_topk` → dense physical top-k →
  compacted to ragged → attention runs against `physical_kv_cache` (the hot
  buffer) instead of the paged KV cache.
- Prefill: mirrors the CUDA guard, staging host rows via `stage_prefill_rows`
  when the context is not fully resident. This is not optional — once a context
  has been offloaded, `all_context_pages_resident` is False and
  `index_group.py:232` asserts outright.
- AITER's persistent work-stealing metadata is disabled under HiSparse: its
  buffers are sized in `build()`, but HiSparse rewrites the indptr at forward
  time fro

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse][NIXL] Recompute unaligned host-import tails locally
bodyExcerpt:
# [Bugfix][HiSparse][NIXL] Leave unaligned host-import tails for local prefill

## Problem

NIXL pull advertises the whole prompt as externally computed. The host-only
HiSparse resident manager requires imported prefixes to end on a cache-block
boundary. A 32,019-token prompt with block size 64 therefore raises:

```text
ValueError: A host-only HiSparse import must end on a cache-block boundary.
```

This escapes scheduler admission and kills the decoder engine. It was observed
on unmodified main `a08dffe21534916f218dcc93012dbaa01f942691`, on 1P TP8 + 1D
TP8, two 8xB200 nodes, using `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` with HiSparse on D. The
new regression also fails on this patch's base, main
`9d14fd3095eb169044e2da0a2a98dd1f2c77ce22`.

## Change

- For host-only HiSparse pull imports, advertise only complete pages, aligned
  across resident and transferable cache groups.
- Omit the unimported tail from local destinations and remote source lists.
  The remote cap is applied after logical-to-kernel block expansion, before
  prefix-cache suffix matching. Rounding the count alone would shift reads
  toward the remote tail and copy the wrong blocks.
- Let normal local prefill compute the remaining tokens. No truncation of the
  user's prompt and no changes to CUDA-graph or memory-utilization settings.
- Keep notify-only receives valid when no complete block can be imported.

For 32,019 tokens / block size 64, import tokens `[0, 32000)` and compute
`[32000, 32019)` on D. Normal non-HiSparse imports retain their existing behavior.
This targets the P-to-D pull path, not bidirectional D-to-P or push admission.

## Validation

New/targeted regression selection:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  -k 'hisparse_import or nixl_hisparse' -q
```

- The original NIXL regression selection on base: **18 failed / 4 passed**.
- Final patched targeted selection, including allocation/resume and DC

title: [Core][KV Offload] Service the P2P control plane while the engine waits on the model
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Addresses #55179. Companion to #55962 (@Etelis) and #57139 (@liranschour), which target the same issue; the comparison with both is below.

The P2P secondary tier services its control socket and answers peer lookups only from the per-step scheduler hooks (`on_schedule_end` -> `get_finished_jobs` -> `_poll_once`, then `serve_external_requests`), so on a source rank busy with long prefills every control-plane round trip waits for a step boundary. Measured on GLM-5.2-FP8 (DP8/TP1, 8xH200 prefill pods, 64 GiB CPU tier, NIXL 1.4.1) with trace stamps on both peers: a pull from a source loaded with three 115K-token prefills spends 2.5-2.9 s in lookup delay, of which the `LookupMsg` sits in the server queue until the next step (0.55-0.61 s) and the `FetchMsg` is dispatched at the step after (0.45-0.50 s), against 0.1-0.2 s of data movement. Registration of the peer's NIXL metadata (`add_remote_agent` plus `prep_xfer_dlist` over 19,599 blocks) is 14-40 ms per side and is not the stall.

### Change

Two independent commits:

1. **Register peers off the scheduler thread.** `DataTransport.add_remote_peer_async` (default: inline, completed future). `NixlTransport` runs it on a single-worker executor and opens the agent with `nixl_agent_config(sync_mode=NIXL_THREAD_SYNC_STRICT)` so registration may overlap transfer calls from the scheduler thread (the NIXL 1.4.1 wrapper applies `sync_mode` when it is set). `P2PSession` sends `ConnectAck` once the registration completes, rejects the peer if it fails, and counts a pending registration as pending work. `remove_remote_peer` waits for an in-flight registration of that peer so a late completion cannot leave a registered peer without a session.
2. **Service connector work while waiting on the model.** `KVConnectorBase_V1.poll_pending_work()` (default no-op; `MultiConnector` forwards; `OffloadingConnector` -> `TieringOffloadingManager`, which runs the same sweep `on_schedule_end` runs: collect finished jobs, serve external re

title: [BugFix] GLM-5: load msmodelslim-native checkpoints and drop MTP draft weights
bodyExcerpt:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Two problems loading official (msmodelslim-exported) GLM-5 W8A8 checkpoints into `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`:

1. **dotted submodule paths**: msmodelslim serializes the MHC and KDA gate modules as `attn_hc.fn` / `self_attn.forget_gate.A_log` while the model registers flattened names (`hc_attn_fn`, `self_attn.A_log`). Load now maps the ten dotted forms at load time via a `WeightsMapper`; already-flattened checkpoints are unaffected (the substrings never match).

2. **MTP draft weights**: the checkpoints ship the QuaRot MTP rotation (`rot.weight`) and the draft layer (`layers.<N>.*` for `N >= num_hidden_layers`). Those weights belong to the separate MTP model used with speculative decoding; without it they have no module to land in and the loader fails with `no module or parameter named 'rot'`. Drop them in the wrapper's `load_weights`, mirroring the reference Ascend implementation.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes — official GLM-5 W8A8 checkpoints (e.g. the msmodelslim-exported ones) load and serve instead of failing on the first weight.

### How was this patch tested?

End-to-end on Atlas 910B3 with the official GLM-5.3-Flash W8A8 checkpoint (81 shards, 311 GB): loads cleanly, serves with the kpool backend, GSM8K-level gate 12/12; behavior verified identical to the flattened self-exported checkpoint (greedy outputs byte-identical incl. timing).

title: [Bugfix][Quark] Honor layer_quant_config for identity packed_modules_mapping entries
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Addresses the identity-entry resolution reported in #54641 by @stefanskiasan. (The
`amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` checkpoint that surfaced it needs #56176 instead — see *Scope*.)

An identity entry in `packed_modules_mapping` (a module mapped to itself, e.g.
`"gate_up_proj": ["gate_up_proj"]`) silently disables `layer_quant_config` for that module. The
layer falls back to `global_quant_config`, so a mixed-precision Quark checkpoint that names the
module is built with the wrong scheme and only fails later, at weight load, with a shape mismatch.

Identity entries exist because the checkpoint really stores the fused tensor: GLM-4.1V ships a
pre-fused `gate_up_proj`, which is why `Glm4vForConditionalGeneration` maps it to itself. A Quark
checkpoint of such a model keys `layer_quant_config` by that fused name, and today that entry is
ignored.

**Scope.** This does *not* fix `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`: that config keys the split
`gate_proj` / `up_proj` names (none `gate_up_proj`), and the actual bug there is the identity
mapping `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` inherits from GLM-4.1V although GLM-5.3-Flash stores
gate/up separately — fixed by the mapping override in #56176. Once the mapping expands to real
shards, the branch this PR changes is not reached; the two are complementary. The reporter's
locally produced config named the fused module (the trace in #54641 shows the key present but
`hit=False`), which is exactly the path fixed here.

Both lookup paths in `QuarkConfig` treat `shard_name == layer_name` as "no shard information":

```python
# get_layer_quant_config_from_name
if shard_name != layer_name:
    config = self.get_layer_quant_config_from_name(shard_name)
else:
    config = None              # identity entry -> no config

# _find_matched_config
if shard_name == layer_name:
    config = fallback_config   # identity entry -> global scheme
```

That guard is only there to stop the recursion, since substituting an identity entry is a no-op.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve model text when tool calling is off
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55080

When tool calling is off — `tool_choice="none"` **or** the request has **no tools** — `DelegatingParser` should skip tool extraction and return the original model text as content.

The engine-based branch of `_extract_tool_calls` still ran `extract_tool_calls` and returned `result.content`. For glm45, qwen3_xml, and other engine-based parsers, tool-call-shaped text was consumed and content became `None`. With `--enable-auto-tool-choice`, `tool_choice is None` is also treated as auto, so a no-tools request could still run extraction and swallow markup (ammo-man measurement on v0.29.0, arms B and C).

This change skips the tool parser when `tool_choice == "none"` **or** `not request.tools`, for both non-streaming and streaming dispatch, and keeps the original text. Tool extraction for `auto` / named / required with tools present is unchanged.

This is not a duplicate of #42868, which changes the serving-layer streaming path in `serving.py`. That path is out of scope here.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest \
  tests/parser/test_tool_choice_none_preserves_content.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/test_tool_choice_content_none.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_delegating_replay.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_replay.py::TestToolCallFilteringNonStreaming \
  tests/parser/engine/test_replay.py::TestToolCallFilteringReplay \
  -v
```

## Test Result

- `tests/parser/test_tool_choice_none_preserves_content.py`: **26 passed** (tool_choice=none + no-tools/omitted + no-tools/tool_choice=None for glm45 and qwen3_xml; auto-with-tools still extracts)

title: [Bug]: vLLM 并发缺陷报告：6 项确认缺陷
bodyExcerpt:
## A. 概述

本报告是针对 **vllm-project/vllm**（github.com/vllm-project/vllm）的并发安全审查结果。审查基于 commit `a46f3eb2`（2026-06-23）完成初始分析，并对照撰写日最新 main `b28c3e15`（2026-09-10）逐项重新核验了每一处代码位置与修复状态——期间 `multiproc_executor.py` 有 11 个提交、`shm_broadcast.py` 与 `kv_events.py` 有多个特性提交，但**没有任何一处触及本报告所述的同步缺口**，6 项缺陷在最新 main 上全部仍然存在。

方法说明：按并发热点将仓库拆分为子系统逐一审查，对每一处疑似缺陷进行两轮独立人工复审（真实源码逐行核对锁的获取/释放边界、全仓调用图与线程/进程拓扑、触发交错推演、可达性与后果评估），并额外做了"是否属设计上可容忍"的二次判定。经上述流程：

最终提交 **6 项**（高 1 / 中 4 / 低 1），核心后果涉及：跨进程共享内存消息的静默损坏与挂死、teardown 期对 zmq 套接字的 use-after-close（可致进程崩溃）、后台线程对已销毁单例的 use-after-destroy、以及故障通知丢失导致的静默挂起。

vLLM 的并发模型以"每进程单线程"为主，真实并发风险集中在**进程间边界**（/dev/shm 共享内存环、ZMQ）、**库自建的后台守护线程与主线程的关停协作**、以及**故障期的异步 shutdown 路径**。本报告 6 项缺陷全部落在这三类边界上，均属库内部生命周期/同步管理缺口，非调用方 API 误用。

Found by @Czile-create  , @LittleS321 and glm via formal concurrency analysis

## B. 本次发现问题总览

| 编号 | 严重度 | 子系统（主要路径） | 一句话描述 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bug1 | 中 | v1/executor（multiproc_executor.py） | `shutdown()` 的 `shutting_down` 检查-置位之间无锁，三个并发入口可双跑 teardown |
| Bug2 | 中 | v1/executor（multiproc_executor.py） | `register_failure_callback` 与 worker 监控线程死亡路径 check-then-act 交错，失败回调丢失、引擎收不到死亡通知 |
| Bug3 | 低 | v1/executor（multiproc_executor.py） | `collective_rpc` 在途时监控线程异步 shutdown 置空 MQ 句柄 → `None.enqueue` AttributeError |
| Bug4 | 中 | distributed/device_communicators（shm_broadcast.py） | 跨进程"内存屏障" `memory_fence()` 是进程私有 `threading.Lock`：单写多读无锁协议在多进程+弱内存架构下可读到撕裂/陈旧消息、写者挂死或过早复用 slot |
| Bug5 | 中 | distributed/eplb + parallel_state | `_EPLB` 后台转发 daemon（无停止标志、不被 join）在 `destroy_model_parallel` 销毁单例期间继续读取 → use-after-destroy |
| Bug6 | 高 | distributed（kv_events.py） | `ZmqEventPublisher.shutdown()` 有界 join 超时后不复查线程存活即 close 套接字，publisher 线程仍在 send → 跨线程 use-after-close（pyzmq 非线程安全） |

## C. 详细问题

### Bug1 ｜ 中 ｜ TOCTOU（检查-置位无锁） ｜ MultiprocExecutor.shutdown() 并发入口可双跑 teardown

**位置**：`vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py:502-533`（guard 读取 :504 `getattr(self, "shutting_down", False)`、置位 :510、teardown 主体 :512-533 含 `_ensure_worker_termination` 与两个 MQ 的 shutdown

title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Disable custom allreduce when expandable_segments is enabled
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Refs #42609, ROCm/aiter#4174.

With `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`, custom allreduce's CUDA-graph buffer registration fails at `cudaIpcGetMemHandle` / `hipIpcGetMemHandle` with `invalid argument` — VMM-backed allocations cannot be exported via IPC — which kills every TP worker during engine startup (`csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh` `get_graph_buffer_ipc_meta`).

This broke the AMD CI LoRA TP shards, which set `expandable_segments` to avoid OOM (builds 87038/87059, `test_llama_lora_tp4_fully_sharded_loras` / `test_chatglm3_lora_tp4_fully_sharded_loras`). #55094 repaired those CI jobs config-side by dropping the env var, but the same crash still hits any deployment that combines expandable segments with TP > 1 (#42609).

Change: `CustomAllreduce.__init__` now detects `expandable_segments:True` in `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` / `PYTORCH_HIP_ALLOC_CONF` and disables custom allreduce with a warning, falling back to the other allreduce backends — turning a hard startup crash into a supported (slightly slower) configuration. The guard runs before any IPC buffer allocation, so it costs nothing.

Relationship to #55094: complementary, not duplicate. #55094 fixes the two CI jobs; this PR defuses the underlying landmine for all users. With both, the LoRA TP jobs pass either way.

## Test Plan

New `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py::test_custom_allreduce_disabled_with_expandable_segments` (parametrized over both env vars), using the file's existing monkeypatch style; needs no GPU — the guard fires before any device access.

## Test Result

Verified locally: with the env var set, `CustomAllreduce(...)` returns with `disabled=True` and the warning; without it, the guard is not taken and init proceeds. The AMD LoRA TP jobs exercise the path end-to-end on CI.

## Duplicate-work check

#55094 (merged) is the CI-side fix for the same symptom; #42609 tracks the code-side issue this PR addresses. No other open PR found at the time of writing.

title: [Bug]: `MooncakeStoreScheduler` fatal assert "Missing current block table for store request" when a KV load failure recovery (#19330) reschedules the request
bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

**Component:** `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/scheduler.py` (`_apply_current_save_block_ids`), interplay between #51358 and #19330.

**Environment:** vLLM main (v0.28.1rc1.dev), GLM-4.7/5.x fp8 MLA, TP8/DCP4, `MooncakeStoreConnector` with async KV loads + KV load failure recovery (`recompute`/`reschedule` policy).

### 🐛 Describe the bug



## Symptom

EngineCore dies with:

```
AssertionError: Missing current block table for store request chatcmpl-xxx
  in _apply_current_save_block_ids (mooncake/store/scheduler.py)
```

The assert fires when the Mooncake store has a degraded moment (SSD read failures `BUFFER_OVERFLOW`, transfer `-200`/`-800`), which triggers the KV load failure recovery path. Every such incident is a hard EngineCore crash (all in-flight requests 500).

## Root cause

Two merged upstream features establish an invariant that is violated under load failure:

1. **#51358** ([Bugfix][Mooncake] Save exact Mamba boundary states) added the defensive invariant in `_apply_current_save_block_ids`: every request whose ReqMeta has `can_save=True` must have a current block table present in `scheduler_output.kv_connector_block_state.block_ids`.
2. **#19330** ([V1][P/D] Add Support for KV Load Failure Recovery) lets the scheduler reschedule a request after an async KV load failure (`failed_recving_kv_req_ids`, request moved back to WAITING, blocks freed/cached).

`kv_connector_block_state.block_ids` only snapshots requests **scheduled this step** (new reqs + cached reqs with new blocks + boundary-state offloads). A request recovering from a load failure can end that step outside the snapshot while a `can_save=True` ReqMeta is still produced (e.g. via the pending-load branch when `can_load` was re-enabled by a retried lookup, or the scheduled-producer branch whose blocks were concurrently released). The assert then fires and kills EngineCore.

This is not specific to Mamba/GLM: any Mooncake Store deployme

title: [Bug] First dummy batch on a DP rank compiles MTP/EP Triton kernels at request time (wide-EP + MTP)
bodyExcerpt:
Setup: GLM-5.2-FP8, prefill instance DP=8 x TP1 on one 8xH200 node, `--enable-expert-parallel`, `--all2all-backend deepep_low_latency`, `--moe-backend deep_gemm`, MTP (`--speculative-config {"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}`), default compilation and CUDA-graph settings, `6f91edf9`.

The first `execute_dummy_batch()` a rank ever runs takes ~10 s. Observed with py-spy on the `EngineCore` main thread (`execute_dummy_batch (core.py:929)` waiting on the worker for 10 s) and with the JIT monitor on the worker, which reports Triton compilations during inference right as that wait ends: `_convert_req_index_to_global_index_kernel`, `eagle_prepare_next_token_padded_kernel`, `eagle_step_slot_mapping_metadata_kernel`, `_fwd_kernel_ep_scatter_2`, `_fwd_kernel_ep_gather`, on every rank of the node in the same DP wave. A rank that has already run a dummy batch (as an idle sibling during another rank's request) pays nothing. A real prefill on the rank does not warm this path.

Why it matters: in DP, a rank runs a dummy batch on every loop iteration in which it has an unfinished request that could not be scheduled (`DPEngineCoreProc.run_busy_loop`). With a KV connector that defers a request on an async lookup, the first such iteration on a cold rank blocks the scheduler thread for the whole compilation, and anything serviced between steps (connector polling, remote lookups) waits with it: I measured a 10.4 s lookup delay and a 13.4 s TTFT on the first P2P-tier pull into a fresh rank, against 0.6-0.8 s once warm.

`compile_or_warm_up_model()` runs `_dummy_run()` for the compile and CUDA-graph sizes and `kernel_warmup()`, and the JIT monitor's own message says "consider extending warmup to cover this shape/config". I have not established which of the listed kernels the startup warmup misses for this configuration (uniform-decode dummy run with MTP drafter and EP dispatch); happy to run a check if someone points at the shapes the warmup is expected to cover.

cc @Etelis @oro

## Purpose

Make the kpool indexer's DeepGEMM paged-MQA launch agree with the schedule metadata it was built with. title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Force reasoning mode for GLM-5.3 chat templates in the GLM MoE parser
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #54744.

GLM-5.3 keeps the GLM-4.x prompt and tool-call format but replaces the `enable_thinking` toggle with an always-on `"Reasoning Effort:"` header. The template's generation prompt unconditionally appends `<|assistant|><think>`, so the model output carries no opening `<think>` tag and thinking cannot be turned off. When a client passes `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}` (or `"thinking": false`, honored by GLM-4.5/4.6/4.7 templates), the `Glm47MoeParser` disabled reasoning extraction while the model still thought, leaking the whole scratchpad into `message.content` and reporting an empty reasoning field. It also made `is_reasoning_end()` return `True` immediately, so structured-output constraints applied from token 0 while the model was still reasoning.

The fix detects the GLM-5.3 template signature on the tokenizer (`[gMASK]<sop>` + `Reasoning Effort:` + no `enable_thinking` + GLM tool-call tags, the same predicate SGLang uses) in `Glm47MoeParser.__init__` and discards the thinking-disable kwargs with a one-time warning. The parser then builds the thinking-armed engine config (`initial_state=REASONING`), so streaming, non-streaming, and `is_reasoning_end` paths all behave exactly as they do today for requests without the kwarg. GLM-4.5–4.7 templates declare `enable_thinking` and are untouched (pinned by a negative-control test).

## Why this is not a duplicate

Two open PRs touch the same symptom with materially different approaches:

- #54276 nulls only the `enable_thinking` kwarg when the template lacks it. A client sending `thinking: false` still leaks, and the loose `"enable_thinking" not in template` check is replaced here by the positive GLM-5.3 family signature ported from SGLang.
- #54825 splits leaked think blocks post-hoc in non-streaming extraction and explicitly leaves streaming broken. Fixing the config at construction time (this PR) covers streaming, non-streaming, tool calling, and the structured-out
author: Dovis01

title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Take video placeholder timestamps from the pixel path's frame sampler
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55644.

GLM-5.3-Flash video prompts are expanded by one frame sampler and encoded by another.

- **Pixels**: `Glm5NextVideoProcessor.sample_frames` samples with the checkpoint's policy — `fps_interval = 2.0`, `extract_t = int(duration * target_fps)` — and `_preprocess` pads the frame axis to a multiple of `temporal_patch_size` and divides by it to get `grid_t`.
- **Placeholders**: `Glm4vProcessingInfo._construct_video_placeholder` emits one frame of placeholders per *timestamp*, and the timestamps come from `_get_video_second_idx_glm46v`, a second sampler on GLM-4.6V's constants — `DYNAMIC_FPS_THRES = {30: 3, 300: 1, 2400: 0.5}`, `extract_t = int(duration * target_fps * temporal_patch_size)`, then `[::2]`.

`Glm5NextProcessingInfo` moved the pixel half over to the checkpoint's own processor (`get_hf_processor`, `_get_vision_info`, `_get_image_max_pixels`, `_get_video_max_pixels`) but left the timestamp half on GLM-4.6V's. title: [ROCm] [Bugfix] Enable Load and Inference of GLM-5.3-Flash Quark MXFP4 Checkpoint
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

The Quark checkpoint `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`, global MXFP4 quant with attention projections kept as source block-FP8/BF16). Two independent bugs break weight load. This PR fixes both and the Quark MXFP4 checkpoint now loads and serves with accuracy on par with the source checkpoint (`zai/GLM-5.3-Flash`).

## Bugs

1. Dense-MLP `gate_up_proj` resolves to the wrong quant scheme:
The class inherits `packed_modules_mapping = {"gate_up_proj": ["gate_up_proj"]}` from `Glm4vForConditionalGeneration`. This identity mapping is correct for GLM-4.1V (whose checkpoint stores a pre-fused `gate_up_proj` tensor), but GLM-5.3-Flash stores gate/up as **separate** tensors (both the [Quark ](https://huggingface.co/amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4)and the [base](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) checkpoints). With the identity entry, `QuarkConfig` falls back to `global_quant_config` (MXFP4) instead of the per-layer block-FP8 in `layer_quant_config` and builds the layer as MXFP4 and mismatches the FP8 checkpoint tensor at load.


2. MLA projection scale name mismatch:
The MLA `q_a` / `kv_a` / `q_b` / `o` projections are dequantized on load by `_try_load_fp8_attn_proj`, which only recognized scales named `weight_scale_inv`. Quark checkpoints export `weight_scale`, so the scale fell through and the fused-qkv-a stacked mapping could not find its target.

## Changes (`vllm/model_executor/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py`)

1. Override `packed_modules_mapping` on `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` so the  fused `gate_up_proj` expands to its real shard names `["gate_proj", "up_proj"]` (matching the `Glm4vMoeForConditionalGeneration` sibling / `glm4_moe` / `deepseek_v2`).
2. In `_try_load_fp8_attn_proj`, accept the Quark scale name:
   `is_scale = "weight_scale_inv" in name or name.endswith(".weight_scale")`.

## Related PRs and Issues:

Bug 1 was initially reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Stabilize sparse-MLA DCP for GLM PCP evals
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Make the B200 GLM-5.2 PCP evaluation complete reliably across its TP/PCP/DCP configurations.

Exact main build [#89033](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89033#01a0a3bf-3adb-4bec-82f2-da92bed83c19) first exposed two independent memory-budget failures after merged backend repair #56677. Successive literal-head and actual-branch gates then exposed the workspace, empty-rank, warmup-key, packed-pointer, and backend-combination edges described below.

## Root causes and fixes

### TP2/PCP2 autotuning headroom

FlashInfer CUTLASS autotuning requests 12.22 GiB with only about 7.6 GiB free after the implicit 0.92 budget reserves 33.46 GiB for KV cache. Set `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85` to leave about 12.5 GiB more autotuning headroom.

### TP1/PCP4/DCP4 KV-cache budget

CUDA graph profiling accounts for 6.15 GiB and reports total non-KV memory of 161.16 GiB, leaving a negative 3.23 GiB KV budget at 0.92. The runtime calculates 0.9545 as the utilization needed to preserve the old effective KV budget. Set 0.96, which produces a positive KV-cache budget.

### FlashInfer sparse-MLA DCP workspace

Under DCP, the TRTLLM-gen launcher requests LSE and carves a softmax-stats slab proportional to gathered heads and scheduled tokens. The old fixed workspace was 413,138,944 bytes; an earlier gate requested 470,810,624 bytes during warmup and failed before evaluation.

This PR carries Jason Yao's byte-derived sizing fix from #50791 with its original author commit, then adapts it to current main's split sparse-MLA backends: preallocation occurs only in `FlashInferMLASparseTRTLLMMetadataBuilder` (SM100), so the separate SM120 backend keeps its own behavior. Explicit `VLLM_FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BUFFER_SIZE` overrides remain respected and warn if undersized; non-DCP allocation is unchanged.

The GLM DCP eval now caps `--max-num-batched-tokens` at its existing 4,096-token model length. With 64 heads per TP1 rank and DCP4, that bounds the computed workspace to exactly 2,561,67

title: [MoE] Allow a fused-MoE kernel to be rebuilt around resident weights
bodyExcerpt:
### Purpose

The experts class a MoE layer uses is selected at load time from the activation format. Anything that changes that format afterwards currently requires reloading the model, because there is no way to re-select the kernel around weights that are already on the device.

This adds one: `FusedMoEMethodBase.rebuild_moe_kernel(layer, dry_run=False)`, implemented for the fp8, unquantized and compressed-tensors w8a8-fp8 paths, with the fp8 oracle helpers it needs.

Two deliberate properties:

- **It does not call `convert_to_fp8_moe_kernel_format`.** The standard and batched variants of one backend take the same branch there, so the resident weights already suit either. Re-running it would allocate a second full-size copy of the weights this exists to avoid moving.
- **Backends whose layouts differ are refused, not half-switched.** `assert_same_fp8_weight_layout` permits only pairs that share a layout (`DEEPGEMM`/`BATCHED_DEEPGEMM`, `TRITON`/`BATCHED_TRITON`, `VLLM_CUTLASS`/`BATCHED_VLLM_CUTLASS`). Running the wrong kernel over the right bytes produces plausible garbage rather than an error, so this refuses up front. Backends added later are refused by default rather than assumed compatible.

`dry_run` runs the selection and every compatibility check without assigning, so a caller can reject an impossible change before it has mutated anything.

This is the first of two changes; the second uses it to switch the all2all backend of a live engine. It is also usable on its own by anything that needs to re-select a kernel without a reload, so it does not depend on that second change landing. Context for why we want it: #56133.

Note this sits next to `_init_moe_kernel`, added by Fast Start (#54921) for the weight cache — same need, arrived at independently. `rebuild_moe_kernel` delegates to it rather than duplicating the construction.

### Test Plan

- `pytest tests/kernels/moe/` on a machine with the FP8 MoE paths available.
- End to end: GLM-5.2

Addresses the block-table mismatch in #56380. This PR does **not** fix the separate kpool-tail slot-mapping fault in that issue.

title: [KV Offload] Scope offload group configs to prefix-cacheable KV cache groups
bodyExcerpt:
# [KV Offload] Scope offload group configs to prefix-cacheable KV cache groups

## Purpose

`build_offloading_config` (`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/config.py`) builds an `OffloadingGroupConfig` for **every** `kv_cache_group` and then asserts, for all of them:

```
assert group.tokens_per_block % tokens_per_hash == 0, (
    f"tokens_per_block={group.tokens_per_block} not divisible by "
    f"tokens_per_hash={tokens_per_hash}. "
    f"Hybrid models (e.g. Mamba+Attention) need "
    f"--enable-prefix-caching to align block sizes."
)
```

But `tokens_per_hash` comes from `resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`), which derives the hash granularity from **prefix-cacheable groups only** (`hashing_sizes = [... if group.kv_cache_spec.prefix_cacheable]`). The two sides disagree about which groups are in scope, so any hybrid model with a non-prefix-cacheable scratch group (`CircularBufferSpec.prefix_cacheable == False`) whose block size does not divide the cacheable groups' hash granularity crashes at boot the moment the OffloadingConnector is enabled:

```
AssertionError: tokens_per_block=4 not divisible by tokens_per_hash=16. Hybrid models (e.g. Mamba+Attention) need --enable-prefix-caching to align block sizes.
```

Enabling prefix caching does not help — the message's advice cannot be followed, because the scratch group is excluded from hash-size resolution *by design* and its ring capacity is set by compression/lookahead geometry, not by the cache block size.

Where this bites: sparse-MLA hybrids that keep a `CircularBufferSpec` ring of pre-compression keys. We hit it deploying GLM-5.3-Flash (support proposed in #53906) on DGX Spark: per rank the layout is MLA + 4 GDN mamba groups at block size 3584 and an SWA drafter group at 64 (all prefix-cacheable, gcd → `tokens_per_hash = 64`), plus a kpool-tail scratch group at block size 4 → `4 % 64 != 0` → boot crash with any `--kv-transfer-config` offloading setup. bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

- vLLM nightly `0.28.1rc1.dev681+ge7edf17ce` (2026-09-11, also reproduced on `dev628+g2a02f6efe`, 2026-09-10), image `vllm/vllm-openai` nightly aarch64, torch 2.13 + cu130

GLM-5.3-Flash served with TP=1 per rank — in our case `--data-parallel-size 4` with or without `--enable-expert-parallel`, i.e. the recipe's `single_node_dep` strategy, at the default CUDA-graph capture sizes (max 1024) — dies during engine start-up at the first CUDA-graph capture, on every DP worker:

```

## Root cause

`SparseMLAIndexGroup` overlaps the logical→physical topk conversion with the compute stream via the `logical_topk_ready` event: the indexer records it on the compute stream after computing topk, and `_convert_once` waits on it on the side stream.

In piecewise cudagraph mode the indexer runs **inside a captured graph segment**, while the consumer runs in the following **eager break** (`unified_mla_attention_with_output` is an `@eager_break_during_capture` point, executed by `add_eager()` after the segment's `capture_end()`). An event recorded during stream capture is graph-local; waiting on it eagerly is `cudaErrorInvalidValue`.

title: [Bugfix] Make hc_expand/hc_contract rank-agnostic
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`hc_pre` / `hc_post` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/mhc.py` are rank-agnostic — they read `shape[-2:]` as `(hc_mult, hidden_size)` and treat everything before it as outer dims. The two helpers that feed them hardcode rank 2:

```python
def hc_expand(x, n):    return x.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, n, -1).contiguous()
def hc_contract(x, n):  return x.mean(dim=1)
```

`unsqueeze(1)` only coincides with "second-to-last" for rank-2 input, and `expand` hardcodes three sizes. A model runner that passes bucketed rank-3 `[1, T, hidden]` or rank-4 `[bs, 1, seq, hidden]` activations — the Intel Gaudi backend does — hits:

```
RuntimeError: expand: the requested shape has too few dimensions!
```

`hc_contract` has the matching problem: for rank-3 input, `mean(dim=1)` reduces over the token axis rather than the mHC axis.

Found while bringing up GLM-5.3-Flash on Intel Gaudi 2.

## Test Plan

`test_hc_expand_contract_rank_agnostic` in `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py`, CPU-only. Covers rank 2/3/4, checks that `hc_expand` puts the axis second-to-last, and verifies the round-trip `hc_contract(hc_expand(x)) == x` (exact, since `hc_expand` replicates).

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py -k rank_agnostic
```

## Test Result

With the fix, all three ranks pass:

```
3 passed
```

Against the unpatched code:

```
FAILED test_hc_expand_contract_rank_agnostic[4-shape1]   # rank-3
FAILED test_hc_expand_contract_rank_agnostic[4-shape2]   # rank-4
2 failed, 1 passed
```

**The rank-2 case passes both before and after** — that is the evidence CUDA paths are unaffected by this change.

---

*AI disclosure: this change was developed with assistance from Claude (Claude Code). I reviewed every changed line, reproduced the failure and validated the fix on real hardware, and ran the tests myself.*

title: [Bugfix] Apply the mHC input RMSNorm in forward_native
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`MHCPreOp` and `MHCFusedPostPreOp` accept `norm_weight` / `norm_eps` and their callers expect a normalized `layer_input`. Only two of the three implementations honour that:

| path | applies the norm? |
|---|---|
| `forward_cuda` | yes, inside the fused tilelang kernel |
| `forward_hip` | yes, explicit `_apply_mhc_norm` call |
| `forward_native` | **no** — takes both parameters and ignores them |

`CustomOp.forward_oot` and `forward_cpu` both fall back to `forward_native`, so every out-of-tree backend — and vLLM's own CPU backend — loses the normalization.

The failure is silent: nothing raises, no NaN appears, the numbers are just wrong.

I hit this running GLM-5.3-Flash on Intel Gaudi 2. All 45 mHC layers lost their input norm; generation degraded to unrelated tokens with a near-uniform logit distribution (top-1 probability 0.99%, top-10 nearly equiprobable), while every per-layer NaN/Inf check stayed clean.

The fix mirrors what `forward_hip` already does.

## Test Plan

Two tests added to `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py`, both CPU-only:

- `test_mhc_pre_native_applies_norm`
- `test_mhc_fused_post_pre_native_applies_norm`

Each compares `forward_native`'s `layer_input` against the same call with `norm_weight=None` normalized by hand. They assert the two differ *before* comparing, so the test cannot pass vacuously.

Worth noting: every existing mHC test is gated on `HAS_TILELANG_MHC`, which is why the native path had no coverage.

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py -k native_applies_norm
```

## Test Result

With the fix:

```
4 passed

title: [KV Offload] Offload namespace records a different cache_dtype depending on the executor, so a TP1 MLA engine never shares blocks with mp engines
bodyExcerpt:
The secondary-tier namespace identity is built from `cache_config.cache_dtype` on the scheduler side ([offloading/config.py#L239-L240](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/663d7f679eda78a8d48613dfede8a4b4bcff2b74/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/config.py#L239-L240)). For sparse MLA models the worker rewrites that field in place ([mla_attention.py#L510](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/663d7f679eda78a8d48613dfede8a4b4bcff2b74/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py#L510), `fp8` -> `fp8_ds_mla`). Whether the scheduler sees the rewrite depends on the executor: with `world_size == 1` the default is `uni`, the worker runs in the EngineCore process, and the namespace records `fp8_ds_mla`; with `mp` the rewrite stays in the worker process and the namespace records `fp8`. The trigger is the executor, not TP: two TP1 engines split the same way if only one passes `--distributed-executor-backend mp`, and a TP1 engine that gains that flag on restart moves to a new namespace and can no longer see the blocks it wrote before.

Observed on `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `canonical_layout: true`, fs secondary tier on a shared directory), `nightly-385dce36`:

- TP1 engine, default executor: `config.json` with `dtype: fp8_ds_mla`, namespace `..._7e96a44f05b8`.
- TP2 engine (`mp`): `config.json` with `dtype: fp8`, namespace `..._0f58f9645522`.
- Same model, same block size, same hash seed, same canonical format; zero hits in either direction because the two engines never look in the same directory. The P2P tier hashes the same fields into its session fingerprint (`FileMapper.from_offloading_spec` -> `config_fields`), so by source a TP1 `uni` peer and an `mp` peer would also reject each other with `config fingerprint mismatch`; in this run the P2P handshake failed earlier on the #56772 length check, so that rejection was not observed directly.

title: [CI/Build] Broaden qwen, llama and minimax label rules
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`label-qwen`, `label-llama` and `label-minimax` enumerate directory-and-extension
patterns, so files for those models living anywhere else get no label:

| rule | matched before | of | coverage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label-qwen` | 83 | 248 | 33% |
| `label-llama` | 16 | 58 | 27% |
| `label-minimax` | 44 | 61 | 72% |

The rules predate several source trees (the Rust frontend, `vllm/tokenizers/`,
`vllm/parser/`, `vllm/renderers/`) and their `\.py` suffixes exclude the `.yaml`
eval configs, `.rs` sources, `.jinja` templates and text fixtures. Qwen is the
worst affected in absolute terms — 165 unlabeled files, most of them under
`tests/evals/`.

## Changes

Replace the enumerations with a single case-insensitive path match, the form
`label-kimi` and `label-rust` already use:

```yaml
- files~=(?i)qwen
- files~=(?i)minimax
- files~=(?i)llama(?!(?:index|stack))
```

All three reach 100% coverage, with zero paths matched that do not name the model.

`llama` needs the exclusion because LlamaIndex and LlamaStack are separate
projects rather than Llama the model; it correctly skips all three such paths
(`docs/deployment/integrations/llamastack.md`,
`docs/serving/integrations/llamaindex.md`, and the LlamaIndex RAG example).

## One judgement call to confirm

The broadened `qwen` pattern now also matches the 8 `colqwen3*` paths
(`vllm/model_executor/models/colqwen3.py` and friends). ColQwen is a
Qwen-derived retrieval model, so labeling it `qwen` seems right to me — but if
you would rather it stay unlabeled, say so and I will add
`(?i)(?<!col)qwen`.

`glm`, `gpt-oss` and `cohere` are left alone. `glm` in particular must not be

title: [PCP][DCP] Declare FlashMLASparse MTP support at CP interleave > 1
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Make MTP reachable for PCP+DCP sparse-MLA prefillers behind NIXL P/D.

With `decode_context_parallel_size > 1` and a `NixlConnector`, `VllmConfig.adjust_dcp_kv_cache_interleave_size` raises `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` to the block size (64) for block-level alignment of the DCP → decoder transfer. `cp_utils.validate_cp_support` then asserts `supports_mtp_with_cp_non_trivial_interleave_size` on every attention impl whenever a speculative config is present:

```
AssertionError: MTP with cp_kv_cache_interleave_size > 1 is not supported in FlashMLASparseImpl.
```

The flag is declared `False` in `vllm/v1/attention/backend.py` and set `True` by no backend in the tree, so MTP + DCP>1 + NIXL is unreachable on main for every sparse-MLA model. This declares it on `FlashMLASparseImpl` only.

**Why this should be safe on this impl:** the mixed-fp8 path processes all scheduled query tokens together, and its slot mapping and sparse-index conversion both thread `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` through (`flashmla_sparse.py` passes it into the DCP index conversion at both call sites). Nothing in the impl assumes interleave 1 except the capability declaration itself.

## Status — draft, validation in progress

Measured on H200, GLM-5.3, PCP8+DCP8+EP8 (TP1) prefiller → TP8+EP8 decoder over NIXL, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=3`:

- With the flag, the arm starts and MTP drafting is mechanically healthy: **0.7755 per-token acceptance, 3.33 tokens/step** (ceiling 4), from differencing `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters across a gsm8k run. Throughput 1.82× the same arm with spec decode off.
- That run also scored **0.325 on gsm8k (200, 5-shot, temp 0)** vs 0.935 for a TP8 reference on the same build. That was on a base that had #55802 but **not** #56715 (*"Respect interleave in indexer KV gather mapping"*), whose description matches the failure exactly. It was not the drafting: acceptance was normal and the corruption was in the KV the draft and target both read.

bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Pass decode_metadata.indices to fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits in the kpool sparse attention indexer decode path.

For flattened speculative decode, the indexer metadata builder flattens multiple query tokens from the same request into individual rows and keeps request indices so that those rows can still be associated with their original request. See DeepseekV32IndexerMetadataBuilder in vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py.

On SM100, DeepGEMM supports varlen paged MQA logits. It uses consecutive equal request indices to identify query rows belonging to the same request and process them together.

However, the kpool logits call did not pass decode_metadata.indices to fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits. As a result, the metadata could be generated for the varlen path (is_varlen=true), while the consuming DeepGEMM kernel was instantiated as is_varlen=false with next_n=1.

This mismatch does not affect correctness, but significantly hurts performance because each flattened query row is effectively handled independently instead of using the varlen grouping information.

This issue is specific to SM100. The varlen paged MQA logits path is currently enabled only for SM100; other architectures such as SM90 do not use this DeepGEMM varlen path.

## Test Plan

Run an end-to-end test with the GLM-5.3-Flash model using the following configuration:

Context length: 120K
Batch size: 40
Speculative decoding steps: 5

Use Nsight Systems (nsys) to capture the execution trace and compare the sm100_paged_mqa_logits kernel latency before and after the change.

## Test Result

The change enables the varlen kernel (is_varlen=true) and reduces the kernel latency from 214.304 μs to 51.808 μs, corresponding to a 4.14× speedup.
